IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Expression of Interest for Various Roles - El Niño Response
body:
**Work on a global humanitarian program contributing to saving lives and alleviating suffering.**

Australia Assists is an Australian Government program that deploys skilled humanitarian specialists to support multilateral agencies, governments, civil society and communities to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and conflict. Australia Assists’ Goal is to: Save lives, alleviate suffering, and maintain human dignity during and in the aftermath of conflict, disasters and other humanitarian crises, and strengthen preparedness for the occurrence of such situations. The program’s Objective is: Targeted deployment of humanitarian expertise that meets the priorities and needs of Australia's multilateral, bilateral and civil society partners and advances Australia's international humanitarian priorities.

For more information [please visit our website.](https://www.australiaassists.org/)

**The Opportunity:**

- Location: Indo-Pacific – Remote support may also be required
- Duration: \[TBC – e.g. 1–6 months per deployment\], with availability to deploy at short notice (within 3–4 weeks)
- Contract type: Employment or Consultancy Agreements where applicable, with guaranteed inclusion to the Australia Assists Humanitarian Roster.

*Submitting an EOI and being assessed as suitable may result in inclusion in a pool of potential suppliers; however, **this does not guarantee paid work or engagement**. Future assignments will be offered as opportunities arise.*

**The Role:**

A very strong El Niño is now established in the Pacific and is forecast to persist into early 2027, alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. Together these are expected to drive drought, water shortages, heat stress, food insecurity, fire and disease risk across much of the Indo-Pacific, while increasing the risk of localised flooding and tropical cyclones elsewhere. These hazards will compound existing vulnerabilities, and impacts are likely to persist well after the El Niño event peaks.

Through this EOI, we seek experienced technical specialists in:

- Water, Sanitation and Hygiene
- Drought Response and Management
- Hydrology and Hydrogeology
- Climate Resilience and Climate Services
- Food Security and Nutrition
- Climate Smart Agriculture and Livelihoods

Successful candidates will join our deployment roster. Roster members may be deployed to support partner governments, regional bodies, UN agencies and civil society organisations to:

- Rapidly scale anticipatory action and preparedness as well as possible response and early recovery
- Protect water, food and livelihood security for affected communities
- Embed climate risk information and resilience into response and recovery, so short-term action reduces longer-term vulnerability
- Strengthen local and national capacity through mentoring, co-design and knowledge transfer

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Provide technical advice and surge support to host partners in the deployees area of expertise
- Undertake rapid assessments and analysis to inform anticipatory action, response and early recovery planning
- Support coordination with national systems and cluster/sector mechanisms, and across sectors
- Strengthen local and national capacity through mentoring, training and co-delivery
- Ensure cross-cutting priorities (GEDSI, Climate Resilience, Localisation, First Nations) are integrated in all work
- Produce timely technical products, reports and recommendations
- Other tasks as specified in the tailored TOR

**Selection Criteria**

**All applicants must demonstrate:**

- Minimum 8 years' relevant technical experience, including preferably at least 2 years in disaster risk reduction, humanitarian, resilience or development contexts in low- and middle-income countries.
- Demonstrated experience applying technical expertise in drought, water scarcity, climate-related emergencies, disaster response, recovery, resilience programming or other relevant technical fields.
- Proven ability to work with and through national governments, local authorities, communities and local partners, with a strong commitment to localisation.
- Demonstrated experience in assessment, planning, implementation, monitoring and coordination of humanitarian, disaster response, recovery or resilience initiatives.
- Experience using evidence, data, monitoring systems, forecasting, risk analysis or technical assessments to support preparedness, decision-making and response activities.
- Experience working in remote, resource-constrained and culturally diverse settings, including in the Pacific and/or Southeast Asia.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, including the ability to translate technical information into practical guidance for decision-makers, communities and non-technical audiences.
- Relevant tertiary qualifications and technical expertise related to the nominated area of specialisation.
- Desirable: previous El Niño, drought or climate-related emergency response experience; experience working with National Disaster Management Offices (NDMOs), government technical agencies, UN agencies, coordination mechanisms or cluster systems.

**Applicants are only required to address the selection criteria relevant to their nominated technical area(s).**

There may be a need for other technical specialists beyond those identified here. If you have experience you believe may be relevant, please submit your profile. **Pacific and Southeast Asian nationals are strongly encouraged to apply.**

For a complete position description please click [here](https://intdev.tetratech.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/AA-PD-Various-Roles-El-Nino-Response.pdf).

title: Global Surge Team Roster: Emergency Deputy Director of People & Culture
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 30 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

The IRC’s Global Surge Team (GST) is a Roster of highly qualified humanitarian professionals who deploy on short notice to emergency and non‑emergency contexts to support the IRC’s mission. GST members provide specialized, time‑bound support where capacity gaps exist, typically for deployments of up to three months.

**The GST Roster is a flexible, OCCASIONAL employment opportunity. Deployment needs vary based on demand. Staff can take on additional deployments as opportunities arise and if they are interested.**

Deployment opportunities depend on organizational and operational requirements and may vary over time; as such, deployments cannot be guaranteed. Staff supporting emergency responses must be prepared to deploy within 72 hours as needs arise.

Members of the GST Roster who specialize in emergencies are deployed to support either existing country programs in their emergency response, or to initiate a new program in the crisis zone. The overall responsibility of the team is to design, develop, and manage the IRC’s on-site humanitarian response, allowing us to meet the immediate needs of the affected population rapidly and effectively.

**Job overview:**

The Emergency Deputy Director of People and Culture, Global Surge (Emergency DD P&C) leads all People and Culture (P&C) work in the assigned response during an emergency. The Emergency DD P&C is responsible for the overall leadership and supervisory management of the response’s P&C team, systems, and services, including workforce planning, policy compliance, staff care and well-being, safeguarding and GEDI commitments, performance management, and handover to sustainable country P&C operations.

In this role, you will be directly responsible for rapidly establishing and scaling P&C structures and a safe, inclusive workplace culture; serving as strategic advisor to the Emergency Country Director and the Senior Management Team; providing oversight for Country Program’s staff; leading emergency recruitment, onboarding, and employee relations in line with IRC policies and local labor law; ensuring accurate and timely payroll, people data, and reporting; and partnering with the Emergency Unit, regional, and global P&C teams to adapt policies and tools to the emergency context.

***The Emergency DD P&C is expected to be deployed in the field, either in an emergency or roving capacity, and must be able to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification, and for up to 12 weeks.***

**Major responsibilities**

**Emergency set-up and scale-up**

- Rapidly establish P&C structures, processes and tools for the response, including employment registration, labor law compliance, contract templates, national staff terms and payroll set-up.
- Conduct a quick review of the local labor and salary market, and recommend a competitive, compliant compensation approach for the response.
- Lead emergency recruitment and onboarding at volume. Coordinate with the Emergency Unit, regional and global P&C teams to deploy surge and roster staff and fill priority national and international positions quickly.
- Co-lead workforce planning and organizational design with the SMT, including rapid scale-ups and adjustments, in line with legal requirements and IRC policies.
- Set up a simple headcount, vacancy and recruitment tracker, and report to leadership on a regular, short cycle.

**Strategic leadership and management**

- Serve as strategic advisor to the Emergency Country Director and the SMT on workforce strategy, compliance and organizational culture, aligned with response priorities.
- Lead, supervise and support the P&C team, including deployed and national P&C colleagues. Remain accountable for the quality and timeliness of P&C services.
- Coach managers on supervision, performance expectations and difficult conversations in high-pressure conditions.
- Advise supervisors on disciplinary matters, act as an impartial mediator, and ensure fairness and compliance with labor regulations.
- Escalate code of conduct issues, and lead or co-lead investigations with the Employee Relations unit and, when needed, the Ethics and Compliance unit.

**P&C operations**

- Ensure context-specific practices in recruitment, compensation and benefits, employee relations, onboarding and offboarding, contract and leave management, and HR information systems.
- Implement IRC People and Culture policies across the response and adapt them to the emergency context, with Regional and Global Surge Team P&C support.
- Ensure accurate and timely payroll and compensation for all staff.
- Contribute expert input on staffing structures and position scoping to proposal design and grant review.
- Where partners are part of the response, provide technical P&C guidance in line with the PEERS framework.

**GEDI and safeguarding**

- Ensure inclusive, fair recruitment and onboarding, and promote a workplace free of discrimination, harassment, bullying and abuse of power.
- Integrate safeguarding into rapid hiring and onboarding, including delivery of the Safeguarding Minimum Standards.
- Ensure all staff receive orientation on the Safeguarding Policy and the IRC Way, with reporting channels visible in all offices in relevant local languages.
- Partner with global investigations teams and response leadership to implement recommendations from safeguarding investigations, particularly disciplinary actions, within two weeks.

**Duty of care and staff well-being**

- With the Duty of Care team, provide guidance on staff duty of care.
- Partner with Safety and Security to ensure best-practice aftercare following critical incidents.
- Develop plans to support the physical and psychological well-being of staff in high-stress, high-risk contexts, including R&R and rotation arrangements.
- Set up engagement and communication approaches suited to fast-changing, remote and insecure environments, including listening sessions.

**Transition and handover**

- Plan and deliver the transition from emergency to sustainable country P&C operations, including a documented handover to incoming long-term P&C staff.
- Coach national P&C colleagues so they can take over core processes.
- Contribute lessons learned to refine IRC emergency P&C policies, SOPs and toolkits.

**Other**

- Support the Emergency Country Director with ad hoc tasks as needed.
- Stay alert to irregularities in operational and administrative procedures and uphold organizational standards.

**Job Requirements:**

You should have strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and be able to communicate effectively, both internally and externally. You should enjoy building trusted relationships with leadership teams, colleagues and partners, and adapting P&C practice to fast-moving contexts.

- Graduate degree in HR management or a related field preferred.
- At least 10 years of progressive P&C experience, including leadership of a P&C function supporting small, medium and large scale Country Programs across multiple locations in an emergency Context.
- Experience working in conflict, post-conflict or disaster response settings, including rapid start-up or scale-up of P&C operations.
- Prior experience working within organizational structures in transition.

**Demonstrated technical skills:**

- Broad knowledge of P&C competencies: recruitment, compensation and benefits, employee relations, contract management, payroll, performance management and HR information systems.
- Working knowledge of international labor law and the ability to establish compliant employment practices quickly in a new country context.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding and deployment of surge and national staff at volume.
- Experience in handling employee relations, safeguarding and code of conduct cases, including coordination with investigations teams.
- Knowledge of duty of care and staff well-being practices in high-risk, high-stress contexts, and the ability to work with security teams on staff safety.
- Ability to use people data and analysis to inform decisions, producing simple, timely reporting.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel, Word and Outlook. Working knowledge of Workday or other HR information systems, and of file-sharing platforms such as SharePoint, is an advantage.

**Demonstrated managerial and leadership competencies:**

- Demonstrated experience advising senior leaders, such as Country Directors and SMTs, and building strong, trusted relationships.
- Demonstrated successful leadership of multi-disciplinary teams in cross-cultural settings, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Ability to build the capacity of national P&C colleagues and hand over systems and responsibilities effectively.
- Ability to supervise in matrixed, remote and fast-changing environments.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner, and to model and promote staff well-being.
- High levels of integrity, empathy and sound judgment on sensitive matters.
- Opportunity-awareness: a successful, innovative approach to unpredictable operational, staffing and funding contexts.
- Ability to represent the P&C context, constraints and successes clearly to senior internal and external audiences, including regulators and government authorities.

**Language and travel**

- English is required. French, Arabic, Spanish are highly desired.
- Ability to deploy within 72 hours of notification.

 **Working Environment**

IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

 **Gender Equality**: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

 **Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international humanitarian organization supporting refugees, internally displaced people and communities affected by displacement. DRC has a long-standing presence in Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, delivering programmes that respond to humanitarian needs while supporting protection, resilience and longer-term solutions for displacement-affected populations.

DRC is moving towards a shared management arrangement across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, bringing the three country operations under a more integrated leadership and management structure while maintaining the appropriate operational and legal arrangements in each country.

 **About the job**

The purpose of the Head of Support Services (HOSS) role is to provide coherent and effective leadership of support functions across the three operations and to enable the new structure to operate efficiently.

The HOSS will lead the development and implementation of harmonized, efficient and fit-for-purpose support services across Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Middle East, Asia and Europe (MEAE) HQ Hub and neighboring country offices where necessary ensuring that systems and resources effectively support programme delivery and organizational priorities. Working closely with the Country Director and senior management, the role will help drive the transition towards shared ways of working, identify opportunities for efficiencies and greater consistency, and ensure strong standards of compliance, risk management and operational support across the three countries and MEAE HQ Hub.

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage Support Services Department Heads across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, including workforce planning, performance, well-being and professional development, while providing technical guidance to the wider support teams.
- Strengthen team capacity through coaching, mentoring, targeted training and regular engagement with country and field offices.
- Promote effective collaboration across the three countries and model DRC’s values, Code of Conduct, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

**Support Services Management**

- Provide strategic leadership and, where required, hands-on support across Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Administration and IT, ensuring responsive, effective and sustainable support to programmes and operations across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq as well as in the MEAE Hub, to best support implementation of strategy
- Strengthen and align support-services systems, processes and controls across the three countries, promoting efficiency and shared approaches where appropriate while responding to different legal, operational and contextual requirements.
- Advise senior management on support-services priorities, compliance, registration, audits, resource management and other operational matters requiring senior-level attention.
- Lead coordinated workforce and resource planning across Finance, Supply Chain, HR, Administration and ICT, ensuring effective financial management and support arrangements across the three countries in line with operational resource plans.
- Ensure effective hosting and operational support to the MEAE HQ Hub, including the support-services arrangements required for Hub staff and functions based in or operating through the three countries.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in the development of the country strategies, annual delivery agreement, and contribute to the strategic leadership of the country programmes.

**Operational Management**

- Lead short- and long-term operational resource planning, ensuring Support Services enable delivery of country strategies, programmes and projects and maintain sufficient capacity to respond to changing operational needs and emergencies.
- Under supervision of the Country Director, oversee implementation of DRC’s Risk Management Framework across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq, ensuring robust compliance and internal controls, with country-level mitigation measures managed through the responsibilities set out under Risk Management.
- Ensure relevant policies, standard operating procedures and administrative systems comply with national legislation, donor requirements and DRC organisational standards. In collaboration with the Country Director, lead on managing legal issues and relationships with legal counsel.
- Regularly review and improve Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment is strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Oversee internal and external audits and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions and recommendations, escalating systemic or significant issues to the HQ/ MEAE HQHub as appropriate.
- Contribute to project development, budgeting and resource-allocation decisions and work closely with programme colleagues to ensure Support Services effectively enable programme delivery, localisation and partnerships.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems.Ensure that the country master budget is updated on a regular basis and is used to adequately prepare project proposals to manage resources efficiently.
- Contribute to organisational development initiatives and deputise for the Country Director when formally requested.

**Risk Management**

- Support the Country Director and Senior Management Team in external engagement with donors and authorities on compliance, registration and audit matters.
- As part of the internal and external audit oversight described under Operational Management, supervise audits and controls relating to DRC’s operational standards within Support Services and follow up implementation of corrective actions.
- Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Develop a country risk management plan identifying major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy, linked to the risk register and action plans maintained with Senior Management.
- Participate in audit kick-off and exit meetings and ensure cooperation at all time during every audit field works. Lead on providing management response on each audit report
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure relevant teams across Lebanon, Jordan and Iraq use DRC Dynamics effectively and consistently.
- Use system reporting and data to strengthen management oversight, decision-making and operational performance.
- Act as a lead user for relevant Projects and Finance functions and coordinate technical follow-up with the HQ/MEAE HQ Hub where required.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

**Required**

- Minimum 7 years’ relevant experience, including substantial senior-level experience managing Support Services within an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience managing multi-functional Support Services within an INGO with an institutional donor portfolio, including responsibility for donor compliance, financial and operational controls.
- Minimum 4 years’ people-management experience, with proven ability to lead, develop and support diverse teams.
- Strong operational management experience, including in complex and emergency settings, with the ability to provide strategic leadership and hands-on support where required.
- Proactive, solutions-focused and change-oriented leadership style, with the ability and willingness to take the lead, make necessary changes and drive improvements.
- Strong communication, negotiation, planning and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively with country teams, partners, authorities, donors and other stakeholders.

**Desirable**

- Extensive professional experience and strong technical expertise in Finance and/or Supply Chain.
- Knowledge of and ability to manage Microsoft Dynamics 365 ERP is a distinct advantage, particularly across Finance, Supply Chain and related operational functions.

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English required while other proficiency in Arabic is an advantage

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

- A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, or Logistics Management

**We offer**

- Contract length: 12 months contract (Renewable based on funds)
- Band: Management - E1
- Duty Station: Amman – Jordan
- Designation of Duty Station: Unaccompanied – Family Duty Station
- Start date: January 01, 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national and expatriate employees.

title: FO Finance Assistant - HQ
body:
Job Title: **FO FINANCE ASSISTANT**

Job location: **HQ – Remote (Dedicated to Gaza Office)**

Reports to: **Global Finance and Compliance Manager**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Finance Assistant will support MedGlobal Gaza Finance operations by processing financial transactions, entering accounting data, preparing payment documentation, and maintaining accurate financial records. The position will work under the supervision of HQ Finance to strengthen financial controls, improve processing efficiency, and ensure timely financial reporting for Gaza operations.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

• Enter financial transactions accurately and timely into the accounting system.

• Prepare and process daily payment vouchers in accordance with MedGlobal policies and procedures.

• Review finance documents for completeness before processing.

• Follow up with the Gaza Finance team on missing or incomplete supporting documentation.

• Maintain organized electronic and physical finance records.

• Assist with account reconciliations and routine financial data verification.

• Support month-end closing activities as assigned.

• Assist in preparing financial reports and schedules.

• Ensure compliance with MedGlobal financial policies, donor requirements, and internal controls.

• Coordinate daily with HQ Finance and Gaza Finance teams to ensure timely processing of transactions.

• Support audit preparation by organizing and retrieving financial documentation.

• Perform other finance-related duties assigned by the HQ Finance team.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.

• 0–2 years of relevant accounting or finance experience.

• Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply.

• Good knowledge of accounting principles.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.

• Experience with ERP or accounting systems is an advantage (Odoo experience is a plus).

• Good numerical and analytical skills.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

• Good command of English (written and spoken).

• Arabic fluency is required.

• Strong organizational and time management skills.

• Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.

• High level of integrity and confidentiality.

• Good communication and teamwork skills.

• Willingness to learn and adapt quickly.

• Ability to follow procedures and maintain accuracy in repetitive tasks.

**ABOUT MEDGLOBAL**

MedGlobal is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals from diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

MedGlobal Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to MedGlobal employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

• Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

• Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving services within and outside MedGlobal.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to MedGlobal, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. MedGlobal is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

MedGlobal provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. MedGlobal employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

title: Maestral PF4C Expert Cohort - Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC)
body:
Maestral is inviting applications from experts in the Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) region for the **Maestral Public Finance for Children (PF4C) Expert Cohort**—a small group of experienced Public Finance for Children professionals who will be among the first trained to use Maestral developed public finance and investment case tools. We are looking for experts who combine strong technical knowledge with the ability to communicate complex public finance concepts clearly and engage effectively with governments and partners.

Selected participants will receive direct training from Maestral President Philip Goldman and Senior Associates, preparing them to become **PF4C Experts** who can introduce the tools and support their application with governments, development agencies, and other partners.

This regional call aims to strengthen the cohort’s capacity to work with governments and partners across the LAC region in Spanish.

**What Maestral provides:**

- Direct training on Maestral public finance and investment case tools
- Recognition as a **Maestral PF4C Expert**, part of a small group trained to introduce and apply the tools
- The potential for paid technical assistance assignments through Maestral when governments or partners seek deeper support to adapt, learn, or apply the tools

**What we ask of PF4C Experts:**

- Participate fully in Maestral training on tools
- Support the introduction of the tools through short webinars and presentations
- Be available for potential short-term technical assistance assignments through Maestral to help governments and organizations adapt and apply the tools

*Participation in the Maestral PF4C Expert Cohort does not guarantee future assignments. It provides specialized training in Maestral’s tools and positions PF4C Experts for consideration as opportunities arise to introduce and apply them in different country contexts.*

**Maestral’s Public Finance for Children Work**

Maestral works with governments and partners to strengthen the financing of systems and services for children. Our Public Finance for Children expertise spans macroeconomic modelling, national and subnational costing, service costing, investment cases and economic evaluation, public financial management, and coordinated financial planning.

Our work combines rigorous analysis with practical tools that help governments understand what quality systems and services cost, identify financing needs and priorities, and make evidence-based decisions about investing in children.

[**Learn more about Maestral’s Public Finance for Children tools and offerings.**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11Hv9gGiW59YfZW-VpLWLbnBwM7XispuR/view)

**Qualifications**

We are seeking experienced professionals with:

- An advanced degree in economics, public finance, public policy, development economics, or a closely related field. Equivalent depth of professional experience will also be considered.
- At least five years of professional experience in public finance, costing, or applied economic analysis.
- Knowledge of Public Finance for Children approaches, investment case methodologies, costing, and/or economic evaluation.
- Advanced spreadsheet modelling skills, including the ability to develop transparent, auditable models with clearly documented assumptions and data sources.
- Experience working with national public finance data and relevant international economic, demographic, and social sector data sources.
- Strong analytical discipline, including the ability to distinguish evidence from assumptions, clearly communicate limitations, and defend analysis under external review.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to make complex public finance concepts and findings accessible to non-technical audiences and engage effectively with government and development partners.
- Professional working proficiency in **Spanish and English** is required. Proficiency in **French** is an advantage.
- Professional experience in the LAC region.
- Experience working in child protection, social welfare, social protection, the social service workforce, health, or education.
- Experience working directly with ministries of finance or planning, co-developing tools with government teams, delivering capacity strengthening, or reviewing economic and costing models

*Participation in the Maestral PF4C Expert Cohort does not guarantee future assignments. It provides specialized training in Maestral’s tools and positions PF4C Experts for consideration as opportunities arise to introduce and apply them in different country contexts.*

**Maestral’s Public Finance for Children Work**

Maestral works with governments and partners to strengthen the financing of systems and services for children. Our Public Finance for Children expertise spans macroeconomic modelling, national and subnational costing, service costing, investment cases and economic evaluation, public financial management, and coordinated financial planning.

Our work combines rigorous analysis with practical tools that help governments understand what quality systems and services cost, identify financing needs and priorities, and make evidence-based decisions about investing in children.

[**Learn more about Maestral’s Public Finance for Children tools and offerings.**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11Hv9gGiW59YfZW-VpLWLbnBwM7XispuR/view)

**Qualifications**

We are seeking experienced professionals with:

- An advanced degree in economics, public finance, public policy, development economics, or a closely related field. Equivalent depth of professional experience will also be considered.
- At least five years of professional experience in public finance, costing, or applied economic analysis.
- Knowledge of Public Finance for Children approaches, investment case methodologies, costing, and/or economic evaluation.
- Advanced spreadsheet modelling skills, including the ability to develop transparent, auditable models with clearly documented assumptions and data sources.
- Experience working with national public finance data and relevant international economic, demographic, and social sector data sources.
- Strong analytical discipline, including the ability to distinguish evidence from assumptions, clearly communicate limitations, and defend analysis under external review.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to make complex public finance concepts and findings accessible to non-technical audiences and engage effectively with government and development partners.
- Professional working proficiency in **Arabic and English** is required. Proficiency in **French** is an advantage.
- Professional experience in the MENA region.
- Experience working in child protection, social welfare, social protection, the social service workforce, health, or education.
- Experience working directly with ministries of finance or planning, co-developing tools with government teams, delivering capacity strengthening, or reviewing economic and costing models

title: Assistant.e Qualité et Administratif - Projet Antibiogo F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Sous la supervision de l’équipe de Coordination du projet et en collaboration étroite avec l’équipe QARA, elle/il est chargé du suivi administratif des ressources du projet (RH, comptable, budgétaire), de la partie approvisionnement du projet et participera activement à la mise en œuvre de la procédure de gestion documentaire selon la norme ISO 13485 auprès de l’ensemble des équipes (Clinique, Développement/Produit, QARA et Coordination).

**Principales responsabilités :**

**1. Suivi Administratif des Ressources du projet**

**a. Gestion des Ressources humaines**

- Collecter et enregistrer les données des collaborateurs pour la constitution et le suivi des dossiers RH.
- Collaborer avec le département RH de MSF Asso pour la rédaction et la saisie des contrats conformément au droit du travail français et du Système d’Information RH de MSF.
- Organiser l’arrivée des nouveaux collaborateurs : matériel, badges, briefings, intégration administrative et opérationnelle.
- Maintenir à jour les tableaux de suivi des contrats du personnel (employés et consultants).
- Planifier les entretiens annuels.
- Diffuser le planning des déplacements/ absences/ occupation des bureaux et animer son utilisation par les équipes
- Mettre en forme et diffuser les annonces de recrutement selon la stratégie définie
- En conformité avec la procédure RH du QMS, maintenir à jour la documentation et le reporting RH (organigramme, tableau de bord des formations, descriptifs de postes, et autres enregistrements RH) nécessaire au suivi des indicateurs de performance.

**b. Gestion comptable et budgétaire du projet**

- Participer à la construction du budget et au suivi de son exécution avec le responsable du projet.
- Contribuer à la préparation des reportings financiers et narratifs à destination des bailleurs.
- Assurer le suivi des dépenses et de la refacturation en lien avec la comptabilité et le contrôle de gestion de MSF Asso et de la Fondation MSF
- Vérifier et transmettre les notes de frais des employés à la comptabilité.

**2. Approvisionnement**

- Coordonner les commandes et livraisons en fonction des besoins du projet.
- Réaliser les demandes d’achat dans le Système d’Information Finance/Achat de MSF et suivre les réceptions des prestations conformément à la Procédure Achat/Fournisseurs
- En conformité avec la procédure Achat/Fournisseur du QMS, maintenir à jour la documentation et le reporting Supply (tableau de suivi des fournisseurs, audits et évaluations des fournisseurs, et autres enregistrements supply) nécessaire au suivi des indicateurs de performance.
- Participer à la sélection des fournisseurs.

**3. Gestion documentaire du projet (ISO 13485)**

- Participer au pilotage opérationnel (organisation et mise en œuvre) de la procédure de gestion documentaire, en garantissant le maintien, la mise à jour, l’accessibilité et l’archivage de la documentation du projet (procédures, ‘template’, enregistrements) conformément aux exigences de la norme et de la procédure.
- Assurer un soutien méthodologique aux équipes pour le formatage des documents.
- Veiller à la bonne mise en forme et à la standardisation des documents.
- Suivre la réalisation des actions, la résolution des problèmes liés à la procédure de gestion documentaire.
- Participer au prochain déploiement d’un outil de GED (gestion électronique des documents) : organisation de la migration des documents, formation des utilisateurs et support à la prise en main.

**4. Appui à la coordination de projet**

- Assurer le suivi et l’animation des dossiers ou projets spécifiques qui lui sont confiés (support à la gestion de l’information et aux activités de plaidoyer).
- Apporter son soutien à l'organisation des réunions et veiller au suivi des plans d'action correspondants
- Rédiger les comptes rendus des comités de pilotage, réunions d’équipe.
- Soutenir le bon fonctionnement des activités transverses du projet selon les besoins.

**Profil recherché :**

**Formation**

- Formation Bac+2 minimum en gestion, administration ou qualité essentielle

**Expérience professionnelle**

- Expérience dans un poste administratif MSF (terrain ou siège) obligatoire
- Expérience exigée en suivi administratif et financier de projets au sein d'une ONG internationale ou financés par des bailleurs institutionnels, avec une pratique du reporting financier et narratif appréciée.
- Expérience dans une entreprise/un projet avec un système de management de la qualité selon norme ISO 13485 requise, incluant idéalement la pratique préalable d'outils de GED (Gestion Electronique Documentaire)
- Expérience dans des projets de plaidoyers dans le domaine de la santé publique est un plus

**Langues :** Anglais courant (C1 minimum) et Français courant (C1 minimum) obligatoire

**Compétences**

- Maîtrise du Pack Office
- Bonne compréhension des exigences de reporting de bailleurs institutionnels et des activités de plaidoyer
- Connaissance de la norme ISO 13485 ou d’un système qualité équivalent souhaitable.
- Aisance avec les outils informatiques : Système d’information, ERP, logiciels qualité.

**Aptitudes :**

- Rigueur, organisation et vigilance
- Esprit d’analyse
- Capacité d’adaptation, flexibilité
- Sens de l’observation
- Bon relationnel et appétence pour le travail en équipe
- Autonomie

**Conditions d'emploi :**

**Statut :** CDI à temps plein. Poste assimilé cadre, basé à Paris avec déplacements sur les terrains MSF à prévoir.

**Rémunération et avantages :** 41,1 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois. 22 jours de RTT par an. Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.). Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%. Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir :** 16/11/2026

title: ENUMERADOR
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**OBJETIVO DEL TRABAJO**

El/la enumerador/a (encuestador/a) se encargará principalmente de levantar y velar por la calidad de los ejercicios de recolección de datos. Esto dentro del marco de colaboración y desarrollo de un proyecto de investigación entre Queen’sUniversity y ACTED.

El proyecto tiene como objetivo conocer el impacto diferenciado del COVID/19 entre diferentes grupos poblacionales. En particular sobre población de mujeres, comunidad LGBTIQ+ y personas con discapacidad. De igual forma, se estima el levantamiento de datos por medio de aplicación de encuestas a grupos control. Ya establecidos los criterios de selección y tamaño de la muestra. El equipo de enumeradores responderá a él /la gerente de proyecto y asistente de investigación en el marco del presente estudio.

**CADENA DE MANDO**

Bajo la autoridad de:

- Gerente de Proyecto
- Asistente de investigación

**RELACIONES LABORALES**

Relaciones internas:

- Gerente de Proyecto
- Asistentes
- Formadores
- Lideres de terreno

Relaciones exteriores:

- Grupos poblacionales encuestados
- Monitores/evaluadores externos

**OBJETIVOS:**

El equipo de Enumeradores (encuestador/a) se encargará de la recolección de información mediante el levantamiento de encuestas a los grupos poblacionales ya referenciados, así como a las muestras control previstas para el estudio. De igual forma, será responsable del adecuado levantamiento, carga y resguardo de dichas encuestas y de la información contenida.

**FUNCIONES Y RESPONSABILIDADES:**

- Velar por la calidad de los datos levantados en el terreno: Registro de encuestas, seguimiento de los planes diseñados para el levantamiento de la data, seguimiento de criterios vinculados con número y tamaño de la muestra, distribución por cuotas, entre otros.
- Contribuye al logro de las metas establecidas por ACTED sobre el número de encuestas a levantar
- Reporta oportunamente problemas técnicos-operativos que puedan presentarse durante el levantamiento de las encuetas y propone soluciones para gestionarlos, en coordinación con el gerente de proyecto, asistentes y lideres de terreno.
- Vela por el adecuado manejo de los equipos tecnológicos dispuestos por ACTED y Queen’s University para el levantamiento de las encuetas.
- El/la Enumerador/a asegura la adherencia con los principios humanitarios, políticas, herramientas, procesos, manuales, directrices y códigos de ACTED y Queen’s University.
- El Enumerador/a guardará estricta reserva de toda la información a la que tenga acceso y conocimiento a razón del desarrollo de encuestas y que sea de naturaleza privada, confidencial o cuya comunicación pueda causar perjuicio, asegurando el pleno cumplimiento de la política de protección de datos y los procedimientos operativos estándar de ACTED y Queen’s University. A su vez, deberá seguirlos lineamientos técnicos y metodológicos que impartirá el equipo de ACTED durante sus capacitaciones.

  
**RESPONSABILIDADES GENERALES DE ACTED**

ACTED proporcionará los archivos, accesos, información y herramientas necesarias para que las encuestas se desarrollen de manera efectiva y con la calidad esperada. Una vez se inicien las labores, ACTED proporcionará acceso a los dispositivos tecnológicos para la aplicación de las encuestas para diligenciar los formularios para cada encuesta. ACTED será responsable de movilizar a los encuestadores a las comunidades para la aplicación de los instrumentos, así como también logística de hidratación y alimentación.

**CUALIFICACIONES, CUALIDADES HUMANAS. CONOCIMIENTOS Y HABILIDADES TÉCNICAS REQUERIDAS**

**Cualificaciones:**

- Profesional o técnico en Sociología, Trabajo Social, Antropología, Psicología, Ciencias pedagógicas Educación, carreras afines.
- Conocimiento y Respeto por los principios humanitarios
- Experiencia en levantamiento y digitalización de datos.
- Experiencia en procesos de recolección y digitalización de datos.
- Se valorará la experiencia o acercamiento con el uso de herramientas como plataforma Spryng.io, sensemaking approach, Kobo Toolbox, o alguna otra herramienta de recolección de datos en campo.

**Conocimientos**

- Manejo de técnicas de entrevista.
- Manejo de técnicas de recolección de datos masiva.
- Comprensión del principio de confidencialidad antela información compartida por participantes y beneficiarios.

**Competencias:**

- Respeto por los principios humanitarios.
- Disposición e interés en participar en los procesos de capacitación dictados por ACTED.
- Empatía.
- Habilidades de comunicación y liderazgo.
- Adaptabilidad a las condiciones y dinámicas del trabajo en terreno.
- Interés y compromiso por permanecer en el equipo de seguimiento.

“Se anima especialmente a mujeres, así como a personas integrantes de grupos sociales como indígenas, afro- descendientes, personas con discapacidad y personas de la comunidad LGBTIQ+ calificadas a aplicar a la posición”

**CONDICIONES CONTRACTUALES:**

- Contrato a destajo, con una modalidad de pago por día trabajado.
- Honorarios a partir de 30 USD por día efectivamente trabajado.
- Ubicación de las posiciones: Caracas / La Guaira.
- **Trabajo 100% presencial. -**
- **Disponibilidad INMEDIATA. Implica movilización dentro las zonas geográficas previamente descritas.**

title: Senior MEL Advisor, Data Systems and Analytics - UK, NL, France, Belgium
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
## **Location: UK or Europe (Netherlands, France, Belgium, Switzerland)**

## **Status: Full-Time, on going**

## **Starting Salary: UK £60,030; NL and other EU countries €70,920, commensurate with professional experience and internal equity**

**Closing Date:** Submit application by **November 10**

## [**Risk Level**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en)**: Level 1 - Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data**

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Prosper Global to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

### **The Program / Department / Team (Program / Department Summary)**

### **The Technical Support, Evidence, and Program Quality (TEQ) unit sits within Programs. TEQ supports program impact though direct program support, program systems and tools, and influence. Our team, in collaboration with our regional and program counterparts, provides technical leadership for all four Prosper Global impact priorities and the sectors they encompass. We bolster program quality by leading the development of guidance and tools that shape how we implement programs and how we assess program effectiveness.**

### **In 2022, Prosper Global piloted a mechanism to measure our progress towards our strategic intent and are now scaling and regularizing associated processes. Our strategy measurement mechanism includes two important components: 1) measuring the alignment and the progress of our programs towards participant-facing strategic goals and outcomes (“Organizational Outcome Measurement”, or OOM); and 2) tracking internally facing indicators of operational health (“Organization Performance Indicators,” or OPIs).**

### **The Position**

### **The position is focused on OPIs, OOM and MEL program support and is part of the MEL team. They will work under the supervision of the Director of Measurement, Strategy and Program Performance, and, in collaboration with various departments, will develop systems and structures to periodically collect, report, and track our OPIs, as well as curate programmatic data. The Senior Advisor will promote appropriate integration of OPIs in country and regional strategic workplans. Additionally, the position will support OOM by analyzing and summarizing programmatic data in each of Prosper Global’s impact priorities, conducting deep dives to identify areas where operational and programmatic progress may be co-dependent, and developing OOM dashboards. In addition to working closely with TEQ and MEL, the position will also work closely with the office of the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Operations Management, Financial Planning & Analysis, and People Team. The position is expected to promote the MEL Tech suite and support teams to integrate their data for use and decision making. Finally, the role will provide training and capacity building support to program teams in the areas of data management, visualization and VfM, and promote the overall efforts around data standardization and data use in countries and programs.**

### **The MEL position is a critical role that requires the incumbent to master organizational performance metrics, data collection, analysis, and reporting, as well as demonstrate exception skill with visualization platforms.**

### **Essential Responsibilities**

#### **Coordinate and support the alignment of OPIs across various units and departments, regions and country offices. (20%)**

- Oversee and lead the OPI working group in refining OPIs, determining data collection cycles, aligning data protocols, developing clear standard operating procedures, promoting integration across technology platforms, and continuously improving these processes. The working group and community of practice will consist of team members from each department contributing OPI data.
- Act as a key organizational authority on OPIs, providing strategic guidance and serving as the primary representative for engaging with senior agency stakeholders. Lead efforts to disaggregate, refine, and adapt OPIs to maintain their accuracy, relevance, and alignment with organizational decision-making and strategic priorities.
- Work closely with the SRU to integrate the selected OPIs in country and regional strategies, by conducting webinars, and leading key communication events as needed.
- Act as technical advisor to Country and Regional teams as necessary, ensuring appropriate integration of OPIs in their strategic workplans. Oversee standardization of measurement units, alignment of reporting schedules, and synchronization of data sources with global reporting mechanisms to ensure consistency and accountability.
- Produce ad-hoc reports for senior leaders, including the Board of Directors, the Executive Leadership Team and Leadership Team, showcasing OPIs and related metrics to gauge organizational health.
- Strengthen data literacy within the organization on appropriate use of OPIs at various levels.

#### **Collect, analyze and report progress against Organizational Performance Indicators (20%)**

- Lead OPI reporting cycles and set expectations for delivery of new functionalities.
- Actively seek and encourage feedback from stakeholders to inform the prioritization of new product features and enhancements for development.
- Design, implement, and oversee the strategic scaling of a comprehensive framework for the systematic collection, analysis, and reporting of OPIs, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and scalability across all operational levels.
- Oversee the collection of OPIs from various units, ensure data quality and consistency over time and identify areas for improvement. Lead efforts to identify and address systemic gaps, driving continuous improvement and alignment with organizational standards and goals.
- Work with data-contributing teams to refine their data collection and management processes as needed for individual OPIs.
- With the support of IT and the Data Strategy Working Group, lead the development of a data infrastructure to automate data ingestion into Fabric and visualization in PowerBI. Streamline existing organizational reporting and data collection efforts to reflect OPI reporting and facilitate data transfer.
- Analyze OPI data on a regular basis or on demand by various units, producing brief reports as requested. Conduct, facilitate and co-facilitate sensemaking sessions, to contextualize, localize and ground truth the observations and analysis generated from the findings.
- Work closely with the other Strategy Measurement team members to identify areas where OPI progress analysis can be integrated in the overall Strategy Results Measurement and progress tracking, identifying interdependencies between OPIs and program results.

#### **Organizational Outcome Measurement and Mapping Our Reach (30%)**

- Analyze programmatic quantitative data reported through TolaData and supplementary sources.
- Create data analysis products/results that are clear, easy to understand, and relevant, including dashboards for country and regional users.
- Support OOM report writing, including providing clear interpretations of data analysis
- Liaise with the MEL automation team to coordinate data gathering, cleaning, and analysis efforts.
- Support the analysis efforts of the annual Mapping Our Reach participant count, including development of dashboards for tracking, quality assurance and final reporting.

#### **Program and HQ data integration support (30%)**

- Support the HQ MEL Tech team in the rollout of the MEL Tech suite with programs.
- Work with IT, MEL and T4D towards data integration to promote data use and learning.
- Provide technical assistance in areas that use blend of datasets and methods, including value for money (VfM) and internal performance reviews.
- Support the organizational efforts in generating cost-efficiency analysis by conducting VfM analysis based on donor requests and programmatic needs.
- Co-lead the workstream on Generative AI and data integration across MEL, Finance, People Team, among others.
- Ensure data integration across departments and automate data ingestion in OPI dashboard, OOM products and program delivery outputs.
- Provide training and capacity building support to teams in the areas of data management, visualization and VfM.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

None.

### **Accountability**

- **Report directly to**: Director of Measurement
- **Works directly with**: TEQ, Finance, Pople Team, Ethics and Compliance, Fundraising team and other OPI leads focal points, in addition to MEL members at HQ and countries/regions.

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

### **- Education: BA/MA in international development, social science , MEL, data analysis, or related sector (or equivalent hands-on experience) and relevant certifications preferred.**

### **- Experience: at least 7 years of experience in aggregating and reporting data across various programs, or for agency-level indicator measurement, including environmental, social and governance (ESG) measurement. In some agencies they are known as internal progress indicators, KPIs, and others. Experience with similar agency reporting mechanisms, such as Balance ScoreCards, and ESG reporting highly preferred.**

### **- Expertise and Knowledge: Deep knowledge of data management is required, including standardization of data variables, data cleaning, data analysis and reporting. Expertise in producing interactive data visualizations, communicating data findings, ground truthing and producing reports on data findings that is understandable and accessible to a wider audience is going to be a core part of the job and skills and knowledge in this area are mandatory. Therefore, the candidate will be required to demonstrate previous success in other employment opportunities.**

### **- Technology and Data Literacy: Knowledge of how to produce and communicate accessible interactive dashboards, help interpret and communicate findings are mandatory for this role. Candidates with prior experience of supporting or leading development of databases, and with a strong understanding of data engineering, data structures, and building data models will be preferred for this role. Familiarity with mobile data collection platforms , Advanced experience with Power BI, including DAX and M languages is required. Familiarity with data automation, Microsoft Azure and SQL is an added advantage.**

### **- Knowledge of English is required and knowledge of French, Arabic or Spanish is preferred.**

### **Success Factors**

### **- Strategic critical and evaluative thinking skills:**

### **Demonstrated abilities and track record in strategic systems and holistic thinking, managing resistance to change and understanding of organizational culture and behavior, learning and change management.**

### **Strong organizational and process management capabilities. Ability to effectively set priorities and handle competing time and resource demands for self and others. Comfortable working independently and with limited oversight in a fast-paced environment across diverse teams.**

### **- Effective Communication, Leadership and Teamwork:**

### **Ability to prepare compelling presentations, written reports, data visualizations, and effectively present work/findings in international forums. Strong communication and facilitation, mentoring and training skills both in person and virtually.**

### **A strong team player, able to successfully cultivate and maintain relationships not only internally within Prosper Global across various HQ teams as well as regional and field offices, but also externally with and through professional networks.**

### **Demonstrated conversation and presentation skills that can influence decision makers and foster organizational change, as well as the ability to implement and adjust them within a complex organizational setting.**

### **Ability to lead a group of departmental focal points responsible for OPI reporting, including gathering feedback, providing key updates, and ensuring that indicator leads meet deliverables in a timely manner**

### **- Data visualization and analysis skills:**

### **Proven experience cleaning, ingesting, modeling, and visualizing complex data sets from across the agency in a clear, concise manner.**

### **DAX and/or m script coding skills to build custom measures and columns in support of OPI reporting in Power BI.**

### **Ability to consult with and advise data-contributing teams on data collection / measurement best practices.**

### **Strong analysis and writing skills that highlight key changes and findings related to organizational health and performance.**

### **- Development of Resources:**

### **Proven experience in development of toolkits and resources based on scope and sequenced approach**

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in UK or Europe and it requires up to 10% travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

### **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

title: Coordinator for a Medical Project (Volunteer Coordination & Health Education)
body:
**Med’EqualiTeam** is a French non-profit organization, created in July 2018. Our aim is to provide free health care to displaced populations, who wouldn’t otherwise have access to it due to any kind of barriers or lack of physicians. We are a volunteer based NGO, with most of the staff coming for short period of term in order to support with their medical or translation skills.

We are running since December 2023 a [**project in Northern Greece**](https://www.medequali.team/en/projects/medical-help-thessaloniki/), with mobile medical units reaching out to different centers to provide medical consultations. We also run a Health Education program with first aid trainings and sessions about health topics designed for the community.

## *Job description*

This is a combined role of two coordination branches: Volunteer Coordination & Health Education Coordination.

### **1) Volunteer Coordination**

Are you someone with **great people skills**, **experience in the humanitarian sector**, and a (academic/professional) **background relevant to our medical project** in Thessaloniki e.g., medicine, public health, psychology, social work, etc.?

Then you might be our next *Volunteer Coordinator* managing our volunteer team on the ground in Northern Greece! This role focuses on recruiting qualified volunteers, composing a compatible medical team, supervising volunteer wellbeing, and managing the project’s HR tasks. This role is a great opportunity to gain project management experience in the medical humanitarian field and further hone your leadership skills.

*Job description:*

- Advertise new positions with recruitment partners
- Implement existing processes for recruitment and on-boarding of new (medical) volunteers; registration and evaluation of applications, holding interviews, composing the volunteer team, organising travel and accommodation logistics, conducting volunteer inductions on the ground, conducting check-in and exit chats, etc.
- Gather and implement volunteer feedback
- Coordinate the recruitment and onboarding of community translators
- Organise volunteer schedules in collaboration with the Medical Coordinator and Field Coordinator
- Look out for the wellbeing of volunteers and coordinate wellbeing activities
- Ensure professional behaviour and respect of MET code of conduct by all volunteers
- Ensure the safe storage and confidentiality of all HR data and information according to MET’s processes
- Be the on-site coordinator and manage the reception for approximately 1-2 clinics a week: register patients, coordinate clinic translation and medical volunteers, and manage on-site safety

### **2) Health Education Coordination**

Are you interested in improving the health of asylum seeker and refugee communities through education and empowerment? We are seeking a volunteer with an **interest in training** **and education** to coordinate the health education branch of our medical project in Northern Greece; where we provide first aid training sessions for NGO volunteers and health education sessions to displaced communities across Northern Greece. This role is a great opportunity to develop your coordination and education skills and use your medical experience to deliver preventative health measures.

*Job description:*

- Plan and coordinate first aid trainings and health education sessions with NGO partners across Northern Greece.
- Lead in developing and delivering sessions with support of the medical volunteer team; designing training materials (presentations, leaflets etc.), overseeing translations, conducting focus groups, etc.
- Work with the medical coordinator to shape the strategy of health education and training
- Implement service evaluation protocols by gathering and processing feedback from attendees of sessions to improve the service

*As a key position, we ask for a minimum of **9 months** commitment. The **starting date is 10th of January 2027** with 2 weeks of handover with the current coordinator.*

***This is a volunteer position with a stipend - we cannot facilitate entry into Greece or obtain a visa.***

## ***Required experience and skills***

- Fluency in English
- Minimum time commitment of 6 months
- Strong organizational and administration skills
- Strong communication and reporting skills
- Strong interpersonal and intercultural skills
- A high level of personal organization, flexibility and resilience
- Capable of working independently, while knowing your professional limits and asking for help if needed
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and to MET’s mandate
- A driving licence and experience driving a manual car
- Proficiency on computer (Office pack, PowerPoint, Canva)

## Desired experience and skills

- Experience in HR and in working with volunteers
- Healthcare professional (or student in a health field)
- Previous experience working or volunteering with displaced or vulnerable people
- Previous work experience in NGOs/INGOs
- Experience providing education/training sessions
- Knowledge of locally relevant languages (Greek, Arabic, Farsi, Turkish)

## Benefits of working with Med'EqualiTeam

- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- A highly rewarding and meaningful job
- Work in a multilingual environment
- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- Accommodation in Thessaloniki in a shared flat, transport to the mission site and emergency health insurance provided.
- Please note that this is a voluntary position, which comes with a basic stipend to cover living expenses. Unfortunately, we cannot offer a salary.

title: Supply Chain intern
body:
## Join MSF OCG as a Supply Chain intern!

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 12 months at 100%

### Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

### Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

To scale up to meet these operational, human resource and financial challenges, the OCG has set up a Supply Unit, with a view to optimise the management flows (goods, information and financial) and supply processes (internal and external). The final aim is to ensure a sustainable and efficient MSF Supply Chain to meet the OCG strategy.

The Supply Chain intern work in close relation with the Supply chain referent Back Office and the Supply Chain program manager on below tasks.

### Tasks & Responsibilities

- Maintain along with the Supply Referent Back office the existing reporting tools
- Participate in development, test, pilot and deployment of the Supply automated reports (Business intelligence system)
- Support the program manager in the improvement of the data management in line with the OCG supply strategy
- Help with the documentation of different data management Project
- Contribute actively to the improvement of the data quality

### Your profile

*Education*

- In progress or completed degree and specialisation in Supply chain management or Business Analytics (Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, Information management)

*Languages*

- French and English with fluency in at least one of the 2 and C1 level in the other.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Experience in data modelling and reporting as well as strong affinity with IT is a plus (R Studio is a plus)
- Knowledge of BI tool (Power BI preferably)

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Attention to detail and structured and independent working method
- Good analytical and communication skills.
- Strong interpersonal skills, team spirit.
- Flexibility and open-mindedness

### Terms of internship

- A tripartite internship agreement is mandatory.
- 6 to 9 months, according to internship agreement.
- Full time (40h/week).
- Based in Geneva, Switzerland
- Start date : February 2027
- Gross monthly remuneration 2'000.- CHF

title: Associate National Project Officer- TVET (Education)
source: UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
body:
**Position Number**: 5JOED0029PA

**Grade**: NO-A

**Parent Sector**: Education Sector (ED)

**Duty Station**: Amman

**Job Family**: Education

**Contract Type**: Project Appointment

**Duration of contract**: 1 year
