title: Business & Human Rights Data Analyst - MyVox Product Owner
body:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

 In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a Business & Human Rights Data Analyst to join our team. The Data Analyst supports the analysis of data collected through MyVox (including the mobile/web app and the live dashboard). The role is responsible for managing, analysing, and interpreting data collected through the mobile and web application to provide actionable insights that will inform advocacy and awareness-raising efforts.

**The Role**

- Collect, organize, and clean data from the MyVox application, ensuring data integrity and accuracy by identifying and rectifying any data anomalies or errors.
- Perform statistical analysis and interpret the results to identify trends, patterns, and insights.
- Use data visualization tools to present data in a clear and actionable manner.
- Develop quarterly comprehensive reports and presentations based on data analysis.
- Collaborate with the development team to ensure data-related issues are addressed promptly.
- Provide ongoing support for data-related inquiries and troubleshooting.
- Support and contribute to the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration, consistent with strategic priorities.
- Develop documentation and guides for data management and analysis processes.

**Your Background**

- Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field. A master’s degree is preferred.
- 5+ years experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar role.
- Strong proficiency in data analysis tools and software (e.g., Python, R, SQL, Excel).
- Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex data clearly and concisely.
- Experience working with non-profit organizations is a plus.
- Work or academic experience focused on topics related to peacebuilding, conflict, human rights, and/or global affairs (or similar).
- Ability to work remotely with limited supervision.
- Excellent organization and time management skills.
- Good judgement and high attention to detail.
- Fluency in English - both written and verbal skills.

title: Mental Health Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTION:**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad. Assistance to Sudanese refugees expanded to include the management of eleven camps in the east and one camp in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, IRC expanded its geographic coverage to Guéra Province, where the organization currently works in five health districts and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population, as well as family planning, response, and prevention activities related to gender-based violence (GBV). In May 2016, IRC established a presence in Lac Province to respond to the crisis caused by Boko Haram. In its 2022–2024 Strategic Action Plan, IRC Chad is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and line ministries in key sectors to ensure that IRC’s actions are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the initiatives undertaken.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Senior Health Coordinator, the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist based in Hadjer Hadid will be responsible for the overall management and implementation of a high-quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) program in all of IRC’s areas of operation, and more specifically in refugee camps. The Mental Health Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Public Health’s mental health program, UNHCR, IRC, HIAS, and all members of the mental health working group in Chad to facilitate the coordination of mental health interventions in the country and strengthen their integration into the minimum package of services provided in health centers and hospitals. The mental health and psychosocial support specialist will supervise health workers in providing prevention, diagnosis, and treatment services for patients with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, using the guidelines of the WHO/UNHCR Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP), and will train new providers on the mhGAP model. She/he will develop standard operating procedures for providing psychological support and psychiatric care, as well as psychosocial support through group psychoeducation and community-based programs. She/he will represent IRC at all mental health working group meetings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Program Coordination:
- Coordinate mental health needs assessments;
- Organize regular meetings on mental health with health program managers and the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) team, in collaboration with other technical coordinators;
- Ensure that mental health and psychosocial support are fully integrated into the various sectors of the health program (primary health care, sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, environmental health) and other IRC programs (WPE and ERD);
- Coordinate the implementation of all interventions in the field of mental health and psychosocial support
- Contribute to capacity building for the MHPSS team to enable them to effectively carry out their duties and ensure a smooth transition;
- Participate in capacity building for local partners (Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, United Nations agencies, etc.) in the field of mental health and psychosocial support;
- Contribute to the development of new funding proposals for mental health and psychosocial support;

**Evaluation and Monitoring of the Quality of Clinical and Community Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services**

- Conduct a situational analysis to identify and assess mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) needs in IRC’s areas of operation in Chad
- Provide formative supervision and/or refresher training for healthcare providers and community health workers.
- Provide specialized mental health consultations and psychosocial support to people with specific needs, including survivors of gender-based violence
- Support the organization of community-based services to improve care, follow-up, and referrals between the community and health facilities.
- Conduct formative supervision of health workers to improve the quality of mental health services provided in health facilities and the community using IRC supervision checklists.
- Ensure that essential medicines and psychotropic drugs approved by the Ministry of Public Health (MSP)/WHO are available in health facilities and that they are properly stored and prescribed by providers.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Reporting**

- In collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator, conduct a monthly analysis of mental health and psychosocial support data and share the database and report with the Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribute to improving the quality of periodic health program reports and donor reports.
- Support the monitoring and evaluation framework for the mental health program through regular data analysis and supervision of program activities in the field;
- Document lessons learned, innovative approaches, and the generation of information and evidence to contribute to IRC’s overall learning;
- Work with the MEAL Coordinator and program managers to ensure that health data collection systems meet the requirements of IRC, the Ministry of Public Health (MSP), and donors

**Partnership, Coordination, and Representation**

- Represent IRC at meetings with partners from the Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, and United Nations agencies working in the mental health and psychosocial support sector
- Participate in the development of the mental health working group’s roadmap
- Provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Health in the development and review of national policies, guidelines, standards, protocols, and programs/modules.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Direct Supervisor: Senior Health Coordinator
- Positions under direct supervision: Mental Health Manager in MIP with the Medical Doctor responsible for the health program
- Indirect supervision: Deputy Director of Programs
- Internal: Communications, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & Logistics Departments
- External: Government partners, humanitarian NGOs, and United Nations agencies

**Job requirements:**

- Advanced degree in clinical mental health, preferably a medical degree with a specialty in psychiatry and experience in neurology;
- Three years of professional experience in the development and management of mental health and psychosocial support programs, preferably in emergency situations or refugee camps;
- In addition to the clinical degree, an additional degree in public health is preferred.
- Knowledge of and experience applying the IASC MHPSS guidelines and best practices as part of previous professional experience.
- Experience in assessment, program design, technical training, and supervision using the WHO’s Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP).
- Flexibility in work;
- Ability to work independently while also being an excellent team leader;
- Technical expertise in program development and in assessing and facilitating training needs;
- Strong organizational and supervisory skills.
- Strong analytical skills demonstrating an understanding of current concepts, priorities, and issues related to monitoring, data collection, and program evaluation;
- Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work in a multicultural environment;
- Fluency in French is required; fluency in English is a plus.

**Work Environment:**

**Security:** He or she will be based in Hadjer Hadid and will travel frequently to IRC’s areas of operation. This is an unaccompanied position.

**Gender Equality**: The IRC is committed to reducing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that enable women to participate in the workforce, including parental leave, safety protocols that take into account the specific needs of men and women, and other supportive benefits and allowances.  
  
**The IRC is an equal opportunity employer**. The IRC evaluates all candidates based on merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

**French Version:**

**DESCRIPTION :**

IRC a commencé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire causée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour à l’est du Tchad. L'assistance aux réfugiés soudanais s’est étendue à la gestion de onze camps dans l'Est et d'un camp dans l'Ouest en apportant un appui aux réfugiés et aux communautés locales en matière de santé, nutrition et eau, hygiène et assainissement. En 2012, IRC a étendu sa couverture géographique dans la province du Guéra où l’organisation travaille actuellement dans cinq districts sanitaires et fournit des services de prévention et de traitement de la malnutrition à la population locale ainsi que des activités de planification familiale, de prévention des violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et de réponse à celles-ci. En mai 2016, IRC a établi sa présence dans la province du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram. L’IRC Tchad s'engage dans son plan d'action stratégique 2022-2024 à continuer à fournir des services humanitaires essentiels en santé, nutrition et protection / VBG, tout en améliorant le bien-être économique et en renforçant la résilience des bénéficiaires, en particulier des femmes et des filles. L’IRC Tchad continuera à travailler avec et à soutenir étroitement les acteurs étatiques / ministères sectoriels des domaines clés afin que les actions de l'IRC s'intègrent dans les politiques nationales pour assurer une meilleure appropriation des actions entreprises.

**Description du poste:**

Sous la supervision directe du Senior Health Coordinator, le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial basé à Hadjer Hadid sera responsable de la gestion globale et de la mise en œuvre du programme de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (SMSPS) de qualité dans toutes les zones d’intervention d’IRC et plus spécifiquement dans les camps de réfugiés. Le spécialiste en santé mentale travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le programme de santé mentale du ministère de la Santé publique (MSP), le HCR, l'IRC, HIAS et tous les membres du groupe de travail en santé mentale au Tchad afin de faciliter la coordination des interventions en santé mentale dans le pays et renforcer leur intégration dans le paquet minimum des activités fournies dans les centres de santé et les hôpitaux. Le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial supervisera les agents de santé dans la fourniture des services de prévention, de diagnostic et de traitement des patients souffrant de troubles mentaux, neurologiques et de toxicomanie en utilisant les directives du programme d'action pour les lacunes en matière de santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS / HCR et formera de nouveaux prestataires sur le modèle mhGAP. Elle / il développera des procédures opérationnelles standard pour la fourniture d'un soutien psychologique et de soins psychiatriques, ainsi qu’un soutien psychosocial par le biais de la psychoéducation de groupe et de programmes communautaires. Elle /Il représentera IRC dans toutes les réunions du groupe de travail en santé mentale.

**Responsabilités principales :**

**Coordination de programme :**

- Coordonner les évaluations des besoins en santé mentale ;
- Organiser des réunions régulières sur la santé mentale avec les gestionnaires du programme santé et l’équipe SMSPS en collaboration avec les autres coordinateurs techniques ;
- S’assurer que la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial sont pleinement intégrés aux différents secteurs du programme santé (santé primaire, santé sexuelle et reproductive, nutrition, santé environnementale) et aux autres programmes de l’IRC (WPE et ERD) ;
- Coordonner la mise en œuvre de toutes les interventions dans le domaine de la SMSPS
- Contribuer au renforcement des capacités de l’équipe SMSPS pour leur permettre d’assurer efficacement leurs fonctions et d’assurer la relève ;
- Participer au renforcement des capacités des partenaires locaux (MSP, ONG, agences des Nations Unies, etc.) dans le domaine de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial.
- Contribuer à l’élaboration de nouvelles propositions de financement en santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial;

**Évaluation et suivi de la qualité des services cliniques et communautaires de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial**

- Mener une analyse de la situation afin d'identifier et d'évaluer les besoins en SMSPS dans les zones d’intervention de IRC au Tchad
- Réaliser des supervisions formatives et/ou des recyclages à l’intention des prestataires de soins et des agents de santé communautaires.
- Réaliser les consultations spécialisées en santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial des personnes ayant des besoins spécifiques, y compris les survivants des VBG
- Apporter un appui à l’organisation de l’offre des services communautaires pour une meilleure prise en charge, le suivi et le référencement entre la communauté et les établissements de santé.
- Réaliser les supervisions formatives des agents de santé afin d’améliorer la qualité de services de santé mentale fournis dans les établissements de santé et la communauté à l'aide des listes de contrôle de supervision d’IRC.
- S’assurer que les médicaments essentiels et les psychotropes approuvés par le MSP/OMS sont disponibles dans les établissements de santé et qu’ils sont correctement stockés et prescrits par les prestataires.

**Suivi, évaluation, recherche, apprentissage et rapportage**

- En collaboration avec le Coordinateur MEAL, faire une analyse mensuelle des données de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial et partager la base des données et le rapport avec le Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration de la qualité des rapports périodiques du programme santé et des rapports bailleurs.
- Soutenir le dispositif de suivi et évaluation appliqué au programme de santé mentale à travers des analyses régulières des données et la supervision des activités du programme sur le terrain ;
- Documenter les leçons apprises, les approches innovantes et la production d’informations et de données probantes afin de participer à l’apprentissage global d’IRC ;
- Travailler avec le Coordinateur MEAL et les responsables du programme afin de s’assurer que les systèmes de collecte des données santé remplissent les exigences d’IRC, du MSP et des bailleurs.

**Partenariat, Coordination et Représentation**

- Représenter IRC aux réunions avec les partenaires du ministère de la santé, les ONG et les agences des Nations Unies qui interviennent dans le secteur de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial
- Participer à l’élaboration de la feuille de route du groupe de travail en santé mentale
- Apporter une assistance technique au MSP dans l’élaboration et l’examen des politiques, directives, normes, protocoles, programmes/modules nationaux.

**Principales relations de travail:**

- **Superviseur Hiérarchique :** Senior Health Coordinator  
    **Position sous supervision directe :** Manager Santé Mentale en MIP avec le Médecin responsable du programme santé
- **Supervision indirecte:** Directeur adjoint des Programmes
- **Internes :** Département de communication, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & logistique
- **Externes** *:* Les partenaires de l’État, ONG humanitaires & Agences des Nations Unies

**Exigences du poste:**

- Diplôme supérieur en santé mentale clinique, de préférence un diplôme de médecin avec une spécialisation en psychiatrie et une expérience en neurologie ;
- Trois années d'expérience professionnelle dans le développement et la gestion de programmes de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial, de préférence dans les situations d'urgence ou dans des camps de réfugiés ;
- En plus du diplôme clinique, un diplôme supplémentaire en santé publique est préférable.
- Connaissance et expérience d’application des directives et des bonnes pratiques de l’IASC en matière de SMSPS dans le cadre de son expérience professionnelle antérieure.
- Expérience de l'évaluation, de la conception de programmes, de la formation technique et de la supervision à l'aide du programme d'action contre les lacunes en santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS.
- Flexibilité dans le travail ;
- Capacité à travailler de manière autonome tout en étant un excellent chef d'équipe ;
- Une expertise technique dans l’élaboration de programme et dans l’évaluation et facilitation des besoins en formation ;
- Solides compétences en matière d'organisation et de supervision.
- Solides capacités d’analyse démontrant une compréhension des concepts, priorités et problèmes actuels en matière de suivi, de collecte de données et d'évaluation de programmes.
- Solides compétences interpersonnelles et capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel.
- La maîtrise de la langue française est requise ; la maîtrise de l'anglais est un atout.

**Environnement de travail :**

**Sécurité :** Il (elle) sera basé/e à Hadjer Hadid avec des déplacements fréquents dans les zones d’intervention d’IRC.Le poste est non accompagné**.**

**Égalité des sexes :** L'IRC s'est engagé à réduire l'écart entre les sexes dans les postes de direction. Nous offrons des avantages qui permettent aux femmes de participer à la vie active, notamment un congé parental, des protocoles de sécurité tenant compte des spécificités des hommes et des femmes et d'autres avantages et allocations de soutien.

**L'IRC est un employeur soucieux de l'égalité des chances. L'IRC** examine tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans considération de race, de sexe, de couleur, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, d'état civil, de statut d'ancien combattant ou de handicap.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Tupande Health, Safety, Security, and Transport (HSST) Coordinator
body:
## Job Description 

Seeking a strategic leaders to lead Transport, OSH, and Security operations. You will manage a team, drive efficiency and compliance, and optimize budgets to ensure a safe, cost-effective environment for Tupande staff and partners.

## Job Level

JL 5

## Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Expected Manager

Ignetius Mukokho

## Will this position be managing others?

Yes, One Transport and Dispatch Senior Supervisor JL4 and three Senior Transport Officers JL2

## Key Job Responsibilities

Manage the Transport workstream.

- Oversee transport workstream daily operations to maintain high-quality standards and exceptional service provision.
- Implement and audit transport workstream management systems to maintain expected performance standards.
- Manage the transport workstream assets through their life cycle for adequate work resourcing.
- Manage large and minor transport workstream projects, ensuring timely completion and customer satisfaction.
- Act as the primary decision-maker for day-to-day transport operational roadblocks, resolving driver or vehicle issues that the supervisors cannot handle.
- Enforce transport policies and maintenance schedules, ensuring the supervisors keep vehicles compliant, clean, and roadworthy.

Support the Occupational Safety and Health workstream

- Engage with relevant internal and external stakeholders to plan, implement, and complete annual OSH audits and related training.
- Organize all audit reports and training certificates for ease of sharing with relevant stakeholders
- Support in overseeing the OSH compliance for all relevant Tupande locations across all our regions of operation.
- Coordinate the implementation of all OSH audit recommendations to ensure 100% implementation rate across all audited locations.

Support Security Operations

- Act as the primary daily contact for the Vendor Security Manager regarding routine deployment updates, ad-hoc requests, and immediate operational issues.
- Validate the daily/weekly reports submitted by the security service provider against the internal observations to ensure "ghost guards" or missed shifts are flagged before invoicing.
- Follow up with the vendor's technical team on maintenance and track their turnaround time to ensure they meet the maintenance Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Collaborate with the Security service provider during initial incident responses; ensure the vendor’s Incident Reports capture the full internal context and accuracy required.
- Track recurring performance issues to provide data and talking points for the HSST lead during the monthly stakeholder sync-ups.
- Coordinate with the security vendor to ensure access control protocols are being enforced on the ground as per Tupande’s policy across all locations.

Budget and Cost Management

- Collate and track expenditure data for Transport, OSH, and Security to assist in budget analysis.
- Analyse HSST workstream expenditure to develop strategies to manage or reduce recurring expenses while maintaining quality.
- Support in preparation of monthly BvA reports for leadership review.
- Monitor budget levels to curb overspends and achieve 10% budget savings annually.
- Review vendor invoices against LPOs to ensure accurate vendor payments

People Management

- Recruit the right team members to fill any personnel gaps.
- Identify and facilitate opportunities for professional growth and development.
- Develop and train the team on HSST workstream performance metrics so they know what success in their roles looks like.
- Track, audit, and report on HSST workstream performance metrics to ensure the team achieves performance expectations.
- Identify potential future leaders within the team and develop their skills to prepare them for leadership roles.
- Foster a collaborative and inclusive workplace culture, implementing initiatives to boost team morale and motivation.

## Top Skills and Qualifications

Technical skills:

- Google Suite applications, i.e., Google Sheets and Google Docs.
- Proficiency in software and systems that manage and track transport operations.
- Experience with tools used for raising PRs and managing vendor payments.

Knowledge:

- Knowledge of fleet management and logistics principles, including route efficiency, scheduling maintenance, conducting safety checks, and ensuring proper vehicle performance.
- Familiarity with safety regulations and compliance standards in the transport industry.
- Knowledge of applicable safety regulations and transport industry-specific compliance requirements.
- Knowledge of OSHA and safety regulations in Kenya.
- Ability to conduct a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment to assist the HSST Lead.
- Knowledge of fire suppression systems and evacuation drill protocols.
- Understanding of security and basic access controls, technology and regulation
- SLA management and understanding of how to hold private security firms accountable to Guard Force Instructions (GFIs).

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Sponsor International Candidates

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

12 November 2026. Applications after this date will be accepted on a rolling basis.

*For more information reach out to ignetius.mukokho@oneacrefund.org*

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:( 20.97$/hourly**): Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Needs Assessment Consultant - Venezuela
body:
Relief International (RI) is seeking an experienced consultant or consulting firm to conduct a comprehensive needs assessment following the recent earthquake in Venezuela. The assessment will inform RI's decision on whether and how to establish a rehabilitation-focused programme and longer-term presence in the country.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities affected by conflict, climate change, and disasters to save lives, strengthen resilience, and support long-term health and wellbeing. RI works across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, delivering programmes in Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Livelihoods.

**The Opportunity**

Following an earthquake that has impacted communities and health services in Venezuela, RI is exploring potential humanitarian interventions focused on physical rehabilitation and assistive technology. We are seeking a consultant or firm to lead an evidence-based assessment that will identify priority needs, evaluate existing services and referral pathways, assess market and supply-chain feasibility for assistive technologies, and provide practical recommendations for future programming.

The consultancy will include desk review, service mapping, primary data collection, analysis, stakeholder engagement, and final reporting.

**Scope of the Assessment**

The assessment will focus on:

- Rehabilitation needs of earthquake-affected populations.
- People with pre-existing disabilities whose access to care has been disrupted.
- Individuals with newly acquired impairments resulting from earthquake-related injuries.
- Access to physical rehabilitation services, prosthetics and orthotics (P&O), assistive technology, and relevant mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.
- Existing service capacity, referral pathways, and partnership opportunities.
- Market availability and feasibility of assistive technologies, including spectacles, hearing aids, and other priority devices.

**Key Responsibilities**

The successful consultant or firm will:

- Design and implement the assessment methodology.
- Conduct secondary data review and stakeholder mapping.
- Lead qualitative primary data collection, including key informant interviews and focus group discussions.
- Assess rehabilitation service availability, accessibility, and continuity of care.
- Evaluate assistive technology markets, suppliers, and supply chains.
- Analyze findings and identify priority needs and service gaps.
- Develop feasible programme options and recommendations for RI.
- Facilitate a validation workshop with RI stakeholders.
- Produce high-quality reports and decision-making materials.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

Essential

- Significant experience conducting humanitarian needs assessments, health assessments, disability inclusion assessments, or similar assignments.
- Strong technical expertise in physical rehabilitation and continuity of care.
- Knowledge of prosthetics and orthotics (P&O) services and assistive technology provision.
- Experience assessing health systems, referral pathways, service gaps, and partnership opportunities.
- Proven qualitative research and analytical skills.
- Demonstrated ability to develop practical programme recommendations and indicative costings.
- Excellent report-writing skills.
- Ability to work independently and manage assessment activities within tight deadlines.

Desirable

- Experience in Venezuela or comparable contexts in Latin America.
- Professional proficiency in Spanish and English.
- Experience working with rehabilitation providers, Ministries of Health, OPDs, or humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Experience assessing assistive technology markets and procurement pathways.
- Familiarity with HD-NEST, Washington Group Questions, or other disability-inclusive assessment tools.
- Experience supporting organizations entering new geographic contexts.

**Consultancy Details**

**Location:** Venezuela (assessment locations to be proposed and agreed with RI)  
**Duration:** Approximately 7-8 weeks from contract signature  
**Expected Period:** November to December 2026

title: Logistics Officer (Ukrainian Nationals only)
body:
**Job Title:** Logistics Officer

**Department:** Operations

**Division:** Logistics & Procurement

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Logistics Coordinator

**Technical Line Manager:** Senior Logistics Officer

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**OVERVIEW:**

The role is within the Nonviolent Peaceforce - Ukraine Country office (CO) to provide a central support service to multiple departments. We are looking for someone with a passion for organisation and accuracy looking to use their skills in complex administration, multi-tasking and problem-solving to make an impact on NP’s administrative and operational duties.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Logistics Officer provides operational and administrative support to the Country Office and all field offices, focusing on procurement, rental and lease agreements, logistics-related payments, cost tracking, and documentation. The role ensures accurate and timely processing of procurement and payment requests, compliance with organizational procedures and donor requirements, and effective communication with field teams, Finance, suppliers, and service providers.

This varied role, will require a high-level of organisational, communication and IT skills to provide a key central support function to various teams: HR, Finance and the Field teams, in particular the Field Programme Officers (FPO).

The role supports the Country Office and all field offices with administrative and operational duties. This includes performing a variety of administrative tasks, including management of office and accommodation contracts, management of the office administration.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

1\. **Commitment to NP Principles:**

- Demonstrate a commitment to NP’s mandate and principles.
- Maintain a positive image of the organisation full-time while communicating with external actors, staff or operating in the field.

2\. **Support to Logistics:**

- Process procurement of goods and services valued below USD 10,000 for the Country Office and all field offices, including simple procurement and procedures requiring BID analysis.
- Research the market, collect and compare supplier quotations, and update the vendor list to support purchasing decisions.
- Arrange procurement for office facilities and premises-related needs, compare options for value for money, and prepare the required contractual documentation.
- Check facility-related contracts and service providers, follow up on service quality and delivery issues, and report any non-compliance with agreed terms.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for utilities, facility services, consumables, and office supplies required by the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare vehicle lease agreements for the Country Office and all NP field offices, follow up on negotiations and signatures, and track renewals and contract implementation.
- Follow up on payments under fuel supply agreements for vehicle refuelling across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Arrange and track payments for vehicle servicing, maintenance, and repairs for the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Prepare and follow up on monthly payments for rented premises, including offices, hubs, and guesthouses, across the Country Office and all NP field offices.
- Check that payment processing and supporting documents comply with NP policies, procurement procedures, delegated approval limits, contractual terms, and donor requirements where applicable.
- Prepare monthly requests and supporting documents for office-related costs, including rent, utilities, telephone services, and other recurring charges, and check them for completeness and compliance with organizational procedures.
- Support monthly cost planning and forecasting by collecting and consolidating information on rent, utilities, facility services, fuel, vehicle maintenance, and other recurring logistics expenses across the Country Office and field offices.
- Track submitted, pending, overdue, and completed payments; follow up on delays with Finance and suppliers; and update the relevant trackers and stakeholders.
- Check invoices and payment requests against the relevant contract, purchase order, delivery or service confirmation, approved budget, and payment terms; clarify discrepancies before submission.
- File payment and procurement records in the relevant SharePoint folders and provide required hard copies to Finance, including BID analyses and payment tracking documents.
- Compile and verify procurement records and update the Purchase Request (PR) tracker with the latest status.
- File logistics documents in the relevant SharePoint folders and arrange for required hard copies to be retained by Finance, including BID analyses, payment documents, and payment trackers.
- Maintain a consolidated payment calendar for recurring and contractual costs, track due dates, and notify relevant colleagues of upcoming deadlines or missing documents.
- Carry out other logistics duties assigned by the Senior Logistics Officer or Logistics Coordinator\*\*.\*\*

3\. **Support to Administration:**

- Update tracking tools and databases for recurring monthly costs, procurement progress, lease agreements, and other operational records.
- Serve as the contact point for office and accommodation lease agreements and related technical services, and assist with drafting and reviewing rental contracts.
- Check contract balances, advance payments, deposits, and outstanding liabilities for assigned services and premises, and flag discrepancies and upcoming renewals or expiries in good time.
- Collect and consolidate monthly payment requests from field offices, check submissions for completeness and consistency, and return incomplete or unclear requests to the relevant focal points for correction.
- Keep in regular contact with Field Team Leaders and FPOs to identify upcoming operational needs, confirm expected costs, resolve documentation issues, and support the timely submission of payment requests.
- Inform Field Team Leaders, FPOs, and relevant budget holders about payment delays, contract or supplier issues, missing approvals, and actions required from them.
- Send documents to the relevant teams and follow up to ensure they reach the appropriate staff for review, approval, and filing.
- Prepare complete and accurate payment packages for Finance, checking that supporting documents are available, approvals are in place, and payment details are correct.
- Liaise with Finance and budget holders to check budget availability, budget codes and donor allocations, required approvals, and the status of submitted payments.
- Provide administrative assistance to the Logistics team as required.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- High school diploma.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft applications, in particular Word & Excel, other applications an asset. High level of computer literacy, knowledge of Salesforce a significant benefit.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

- Experience working in NP or similar organisation.
- Familiarity with INGO logistics and administration structure and function with preferred experience within NP.

**KEY CHALLENGES:**

- Building and sustaining collaborative partnerships, negotiating, and resolving contentious issues and conflicts of interest while managing and balancing varied, diverse stakeholder priorities across a geographically dispersed region.

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

- Experience in I/NGO administration, office management, procurement and/or logistics.
- Good knowledge and understanding of the conflict context in Ukraine expected.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in English and Ukrainian.
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a team and independently.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Independent Judgment/Analytical: Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

- This country office position includes travel to field locations (Kramatorsk, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Kherson) and may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable and changeable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic accommodation, which may include shared housing during travel and field site support tasks.
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols and maintain high level of discipline.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) [Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

title: Regional Emergency Response Advisor (Asia)
body:
***Job Summary***

The STRIDES Regional Emergency Response Advisor supports outbreak response planning, coordination, and implementation across Asia, ideally bringing prior experience with high-consequence pathogens. The advisor aligns country programs with STRIDES leadership’s direction, tracking and reporting on response efforts while leading coordination with technical, finance, and operations teams to mobilize resources. They develop tools and guidance, and work within established incident management frameworks to strengthen emergency readiness and execution. In addition, this person will manage the creation of knowledge products—reports, technical materials, and conflict-sensitive solutions. Working with project teams and HQ, the advisor leads program evaluations on effectiveness, reviews technical/operational activities, and directs assessment reports across their portfolio. The role also contributes to business development, including pursuing opportunities, capture/proposal leadership, and building partnerships. This position will be based either in Manila, Bangkok, or Jakarta.

## ***Accountabilities:***

**Technical Requirements:**

- Leads outbreak response and preparedness activities in alignment with established STRIDES emergency response protocols and in-country incident management systems.
- Manages the coordination of day-to-day response activities across technical, operational, and administrative teams to ensure alignment with response objectives and timelines.
- Oversees the consolidation of response information and manages internal coordination during active outbreaks.
- Leads standardization of response processes across their portfolio of countries, including reporting templates, deployment trackers, and coordination tools.
- Spreadheads continuous improvement of emergency response systems by integrating lessons learned and best practices into tools and guidance.
- Provides project staff with overall technical direction and guidance in line with the project expected outcomes.
- Leads analysis of project implementation to identify areas for improvement and propose appropriate technical strategy and guidelines.
- Manages the collaboration with the research and evaluation team to report on data and assessments.
- Leads the development and dissemination of tools, materials, reports, papers, and intervention for research projects.
- Serves as the authoritative on emergency response and preparedness best practices to assist with implementation
- Reviews technical work plans and budgets for accuracy and aligned with the STRIDES program and donor goals.

**Project Design Implementation:**

- Mentors and provides technical guidance to junior emergency response staff and partners across the region; may supervise junior technical staff, sub-contractors, and others implementing technical project work.
- With technical oversight, provide technical leadership in design, development, planning, implementation; and capacity- building of specific technical components of projects
- Creates technical portion of the project plan, within the given resource and financial constraints
- Directs the day-to-day technical and operational activities of assigned projects, tracking delivery of project outputs and monitoring staff members' LOE (Level of Effort) needs to ensure adequate coverage of resources.
- Coordinates requests from CO (Country Office) for technical assistance
- Engages in the design, development, planning, and implementation of global-level innovative technical strategies.
- Develops or writes technical briefs, reports, or other necessary materials to facilitate research, best practices, policies, and procedures.
- Leads collaboration with the DTT (Digital Transformation & Technology) team to develop and maintain response tracking systems (e.g., dashboards, trackers, logs) to support situational awareness and decision-making.
- Oversees the adaption and maintenance of tools, templates, SOPs (standard operating procedures), guidance notes, and job aids to support outbreak preparedness and response activities, ensuring implementation is consistent with best practices in the industry/subject and meets client/funder contractual obligations.

**Business Development and Client/Funder Support:**

- Maintains collaborative relationships with donor/client organizations, relevant government agencies, bilateral and other NGOs (non governmental organizations) and consistently maintained and viewed as a knowledgeable resource in their technical area.
- Leads proposal research and development proposal strategies, which consists of directing proposal research, data collection, and strategies.
- Reviews proposal, budgets, and workplans.
- Participate in client / funder meetings and provide technical input, and drafts sponsor reports and presentations
- Represents the organization and / or Institute to external entities at professional meetings and conferences.

**Capacity Building, Training and Supervision:**

- Develops and implements technical training and capacity building interventions related to emergency response and preparedness.
- Supervises and/or provide technical guidance to staff members locally and in the region.

**Operations Management (Finance, HR, etc.):**

- Manages the processes, services, planning, organizing, coordinating, and controlling of all technical resources for a project.
- Directs efforts to work with the Finance Team to develop and track response budgets, spending forecasts, and cost monitoring in coordination with finance teams.
- Oversees the processing of emergency procurement requests, consultant deployments, and surge staffing needs.
- Ensures the overall project portfolio remains aligned with organizational timelines, technical standards, and donor/client expectations, holding junior technical officers accountable for work plan execution.
- Manages the timelines of multiple projects and budgets, leading the development of donor reports and presentations.
- Proposes and executes solutions to operational resource gaps and constraints
- Reviews SOPs (standard operating procedures), SOW (statement of work), and reports on technical and financial tracking data.
- Cultivates supplier relationships to ensure rapid procurements for outbreak response

**Project/Program Reporting:**

- Organizes processes with the MEL Team to track outbreak response activities, milestones, deliverables, and resource utilization across response pillars or workstreams.
- Reviews regular situation reports, activity summaries, and operational updates for leadership, partners, and donors as required.
- Manages the timely and accurate documentation of response actions, lessons learned, and after-action inputs.
- Oversees SOWs and budget tracking systems
- Drafts sponsor financial and technical reports.
- Collates and uploads output and deliverables data to sponsor data systems.
- Prepares and delivers presentations to sponsors on progress.
- Helps in the development and review of country work plans.

**Quality Assurance:**

- Ensures technical deliverables are consistent with best practices in the industry / subject and meet client / funder contractual obligations
- Identifies areas for improved efficiency or effectiveness within prescribed parameters, and institutes enhancements to procedures.

## ***Applied Knowledge & Skills:***

- Ensures appropriate and timely technical support for field projects.
- Ensures the quality of implemented technical activities and systems at all levels. Conducts routine coordination with employees and consultants, on-site and in the field.
- Strong knowledge and skills in a specific technical area/function and general understanding of concepts and principles of related technical areas/functions.
- Solid knowledge of standards for the technical area/field, operational processes and procedures, work, and task flow.
- Has the ability to manage projects, set realistic priorities, and plan for the successful implementation of activities.
- Proficient writing and verbal communication skills.
- Relevant computer software skills (including, at a minimum, the standard applications in MS Office).
- Ability to manage their own work to job and performance standards.
- Must be able to read, write and speak fluent English fluent in host country language. Other languages would be helpful, including: Georgian, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Nepali, Bengali, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, Filipino, or Indonesian.

## ***Competencies:***

There are 31 FHI 360 development competencies, of greatest focus for this particular job will be:

- Project Management (Planning and Time Management) - Accurately scopes out length and difficulty of tasks (sets objectives/goals/measures). Breaks down work into steps, schedules, task/people assignments. Marshals people, time, and resources efficiently. Arranges information in a useful manner and orchestrates multiple activities at once.
- People Management (Making Others Great) – Facilitate professional development of staff by providing challenging, learning assignments and opportunities. Shares and solicits feedback monthly at the very least. Helps establish compelling development plans. Assigns responsibility and accountability for tasks/decisions. Monitors process, progress, and results. Creates a climate in which people want to do their best.
- Creating and Managing Systems and Processes – Recognizes the need for standardization and balances client and organization need in systems design. Anticipates the effects of process change on people while optimizing task efficiency and simplicity.
- Employees are expected to possess or have high potential for the development of these three fundamental competencies.

## ***Problem Solving & Impact:***

- Demonstrates the ability to assess needs within agreed upon duties and considers course of action best to meet those needs.
- Effectively applies knowledge of technical area to solve a range of problems. Demonstrates the ability to develop solutions to problems that cannot be solved using existing methods or approaches.
- Faulty decisions/ recommendations /failures to complete assignments will normally result in serious delays to assigned projects resulting in considerable expenditure of additional time, resources, and funds.
- Decisions and actions impact primarily workflow, project processes and timeframes. Problems encountered are varied, requiring review of practices and precedents to resolve. Problem solving involves evaluating and resolving discrepancies with data, analyses, processes, etc. within prescribed guidelines.
- Policies or guidelines exist for most problems; others must be referred to by a supervisor or more senior professional.

## ***Supervision Given/Received:***

- May supervise junior staff members.
- Coordinates own workflow and sets individual priorities.
- Works under general guidelines for completion and accuracy as determined by the supervisor.
- Accomplishes results through lower-level staff managers or through experienced staff who exercise independence in their assignments.
- May manage a centralized functional area of activity.
- Serves as mentor to more inexperienced technical staff.

## ***Education:***

- Master’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Knowledge/Information Services, Communications, Education, Environment, Health, Behavioral, Life/Social Sciences International Development, Human Development or Related Field.
- Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.

## ***Experience:***

- Typically requires 8+ years of relevant experience in technical implementation of large projects and/or programs – may manage activities of lower-level staff, however, main function is individual contributor.
- Documented experience providing technical assistance, capacity building and business development in the specific technical domain.
- Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or private organization.
- International or Domestic (US) Program Development or Program management preferred.
- In-depth knowledge of concepts, practices and procedures associated with outbreak emergency response, with a focus on high consequence pathogens.
- Development of scope of work and deliverables for partners, consultants, etc.
- Broader knowledge of incident management (IM) structures, emergency response frameworks, and quality standards for outbreak response
- Has sensitivity to cultural differences and understanding of political, contextual, and ethical issues.
- Must be able to read, write and speak fluent English fluent in host country language. Other languages would be helpful, including: Georgian, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Nepali, Bengali, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, Filipino, or Indonesian.
- Excellent organizational and analytical skills.
- Ability to influence and collaborate with others.
- Ability to analyze and interpret data, identify errors, and prepare reports.
- Ability to solve problems and implement corrective action as needed.

## ***Typical Physical Demands***\*\*:\*\*

- Typical office environment.
- Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
- Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
- Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.

## ***Technology to be Used***\*\*:\*\*

- Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

## ***Travel Requirements:***

- Up to 35%

***The expected hiring salary range for this role is PHP 2,500,000 - 3,500,000 for annual basic salary. When determining an offer amount, FHI 360 factors in multiple considerations, including but not limited to: relevant years of experience and education possessed by the applicant, internal equity, market pay, and budget. For internal candidates, salary placement will also follow FHI 360’s current promotional increase guidelines.***

This job posting summarizes the main duties of the job. It neither prescribes nor restricts the exact tasks that may be assigned to carry out these duties. This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time.

FHI 360 is an [equal opportunity employer](http://www.fhi360.org/careers/eeo) whereby we do not engage in practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.

Our values and commitments to safeguarding:FHI 360 is committed to preventing any type of abuse, exploitation and harassment in our work environments and programs, including sexual abuse, exploitation and harassment. FHI 360 takes steps to safeguard the welfare of everyone who engages with our organization and programs and requires that all personnel, including staff members and volunteers, share this commitment and sign our code of conduct. All offers of employment will be subject to appropriate screening checks, including reference, criminal record and terrorism finance checks. FHI 360 also participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), facilitated by the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response. In line with the MDS, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any substantiated findings of sexual abuse, exploitation and/or harassment during the applicant’s tenure with previous employers. By applying, job applicants confirm their understanding of these recruitment procedures and consent to these screening checks.

FHI 360 will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws.

**FHI 360 will never ask you for your career site username or password, and we will never request money, goods or services during the application, recruitment or employment process. If you have questions or concerns about correspondence from us, please email CareerCenterSupport@fhi360.org.**

title: Baseline Study Consultant
source: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
body:
**Baseline Study Consultant**

**Organisation**

Amal Organization for Relief and Development

**Position**

Baseline Study Consultant

**Type of Contract**

Short-Term Consultancy

**Location**

Home-based with field mission travel to Aleppo, Syria

**Relevant languages**

English, Arabic

**Application Deadline**

17.11.2026

**Starting Date**

01.12.2026

**Project Title**

Fostering climate-resilient livelihoods,  
inclusive learning environments,  
and social cohesion in conflict-affected Aleppo

**Background and Organisational Setting**

This baseline study is commissioned, prior to project implementation, under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) budget for development projects run by private organisations.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Amal Organization for Relief and Development (Amal)being the local implementing partner.

The project aims to sustainably strengthen the resilience and recovery capacities of conflict-affected communities in Eastern Aleppo through an integrated approach that links livelihoods, education, and social cohesion. In the livelihoods component, market-oriented and sustainable vocational training, entrepreneurship support, on-the-job training and apprenticeship schemes, as well as small grants will be provided to promote sustainable income opportunities. In parallel, the project supports access to quality education by rehabilitating educational infrastructure, integrating mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and social-emotional learning (SEL), and strengthening teachers’ capacities. Complementary activities will foster social cohesion through dialogue-based youth- and women-led initiatives, contributing to trust-building in conflict-affected Aleppo. By combining these components, the project contributes to community stabilisation and the creation of long-term development prospects.  
Direct target group: 3,850 people

**Baseline Study Objectives**

The purpose of the baseline study is to provide SoH with a sound basis for developing a complete project concept, by identifying project prerequisites, opportunities and risks. This process includes an assessment of the baseline of the proposed project intervention to assess if it can plausibly achieve planned objectives given existing contextual realities.

This comprehensive study will verify relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the proposed project intervention. The study will provide concrete and practical recommendations that will assist with the finalisation of project design elements, including the logframe, risk analysis, problem analysis and relevance of the proposed project intervention, stakeholder analysis, among others.

The study will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process regarding the funding of the proposed project activities.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The selected Consultant will work in close cooperation with the responsible SoH Officer and the local implementing partner.

The duties and responsibilities of the consultant will include:

- Develop a work plan outlining the proposed research methodology, geographical coverage, and schedule to conduct the baseline study,
- Carry out a project site visit to the project location to conduct research, collect data and establish contact with the local implementing partner, potential beneficiaries and relevant project stakeholders,
- Review existing policies and structures, government development strategies as well as relevant studies and research projects that could serve as a basis for the baseline study,

Identify relevant project stakeholders at various levels (local, district and national if applicable), including local governing bodies, academia and industry as well as lessons learned and best practises of similar on-going and implemented projects relevant to the project, including the identification and assessment of existing formal and informal organisational structures among the target groups, comprising their composition, membership, roles, capacities, representativeness and level of participation,

- Evaluate all available data and sources providing background information on identified issues, the problem analysis as well as the selected intervention and establish the baseline values for all indicators included in the project impact matrix using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods, including the respective data sources and measurement methods,
- Assess the proposed activities, as well as their timing and required financial resources.
- Assess the physical condition, safety, accessibility and functionality of the four selected schools and the existing VTC facilities, including relevant equipment and refurbishment needs,
- Examine institutional, technical, staffing and financial capacities of the selected implementing partner, as well as its relationship with the target group. Based on the findings, determine if there are areas in which capacities of the local implementing partner need to be developed,
- Review main governmental and non-governmental stakeholders with a purpose to see if there is a potential overlap or conflict of interest as well as opportunities for coordination with the aim of creating synergies and new cooperation partnerships, while also assessing the alignment of the proposed project with the national recovery plan,
- Examine the identified target group, its needs and role in the broader social context as well as the relevance of the planned project activities for addressing their needs,
- Assess the environmental and climate-related production practices of selected enterprises, including energy and water use, waste generation, raw material efficiency, procurement and processing practices.
- Identify potential obstacles and alternatives to overcome the foreseen challenges,
- Review and analyse all available project design elements and draft documents related to the project concept, if necessary,
- Critically review the planned project in terms of OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability (please see [http://www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html](http://www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html)),
- Prepare a report containing the findings on the above items, specific recommendations for the project concept with a view to planning and implementing foreseen project activities.

**Expected Deliverables**

The study will produce the following deliverables:

- a baseline study outline, including the proposed methodology and data collection tools, table of content and a timeline of research activities (inception report) prior to the site visit to the project location,
- a summary containing a brief overview and the main findings of the study,
- Baseline values for all indicators included in the project impact matrix, specifying the respective data sources and measurement methods.
- a comprehensive report of a maximum of 30 pages with practical recommendations and relevant annexes,
- Findings and recommendations regarding the condition of the four selected schools and the existing VTC facilities, including identified refurbishment and equipment needs.
- a review of the main project design elements and provision of concrete recommendations for improvement,
- an analysis of the institutional structure required for project implementation, stipulating the roles and responsibilities of staff members involved, a detailed problem analysis, a stakeholder analysis, a revision of the target group, an analysis of the potential risks and recommendations on how to mitigate these risks, a schedule of project activities, a financial plan (planning budget), a detailed project logframe with SMART indicators for the project objective and results listing related activities and required resources,
- a “Do-no-harm analysis” including recommendations on how to mitigate potential harm and conflict situations that can potentially arise during or as a result of the project activities
- a Gender mainstreaming analysis identifying potential risks and recommendations to ensure gender equality in all aspects of the project design and implementation.

A template will be provided to serve as a guide and suggested structure for the final report.

**Process/Timeframe**

- A total duration of the assignment is up to 20 working days within the period of 01.12.2026 to 28.12.2026.
- A planning meeting with Amal, handover of relevant documents 1 day
- Initial document review and preparing inception report 3 days
- Sharing inception report with SoH and Amal 1 day
- Data collection site visit to a project location 5 days
- Data analysis, draft report with annexes, presenting to SoH 5 days
- Incorporating received feedback and finalising the report 5 days

**Qualifications and Experience**

Essential:

- Minimum of 5 years of project evaluation and/or implementation experience in the result-based management framework
- Proven experience of conducting baseline studies, evaluations and other research projects
- Technical and methodological knowledge to conduct research projects and formulate conclusions based on a solid methodology, assessing projects for relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of projects
- Experience working with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and partnered projects
