title: Expression of interest: Humanitarian Health and Climate Collaborative – Ethiopia Anchor Institution
body:
## **Overview**

Elrha is seeking to identify a single anchor institution to act as the national secretariat, operational coordinator and strategic home for the Humanitarian Health and Climate Collaborative (HHCC) in Ethiopia. Ethiopia has been selected as the first national hub, creating an opportunity to establish a credible, country-led mechanism that strengthens local capacity, informs national decision-making and contributes learning to wider regional and global efforts on climate and health in humanitarian crises.

Elrha is a global organisation that strengthens humanitarian action by supporting the generation, use and scale of research and innovation that improve outcomes for people affected by crises. The HHCC will bring together public health, climate, humanitarian, research, government and community actors to generate, test and use evidence for more anticipatory and adaptive health action in crisis settings.

## **Objective**

The anchor institution will provide leadership, convening and operational stability for the Ethiopia hub. It will:

- **National secretariat and coordination:** Host the HHCC secretariat, assign core personnel, manage hub operations and act as a trusted convening point across government, academia, meteorological services, humanitarian responders and crisis-affected communities.
- **Governance and priority setting:** Establish and convene a national multi-sectoral Steering Group and help identify one or two priority climate hazards for focused collaborative action.
- **Ecosystem scoping and programme design:** Lead participatory ecosystem scoping to map evidence gaps, operational challenges, active initiatives, data sources, research questions and innovation opportunities, then co-design the Years 2–5 programme of work.
- **Evidence translation and uptake:** Connect climate information with health-sector contingency planning and support the translation of evidence into national policy, planning and frontline humanitarian practice.
- **Grant management readiness:** Establish the governance, technical review, financial management and due diligence systems needed to assume devolved research and innovation grant-making responsibilities from Year 2, subject to institutional assessment and systems readiness.

## **Timeline**

- 2 November 2026: invitation for expressions of interest
- 20 November 2026: Deadline for EOI submissions
- December 2026: Communication on grant award (expected)
- December 2026 - January 2027: Due diligence and contracting completed (anticipated)
- January 2027: Start of grant (anticipated)

### **Funding and opportunity details**

- **Opportunity type:** Invitation for expressions of interest to become the HHCC Ethiopia Anchor Institution.
- **Programme length:** The programme is intended to run from January 2027 to October 2031, subject to funding confirmation.
- **Total programme envelope:** Up to £2.4 million with approximately 80% intended for research, innovation and implementation grants delivered through the collaborative platform.

title: Research Manager for Nigeria, based in Abuja
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the PANDA Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT operates through three Initiatives: REACH, PANDA, and AGORA. This recruitment opportunity pertains to the PANDA Initiative.

PANDA is IMPACT’s lever on humanitarian aid responses which focusing on improving outcomes for beneficiaries through direct engagement with partners and their activities. Where REACH works through soft power and partnerships to affect systemic change, PANDA is direct action that allows us to ensure that system and its participants are trustworthy and delivering the most effective, efficient and equitable response possible. PANDA is praxis – it is how IMPACT manifests our vision of acting as a catalyst of change within the aid community to work through focused or multidimensional analysis of projects, programmes and policies to identify their results, strengths and weaknesses, and how they can be improved, then proposes or implements a concrete plan for improvement.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to support our team in Nigeria.**

**Department**: PANDA

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Location**: Abuja, Nigeria (with occasional stays in Dakar, Senegal)

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Nigeria is among the world's most critical hunger hotspots, where protracted conflict, displacement, economic pressures, and climate shocks are driving rapidly worsening humanitarian needs. In the Northeast, more than 8.8 million people require urgent assistance, including 4.9 million children, sustained displacement, protection risks, severe funding shortfalls, a growing nutrition emergency, and a cholera outbreak. Food insecurity is expected to reach record levels, with an estimated 34.7 million people nationwide projected to face Crisis-level food insecurity or worse by August 2026. Meanwhile, the Northwest faces a different but equally severe crisis driven by chronic poverty, banditry, communal violence, and recurrent flooding, which have displaced hundreds of thousands of people (800,000 IOM DTM R18), damaged livelihoods and farmland, and contributed to sharp declines in agricultural production. Together, these overlapping shocks are undermining resilience, increasing humanitarian needs, and threatening both current food security and future harvests.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. Historically, IMPACT Initiatives has been present in both the Northeast and Northwest of Nigeria. Thematically, across 2021 – 2023 IMPACT Initiatives fielded [Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7b6cde65/REACH_NGA_TOR_MSNA-Northwest_March-2022-1.pdf) (MSNAs), [Hard to Reach](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/0f980ce2/NGA-1809_Situation_Overview_Q1_Feb_Mar_2022.pdf) (H2R) assessments, [Area Based Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7cddc3c2/REACH_NGA_TOR_Rapid_Area-Based_Assessments_in_Areas_of_Return_February_2021.pdf) (ABA), [Rapid Overviews of Areas of Return](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/07db0c79/REACH_NGA_ToR_Rapid_Overview_Of_Areas_Of_Return_ROAR_-Feb-2022.pdf) (ROAR), [Thematic Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/9fa6a7cf/REACH_NGA_Brief_assessment-of-H2R-Gujba-and-Tarmua-LGA_April-2022.pdf) (TA), [Rapid Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/6b1d770d/REACH_NGA_Yobe_Floods_Brief.pdf) (RA), and [WASH Infrastructure Mapping](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/afb497ac/REACH_NGA_Factsheet_WASH-Infrastructure-Maiduguri_May-2021.pdf), while also playing a key role in Famine Monitoring, Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance, and the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI). Since 2026, IMPACT has reintroduced the MSNA, Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), JMMI and other thematic assessments in Nigeria in addition to the HARP TPM project which has been running since 2024.

## **PROJECT PRFILE**

The position is recruited for the Third-Party Monitoring (TPM) Project covering FCDOs Humanitarian and Resilience Programme (HARP) Facility. For this programme, IMPACT is in partnership with FACT Foundation. While in Nigeria, staff shall be hosted by FACT Foundation and for his or her mission, the Research Manager will fall under the direct responsibility and management of FACT and their delegates for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by FACT’s Security, HR, Administration, and Logistics rules and regulations, and in coordination with FACT, ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the management of the Country Representative, the Research Manager oversees the research activities and staff within the purview of the FCDO-funded Third Party Monitoring (TPM) Project. The Research Manager shall oversee and execute all research activities within the above-mentioned Project, meeting quarterly deliverables in a timely fashion while ensuring that the quality of research remains high. S/he will moreover liaise extensively with counterparts from Fact Foundation who are IMPACT’s partners in the Consortium for the Project, while supporting the Country Representative in stakeholder engagement with FCDO’s Implementing Partners.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager responsibilities include the following:

***Strategy development & implementation***

- With specific attention to the FCDO-funded TPM Project’s, and while supervised by the CR, the RM is to ensure that IMPACT has an up to date understanding of the country’s socio-economic situation, the impact of a crisis and the aid/humanitarian situation, as well as the humanitarian planning, coordination, response mechanism developments, and key humanitarian stakeholders.
- For the TPM Project, **develop and oversee the implementation of the project’s strategy**. Specifically, during the inception period, in conjunction with the CR, set out the project’s overall strategy, develop concomitant workplans for each staff member, and put in place the requisite structures for the staff members such that each individual has clarity as to how to work towards the common goal of completing deliverables in a timely manner and at a high standard, and ultimately supplying impact to FCDO and Implementing Partners at the outcome level.

## ***Research Planning***

- For the TPM Project, ensure that all the research is planned in line with the relevant project and programme objectives, as well as the Project and Country Strategy. This is to include:
- Ensure that all research complies with IMPACT’s HQ Research Department guidelines and standards.
- Ensure that al necessary Secondary Data Reviews are conducted and integrated into the research.
- Ensure that research ToRs are validated by HQ prior to the commencement of data collection.
- Ensure that research ToRs are understood by the team and updated accordingly.
- Keep track of progress and delays of all assigned assessments throughout the research cycle.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to include their two assessment and data staff in the research.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation to ensure that the portion of the research carried out by them is validated by IMPACT HQ.
- Where necessary, proactively support the team by conducting research (research design. ToRs, tool building, data management, data analysis, product drafting).
- While supported by the CR, conduct dissemination and stakeholder meetings with FCDO and Implementing Partners.

***Research Implementation***

- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to **ensure that the data is collected in the fashion and format that allows IMPACT to clean and analyse the data**.
- Ensure that all collected data is stored **in line with IMPACT’s Data Management Guidelines**, as well as with the data management plan Annex in the Research ToR.
- Ensure that data is revised and cleaned, **with all revisions recorded** as per IMPACT data management guidelines.
- **Oversee all the analyses of the collected data**, as stipulated in the Research ToRs.
- Ensure that data and its analysis **do not contain personal information** and are validated by IMPACT HQ, before sharing to external parties.
- Supervise and where necessary support the team with the analysis and drafting of the information products.
- **Review all products** before they are sent to the CR or IMPACT HQ for validation.
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ **before release to FCDO and Implementing Partners**.

***Team Management and Leadership***

- Ensure that all staff members understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities, as well as their reporting and validation duties to HQ.
- Ensure that all staff members have **clear and regularly updated ToRs, Workplans, and Key performance Indicators (KPIs)** against which their performance will be appraised.
- **Promote team building, productivity, and staff welfare**.
- Mentor and support the team **to build capacities, improve efficiency and performance**.
- **Promote the growth and development of staff** within the organisation, actively linking with HQ to provide feedback and support retention and internal mobility. Identify capacity building opportunities for growth, proactively provide high-performing staff with opportunities to surge (a short-term deployment to another mission) and develop pathways for junior staff to grow and move into management or specialist positions.
- **Ensure communication and linkages with HQ** are made immediately in case of the occurrence of an HR-related problem.

***Internal Coordination and Communication***

- Facilitate clear and seamless communication within the IMPACT TPM team across Senegal and Nigeria, as well as the FACT Foundation team in Nigeria.
- Ensure regular reporting to the CR.

***INFLUENCING - External Engagement***

- With the support from the CR, on a quarterly basis, engage with FCDO and the Implementing Partners to share findings and hold analysis and lessons learned workshops.
- Under the supervision of the CR, and where necessary, engage with the humanitarian response beyond the remit of the TPM Project.
- In conjunction with FCDO and Implementing Partners, support the CR in the dissemination of selected research with key stakeholders and coordination forums.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Academic** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Economics, Development Studies, or similar)
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Proven track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts
- **Familiarity aid system** Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings.
- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant working experience or proven progression within IMPACT.
- **Research skills:** Excellent research and analytical skills an asset. Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations is an asset.
- **Software skills:** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to multitask with tight deadlines, on numerous research cycles in complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the \[relevant\] region is desirable.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situational security training;
- Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Request For Proposal Kenya Call Centre
body:
Tiko is an organization that uses its digital platform called Tiko to motivate users primarily young women and adolescent girls to make positive choices. We use nudges like reminders, discounts, in person and digital follow-ups, and reward points to encourage our users to access and use healthy products and services. We also support them in becoming entrepreneurs and adding value to their economies. Tiko’s reward points can be used to redeem products and services at local shops, or as subsidies to cover the cost of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, removing the cost to access for the users, who are primarily 15–24-year-old adolescent girls and young women (AGYW).

Tiko has operations in the following countries either by having offices or by working through local partners in Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso, Nigeria and South Africa.

Tiko is looking to source a firm(s) to support through providing call center services in Kenya. We encourage local entities in the specific markets to apply. The firm/firms shall assist in being the recipient of beneficiary and partners queries (inbound calls) and carrying out interviews through the outbound calls to both validate uptake of services and obtain feedback on the quality of services provided.

**Scope of Work**

The call centre partner is expected to provide outbound call centre services oversee inbound client support on Phone with other possible channels being WhatsApp, SMS, Facebook and Instagram for a period of 1 year.

The required partner shall render call centre services that meet global standards which should include but not be limited to workspace for call center agents, with workstations that include a computer for each Agent, secure computer telephony integration systems, as well as sufficient reporting, training, staffing, supervision and quality control tools.

The details of the required services are as listed:

- Make outbound calls on behalf of Tiko.
- Capture data including voice logs resulting from outbound calls in a secure information management system.
- Provide raw data resulting from outbound calls at periods to be specified by Tiko.
- Oversee inbound client support services on Phone, SMS, WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
- Provide analyzed reports from data resulting from outbound calls inbound client support in the form of dashboards.

## General Requirements

- They will use their own premises to extend outbound call center services inUganda . The cost of premises & recurring costs related to connectivity & all kinds of utility services associated with setting up infrastructure and conducting the outbound calls will be borne by the call centre partner.
- They will recruit, train (provide language, operational and soft skills training) and maintain the necessary staff in order to run the centre at optimum capacity at their own cost.
- The Call centre partner is required to do all prior work of installing the required hardware & software, recruitment and training of agents, test dialing etc. in 30 days time from the date of award of contract to them and should start operations within this period.

**TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS**

The qualified firm should exhibit the following:

- Demonstration of experience and expertise of similar assignment with non-governmental

organizations;

- Providing an activity plan (project plan) of actions to achieve the objectives of the assignment, specifying budgeted hours, timelines and sequence for its consultancy procedure and level of staff to be assigned;
- Incorporating CV's of the proposed professional staff of the core management team proposed for the engagement and the authorized representative submitting the proposal. CVs should demonstrate relevant experience of dealing with Tax matters within organizations similar to Tiko;
- List of current and past clients where the bidder has conducted mystery client/shopper experience along with the name of the organization, contact person, designation, and a contact number, nature of services and length of the appointment for at least three (3) International non-governmental organizations.

**EVALUATION CRITERIA**

Proposals will be evaluated in two parts. The experience, technical proposal and financial quotation shall bear 70% of the total marks while the references and financial capacity shall bear 30% of the total marks.

- Proposals should make clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant, in respect of this particular SOW.
- Proposals must contain the details of the proposed approach to be adopted in order to deliver the service in accordance with the SOW.
- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the SOW.
- Proposal should clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical issues applicable to the country
- Must be a registered firm in the country where they seek to provide the services.

**Functionality evaluation criteria**

**Description**

**1. Experience, Skills and Ability of Service Provider**

- Past experience in similar work of this nature.
- Team member experience (accompanied by brief CV's).
- Ability of the bidder to fulfil Tiko’s requirements.

**Weight: 30**

**2. Technical Approach and Execution Plan**

- Proposals must contain the details of the **proposed approach** to be adopted in order to deliver the service in accordance with the SOW.

**Weight: 30**

**3. Financial quotation**

- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the **financial** **capacity** to meet the requirements of the TOR based on the previous value of similar works done e.g. by sharing copies of recent audited financial statements.

**Weight: 10**

**4. References**

- Did the bidder submit at least three relevant and **contactable clients** that were serviced in the past 36 months.

**Weight: 10**

**5. Capacity**

- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the **capacity** to meet the requirements of the SOW.

**Weight: 20**

**Total Weight: 100**

title: Associate Research Manager for Syria, based in Damascus
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for an Associate Research Manager to lead our Early Recovery, Markets, and Durable Solutions work in Syria.**

**Department**: IMPACT Syria mission

**Position**: Associate Research Manager Contract duration: 6 months

**Starting Date**: 1 December 2026

**Location**: Damascus, Syria.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

After more than a decade of conflict, economic collapse, and large-scale displacement, a regime change in December 2024 marked a new phase in Syria’s history. Conditions remain volatile, marked by regular armed clashes, prolonged socioeconomic and infrastructure challenges, and limited access to basic services such as healthcare, education, water, and electricity. While it is widely acknowledged that Syria needs large investments in development in order to recover from years of destruction and economic degradation, the humanitarian response also continues at scale due to high levels of need after fifteen years of conflict, exacerbated by the economic situation and poor basic services infrastructure.

Active in Syria since 2013, the IMPACT Syria mission has been producing key information products over the last decade to provide an evidence base for an informed humanitarian response. Activities have ranged from monthly humanitarian situation overviews and market monitoring, to displacement tracking, to supporting joint planning processes through the provision of multi-sectoral needs data, to providing evidence for durable solutions via area-based assessments.

## **POSITION PROFILE**

The Associate Research Manager will be responsible for leading research workstreams around Area-Based Assessments in support of Durable Solutions, market monitoring in support of economic analysis and recovery, and other related thematic assessments and analyses. Under the supervision of the Senior Research Manager (SRM), the ARM will lead on the development and timely implementation of the team’s strategy and research cycles.

This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Associate Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, sector stakeholder, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products, as well as support on data collection logistics, reporting, and financial planning.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Associate Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, direct management of two team members, including recruitment, capacity building and staff career management, with potential for growing the team as funding allows.
- In coordination with the SRM, development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Day-to-day management of team members, including the development of work plans and performance indicators.

***PROJECT/RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure all assessments and analysis are planned and implemented in a structured and coherent manner, in line with relevant project and strategic objectives, and with global REACH guidelines;
- Oversee all of the team’s research cycles, including reviewing ToRs, methodology notes, tools, products and dissemination strategies.
- Ensure the writing and production of timely, accurate and analytically rigorous outputs;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning;
- Monitor output achievement and ensure timely completion of the project.
- Actively advocate for the improving of analysis within REACH products, and using common methodologies, tools and analysis frameworks across workstreams where relevant.

***GRANTS MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, manage grant components, including conceptualisation of new projects, drafting proposals, regular reporting, and M&E. Lead in identifying funding opportunities and strategic positioning for the team.
- Support the SRM / Country Representative in the financial management of all grants covering the team’s projects, including oversight of budget and expenditure with regards to data collection.
- Ensure that contractual obligations are met at a high-quality standard in terms of programs deliverables.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- In coordination with the SRM and Country Representative and where relevant, represent REACH with donors, partners, and the wider response community in Syria, particularly with the Solutions Working Group, Data for Solutions Working Group, and Cash Working Group.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- Work with key sectors and partner organizations and working groups to understand the various relevant information gaps within Syria and identify how REACH can fill these gaps.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Research Unit’s strategy, ensuring workstream research strategies are integrated within the wider strategy.
- In coordination with the SRM, develop and implement dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of the team’s research cycles.
- Engagement with HQ on research and/or coordination and provide support to relevant IMPACT Global Community of Practices (CoPs).
- The Associate Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant and progressive working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as program management, evaluation and assessments.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required. Solid understanding of IMPACT Research Quality Assurance standards also required.
- **Understanding of aid system** Good understanding of the response system and key actors, as well as of the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated progressive staff management skills, including remote management and inspirational leadership.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with displacement, durable solutions, area-based and movement-related research highly desirable.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region is desirable but not decisive.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and external engagement with donors and other high-level stakeholders.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Request For Proposal Uganda Call Centre
body:
Tiko is a global non-profit that motivates young people to make positive choices using innovative tech, real-time data, and behavioural insights. Through our digital platform, Tiko, and our local ecosystem of partners, we connect Tiko members to existing local service providers to meet their health and wellness needs. As part of this ecosystem, Tiko works with Community-Based Organisations (CBOs) to manage a network of mobilisers, also known as Tiko Pros, who engage with youth in their communities, inform them about Tiko, enrol them to the Tiko platform, refer them for sexual and reproductive (SRH) and HIV-related services at participating public and private clinics and pharmacies. Mobilisers are also expected to follow up with adolescents to gauge their experience, offer support and encourage them to return for services, if required, to ensure consistent positive healthy behaviour.

**Scope of Work**

The call centre partner is expected to provide outbound call centre services and oversee inbound client support on the Phone with other possible channels being WhatsApp, SMS, Facebook and Instagram for a period of 1 year.

The required partner shall render call centre services that meet global standards which should include but not be limited to workspace for call centre agents, with workstations that include a computer for each Agent, secure computer telephony integration systems, as well as sufficient reporting, training, staffing, supervision and quality control tools.

**The details of the required services are as listed:**

- Provide a toll-free number which will give clients the opportunity to call in at their convenience and also receive callbacks for more support;
- Provide inbound and outbound user support by committing counselors and a nurse who in addition to English will attend to client issues in both Luganda and Lugbara;
- Conduct outbound insight calls (including risk calls) and survey a sample of users and/or platform actors regularly as advised by the company to generate insights that feed into programme implementation which will allow improvements;
- Capture data including voice logs resulting from outbound calls in a secure information management system;
- Provide raw data generated from outbound calls to the Company on Friday of each week;
- Oversee inbound client support services through the toll-free number (SMS and phone calls) and interactions through Tiko Uganda Facebook;
- Provide weekly analyzed reports from data resulting from inbound and outbound calls. Reports will be provided in the form of analysed text including screenshots and will include data points such as:

1. Number of daily inbound and outbound calls made on a weekly/monthly basis reported by age and gender of clients;
2. Number of successful and unsuccessful calls made for the above time periods;
3. Reports on interactions made with clients through the Facebook page;
4. The topic of conversation with the clients;
5. Whether a client was referred for a service (and where);
6. a summary of topics which clients have called to discuss

The Company will update the requirements of the report based on recognised program needs as implementation is ongoing. The Contractor may also provide suggestions on information to be collected from the calls made.

**GENERAL REQUIREMENTS**

- They will use their own premises to extend outbound call centre services in Uganda. The cost of premises & recurring costs related to connectivity & all kinds of utility services associated with setting up infrastructure and conducting the outbound calls will be borne by the call centre partner.
- They will recruit, train (provide language, operational and soft skills training) and maintain the necessary staff in order to run the centre at optimum capacity at their own cost.
- The Call centre partner is required to do all prior work of installing the required hardware & software, recruitment and training of agents, test dialling etc. in 30 days' time from the date of award of contract to them and should start operations within this period.

**DELIVERABLES**

- Provide a Toll-free number for the Tiko program in Uganda.
- Recruit, train (provide language, operational and soft skills training) and maintain the necessary staff in order to perform services required including at least 2 dedicated counsellors (1 English speaking, and 1 Luganda speaking) for the Tiko Uganda project.
- Set up the infrastructure required for services as per this contract within 15 days of completing the contract signing.

Tiko will share the relevant templates for data collection which will be through a survey software tool, KoboToolbox, where all call results will be submitted to. Contacts to be called will be shared on a daily basis (or alternate days) and submissions made in real-time to the software tool.

All contacts shared in the month need to have been contacted and submitted to KoboToolbox by the 5th of the following month for analysis.

**TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS**

The qualified firm should exhibit the following:

- Demonstration of experience and expertise of similar assignment with non-governmental

organizations;

- Providing an activity plan (project plan) of actions to achieve the objectives of the assignment, specifying budgeted hours, timelines and sequence for its consultancy procedure and level of staff to be assigned;
- Incorporating CV's of the proposed professional staff of the core management team proposed for the engagement and the authorized representative submitting the proposal. CVs should demonstrate relevant experience of dealing with Tax matters within organizations similar to Tiko;
- List of current and past clients where the bidder has conducted mystery client/shopper experience along with the name of the organization, contact person, designation, and a contact number, nature of services and length of the appointment for at least three (3) International non-governmental organizations.

**EVALUATION CRITERIA**

Proposals will be evaluated in two parts. The experience, technical proposal and financial quotation shall bear 70% of the total marks while the references and financial capacity shall bear 30% of the total marks.

- Proposals should make clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant, in respect of this particular SOW.
- Proposals must contain the details of the proposed approach to be adopted in order to deliver the service in accordance with the SOW.
- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the SOW.
- Proposal should clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical issues applicable to the country
- Must be a registered firm in the country where they seek to provide the services.

**Functionality evaluation criteria**

**Description**

**1.Experience, Skills and Ability of Service Provider**

- Past experience in similar work of this nature.
- Team member experience (accompanied by brief CV's).
- Ability of the bidder to fulfil Tiko’s requirements.

**Weight: 30**

**2. Technical Approach and Execution Plan**

- Proposals must contain the details of the **proposed approach** to be adopted in order to deliver the service in accordance with the SOW.

**Weight: 30**

**3. Financial quotation**

- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the **financial** **capacity** to meet the requirements of the TOR based on the previous value of similar works done e.g. by sharing copies of recent audited financial statements.

**Weight: 10**

**4. References**

- Did the bidder submit at least three relevant and **contactable clients** that were serviced in the past 36 months.

**Weight: 10**

**5. Capacity**

- Proposals should clearly indicate whether or not bid participants have the **capacity** to meet the requirements of the SOW.

**Weight: 20**

title: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala
body:
**BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Data Analyst or Data Specialist, depending on profile, to work with our team in Ethiopia.**

**Position:** Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist (depending on profile)

**Contract duration**: 5 months

**Location**: Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country.

## **JOB PROFILE**

The Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist position is based in Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa. The position is fully dedicated to the Ethiopia mission and will report directly to the Deputy Country Representative. The postholder will lead the mission’s data team, coordinating its work across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units in close collaboration with Research Managers, the GIS Specialist and relevant HQ technical teams.

The postholder will provide technical leadership and backstopping throughout the research cycle, from methodology and sampling design to data collection, cleaning, analysis, validation and dissemination. The role is responsible for coordinating data officers and interns, agreeing priorities and resource needs with Research Managers, maintaining reusable analysis systems, and ensuring compliance with IMPACT research standards and data protection requirements. The appointment level will depend on the selected candidate’s experience and technical skills; both profiles will carry responsibility for leading the data team.

During the assignment, the Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist will be hosted by Acted, IMPACT's global partner, and will be under the responsibility of its delegates for all administrative, security, logistics and financial matters. The postholder will fully comply with Acted and IMPACT rules and procedures, including those relating to data protection and information security.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Planning and coordination:** Estimate deadlines and resource requirements for each research cycle across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units. Coordinate team members’ workloads, agree data team priorities with Research Managers, and flag risks, capacity gaps and delays early, in writing, to the relevant Research Managers and direct manager.
- **Research design:** Support assessment teams in designing methodologies, sampling strategies (including sample size calculations and survey weighting), data analysis plans and data collection tools, in line with IMPACT research standards.
- **Data collection and cleaning:** Oversee the review, testing and deployment of XLSForms on IMPACT’s Kobo server, data checks during collection, and data cleaning in line with IMPACT’s Data Cleaning Minimum Standards. Where relevant, train enumerators and partner staff on data checks and cleaning.
- **Analysis systems:** Maintain and develop the mission’s R-based cleaning and analysis workflows, including IMPACT R packages, templates and Shiny applications, under version control and with up-to-date documentation so that they can be reused across research cycles.
- **Information products:** Review country-level information products and dissemination strategies to maximise the use of findings, in accordance with IMPACT research standards and in close coordination with the direct manager.
- **Data quality:** Improve data quality and monitoring at country level, including resolving discrepancies, keeping geospatial and administrative reference data up to date in coordination with GIS colleagues, and ensuring collected data is correctly georeferenced.
- **Data protection:** Ensure compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOP on personally identifiable information in all research cycles. This includes anonymisation and disclosure-risk checks before any dataset is shared, secure transfer, storage and deletion of data, and compliance with data-sharing or data processing agreements with partners.
- **Capacity building:** Lead the development and implementation of an ongoing capacity-building plan for country data officers and interns, with support from relevant technical colleagues and HQ teams. Provide training, mentoring and regular feedback on data cleaning, analysis and tools, and coordinate with Research Managers on staff development and performance.
- **Partner engagement:** At the request of the line manager, support partners on data processing, data sharing and the use of findings, and represent IMPACT on data matters in relevant coordination forums.

***DELIVERABLES***

- Lead weekly data team meetings, maintain a shared task tracker with clear responsibilities and agreed timelines, and follow up on progress and outstanding actions.
- Provide technical guidance to data officers and interns on cleaning, analysis and troubleshooting, implement and track the capacity-building plan, and provide input to their performance appraisals in coordination with Research Managers.
- Regularly liaise with project focal points and Research Managers to monitor deadlines and resource needs, anticipate delays, and communicate risks and agreed corrective actions in writing.
- Conduct internal technical validation of all research cycles, including review of sampling, data collection tools, cleaning and analysis outputs, to ensure alignment with IMPACT/HQ guidelines before submission to HQ for validation.
- Ensure regular maintenance of all mission dashboards, including Power BI and Shiny, and contribute to the design and development of new dashboards when required.
- Keep documentation, including READMEs, SOPs and decision logs, up to date for all workflows and dashboards maintained by the data team, with code under version control and clear maintenance responsibilities.
- For every dataset shared outside IMPACT, document the anonymisation applied, disclosure-risk checks and transfer, in line with the relevant agreement and applicable IMPACT procedures.

## **REQUIRED SKILLSET**

- At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in data management and analysis, preferably in humanitarian settings.
- A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as statistics, data science or social sciences, is preferred.
- Fluency in English is required.
- Excellent communication and data visualisation skills.
- Strong skills in R and in data cleaning and survey analysis workflows; familiarity with IMPACT’s R packages is an asset.
- Proven skills in Power BI and R Shiny.
- Experience with KoboToolbox or ODK and XLSForm design.
- Sound knowledge of sampling methods, sample size calculations and survey weighting.
- Experience with Git/GitHub; GIS skills in QGIS or ArcGIS are an asset.
- Knowledge of humanitarian data protection practice, including anonymisation of microdata and disclosure-risk assessment.
- Experience supervising or mentoring data staff, including remotely.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities across many research cycles, at times under tight deadlines.
- Strong ability to work independently in support of colleagues and partners.
- Ability to work in an intercultural environment.
- Previous experience in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa is highly preferred.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Rehabilitation Technical Officer - Darfur
Security Advisory – Journalist protection - West Asia (repost)
body:
MiCT is calling for proposals for freelance Security Advisory services in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027” in West Asia, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. This will be a service contract, running from November 2026 - June 2027. MiCT invites interested and qualified people and /or organisations to submit proposals by 1.11.2026.

**Introducing MiCT:**

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

**About the Project:**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

**Description of the role:**

To support the Fellows from West Asia, MiCT is looking to provide support and guidance on security matters through trainings, risk assessments, security briefings and one-on-one mentorship sessions. The focus areas will include, but are not limited to, advanced digital security, identifying, mitigating and responding to digital threats, preventive and responsive protection mechanisms, identifying digital attacks, secure communication, device and data protection, risk mitigation strategies, and individualized support to Fellows facing security threats. The contract will run from November 2026 until June 2027. Provision of all deliverables will be needs based - with no minimum guaranteed. Maximum contractual value will be up to 8 security briefings, 45 individualised risk assessments, 60 hours of mentoring and 6 trainings.

The risk assessments should give a comprehensive overview of the person’s security situation, covering digital and/or physical security as required, and providing concrete and prioritised next steps. Any additional mentoring sessions will be agreed upon in writing following the finalisation of the needs assessment.

**Application Requirements**

Successful applicants should be able to provide proof of the following:

- Minimum of 5 years of experience in security risk management in West Asia.
- Strong understanding of the media and security landscape in West Asia.
- Experience working with journalists in crisis and conflict contexts.
- Proven experience in conducting individual risk assessments and crisis management.
- Ability to develop and deliver security training and one-on-one consultancy.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to work with diverse teams.
- Fluency in Arabic is a must. Fluency in English is preferred.
- Flexibility and teamwork.

title: Terms of Reference (ToR): Request for Proposals - Job Grading, Role Clarity and Salary Structure Review
body:
**About CIVICUS**

CIVICUS is a global civil society alliance working to strengthen citizen action and civil society around the world. Our Secretariat has approximately 85 colleagues and registered hubs in South Africa, Geneva and New York. Colleagues work across different countries, and their locations may change over time.

**Background and purpose**

CIVICUS currently operates a common global salary scale, rather than separate country salary scales. We provide location allowances for designated positions that the organisation requires to be based in New York or Geneva. Subject to applicable requirements and organisational arrangements, colleagues may also relocate to countries where they have, or obtain, the right to live and work. This mobility is an important feature of our operating context. The assignment is not intended to commission a separate salary scale for every country where a colleague happens to be based as staff location is fluid.

In 2021, CIVICUS reviewed job descriptions and grading using the Paterson approach. A separate review of the broad-banded salary structure sought to address historical anomalies, and a revised structure was implemented in 2022. We would now welcome an independent assessment of the continued suitability of our grading, role descriptions and remuneration arrangements, including how they compare with relevant organisations in the sector.

We have not determined what the findings or preferred approach should be. We are seeking consultants who can bring independent judgement, relevant evidence and practical options for consideration.

**Objectives and scope**

Working with the HR team and relevant stakeholders, the consultants will:

- Review the existing job grading framework and assess the consistency of role levels, responsibilities and accountabilities.
- Consider the clarity and consistency of job descriptions, including expected deliverables, and recommend a practical approach to strengthening them.
- Undertake proportionate salary benchmarking against relevant international civil society, NGO or comparable mission-driven organisations, explaining the choice of comparators and limitations of the data.
- Assess internal equity, external competitiveness, affordability and the practical implications of different remuneration approaches in a mobile, globally dispersed workforce.
- Present evidence-based findings and feasible options, with their advantages, risks, indicative cost implications and implementation considerations.

**Expected deliverables**

1. Brief inception plan confirming methodology, consultations, information requirements and benchmarking approach.
2. A concise assessment of job grading, job-description consistency, and internal equity, with recommended principles or templates to promote fairness, transparency, and consistency in future use.
3. A salary benchmarking and structure review, clearly identifying sources, assumptions and any data gaps.
4. Equity and Fairness Assessment: An assessment of equity considerations within the proposed grading and salary structure, with recommendations appropriate to CIVICUS' global operating context.
5. A final report and presentation setting out findings, options, recommendations and a proportionate implementation roadmap.

**Duration and budget**

The assignment is expected to be undertaken over a period of 40 working days, with a maximum available budget of US$15,000. Consultants are invited to propose a realistic workplan and indicate what can be delivered within this envelope. Please specify whether fees, taxes and any external salary-data costs are included.

**Consultant experience**

We welcome proposals from specialist consultants or teams with demonstrated experience in job evaluation, remuneration design and benchmarking for international NGOs, civil society organisations or similarly distributed workforces. Access to credible comparator data, sound analytical skills and the ability to communicate clearly with diverse stakeholders will be important. Physical presence in a specific location is not required. The assignment will be conducted remotely with no travel.

body:

**ROLE PURPOSE:**   
The key purpose of this post is to is to ensure that the IT strategy and vision  
aligned, tuned up and supporting Save the Children strategy and vision, manage and ensure  
efficient and effective IT and Communications systems and applications are in place to facilitate the CO  
operations and keep staff informed through timely and pertinent communications, providing the IT  
technology infrastructures and contributing to organizational policy regarding quality standards  
and strategic planning.  
**SCOPE OF ROLE:**   
Reports to: SCO Finance & IT Director   
Staff directly reporting to this post: 3

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

Support the delivery of effective Programmes, in both development and humanitarian contexts, by:

• Roll Out all new global IT policies and/or initiatives as requested by the Global Team.  
• Coordination with regional and global teams to provide and implement newest technologies and services

title: Partnerships Officer
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Partnerships Officer**.

## **About the job**

Under the direct line management of the Area Manager - Tripoli and technical supervision of the Partnerships Coordinator - ALT, the Partnerships Officer supports the implementation of DRC’s partnership approach across the Algeria, Libya and Tunisia (ALT) country operation. The role works closely with relevant sector teams, MEAL and support services focal points, serving as a central coordination point between partners and DRC programme, MEAL and support-service teams. The role promotes equitable, accountable and locally led partnerships while helping ensure quality, compliance, learning and timely delivery of partner-implemented activities. The role supports the full partnership cycle, from partner mapping and assessment through agreement development, implementation monitoring, capacity strengthening, review and closure.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**1. PARTNERSHIP MAPPING AND ENGAGEMENT**

- Support regular mapping of national and local civil society organisations, networks and other potential partners across ALT, based on programme priorities and geographic needs.
- Maintain up-to-date partner profiles, contact lists and partnership pipeline information.
- Support initial engagement with prospective partners and contribute to transparent, inclusive partner identification and selection processes.
- Contribute partnership inputs to country strategies, programme design, proposals, donor engagement and operational planning.
- Monitor relevant contextual, policy and civil society developments that may affect partnerships and flag key issues to the line manager and technical supervisor.

**2. PARTNERSHIP CYCLE MANAGEMENT**

- Support organisational assessments, due diligence, risk reviews and partner selection in coordination with programme, finance, supply chain, HR, safeguarding and compliance colleagues.
- Support the preparation, review and amendment of partnership agreements, MoUs, budgets, workplans, procurement plans and reporting schedules.
- Track partner deliverables, activities, expenditure, risks and agreed follow-up actions, and maintain a consolidated overview of partnership status across ALT.
- Lead and Support regular partnership review meetings, field monitoring visits and timely documentation of decisions and action points.
- Support orderly partnership closure, including final reports, asset and documentation follow-up, learning reviews and closure checklists.

**3. PARTNER SUPPORT AND CAPACITY STRENGTHENING**

- Coordinate partner support plans based on jointly identified priorities, ensuring that capacity strengthening is practical, demand-led and linked to partnership objectives.
- Connect partners with relevant DRC technical and support-service focal points and follow up on agreed training, coaching and systems support.
- Support peer learning, exchange and dialogue among partners across Algeria, Libya and Tunisia.
- Support the implementation of DRC ALT’s localisation agenda, and help partners understand and apply DRC’s partnership tools, templates and minimum standards.
- Promote equitable partnership practices, mutual accountability, safeguarding, participation and respect for partner leadership and identity.

**4. MONITORING, COMPLIANCE AND DOCUMENTATION**

- Work with programme and MEAL teams to follow partner-implemented results, quality, accountability to affected populations and learning.
- Support partners to use DRC reporting templates and provide first-line review of partner narrative and financial reports before submission to the relevant technical and finance teams.
- Support the collection and follow-up of partner and community feedback related to partner-implemented activities, in coordination with MEAL.
- Liaise with Finance, Supply Chain, HR and other support teams to resolve operational bottlenecks and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Maintain complete, accurate and accessible partnership files, including signed agreements and MoUs on the partnership SharePoint and related trackers, in line with DRC procedures, donor requirements and data-protection standards.
- Promptly report compliance concerns, safeguarding issues, irregularities or incidents through established DRC channels.
- Prepare concise partnership updates, portfolio overviews and management information for internal planning and reporting.

**5. COORDINATION AND REPRESENTATION**

- Coordinate closely with programme and project managers, technical coordinators, MEAL and support-service teams across ALT.
- Participate in relevant external meetings, partner events and field visits when requested, and present DRC’s partnership approach and ALT portfolio accurately.
- Support the organisation of partnership events, trainings and field visits for partners, donors and visitors, in coordination with support-service teams, including related procurement requests where needed.
- Contribute to organisational learning and continuous improvement of partnership tools, processes and ways of working.

**Note:** This job description remains flexible to respond to additional tasks or changes identified by the line manager and/or technical supervisor.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2 years of relevant experience in the fields of working for international or national humanitarian organizations in complex settings.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

- Excellent knowledge of authorities’ structures, reporting lines, and areas of responsibilities.
- Demonstrated experience in partner capacity assessment and capacity strengthening, including training, coaching and follow-up of support plans
- Good knowledge of project cycle management; knowledge of due diligence, donor compliance and partnership agreement requirements is an asset
- Previous working experience with DRC is a strong asset
- Proven networking experience
- Ability to properly communicate with different kind of audiences (partners, authorities, humanitarian stakeholders, etc.)
- Ability to work flexibly in a diverse team
- Strong skills in collecting and analyzing information, and in maintaining trackers and partnership files (Excel or similar tools)
- Motivated, dynamic; able and willing to take initiative
- Time and work management abilities as well as autonomy
- Willing and able to travel nationwide and abroad (including to those considered as hardship duty stations) with at least 70-80% of their working time

title: International Consultant CC-2026-27
body:
Position Title: **International Consultant**

Duty Station: **Yerevan, Armenia**

Classification: **Consultancy**

Type of Appointment: **6 months**

Estimated Start Date: **As soon as possible**

Closing Date: **17 November, 2026**

*Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.*

***Context:***

The Scientific and Educational Centre of the National Security Service of the Republic of Armenia (NSS) is developing a six-month secondary vocational (professional) training program for contract servicemen of the Border Guard Troops who will serve at the green border and border outposts. The objective is to establish a modern, competency-based curriculum aligned with European border management standards and contemporary border security requirements, with a particular focus on the operational duties, challenges, and competencies required for effective service at green border sections and border outposts.

The purpose of this consultancy is to support the development of a comprehensive six-month vocational training curriculum for contract border guards of the NSS Border Guard Troops, specifically preparing personnel for assignments at the green border and border outposts. The curriculum will draw upon EU Integrated Border Management (IBM) principles, FRONTEX Common Core Curricula, and relevant international standards and best practices, while emphasizing practical skills, operational readiness, surveillance, border patrolling, detection, and response capabilities required in green border and border outpost environments.

***Background of the activity:***

The Project is implemented in Armenia to further strengthen the capacities of the national authorities to tackle cross-border organized crime and independent border management capacities. The primary national partners benefiting from its outcomes are the National Security Service of the Republic of Armenia (NSS) and its Border Guard Troops (BGT). The Project will build on the results achieved in recent years and will further advance the alignment of the border guard training/ educational system and standards with European and international best practices, enhance capacity to autonomously manage borders through enhanced secondary inspection as well as capacity to detect and counter irregular travellers, including terrorists and serious criminals through setting up Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) data.

***Core Functions / Responsibilities:***

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office and direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the International Consultant shall deliver the following outputs:

**Inception and Needs Assessment**

- Review existing NSS training documentation, legal framework, and operational requirements.
- Conduct consultations with NSS leadership, Border Guard Troops command, instructors, and relevant stakeholders.
- Identify training needs and competency gaps.
- Prepare an Inception Report outlining methodology, work plan, and curriculum development approach.

**Competency Framework Development**

- Define occupational profile(s) for contract border guards.
- Develop learning outcomes and competencies required for operational deployment.
- Align competencies with EU IBM principles and relevant FRONTEX standards where applicable.

**Curriculum Design**

- Develop a complete six-month training curriculum, including:
- Curriculum structure and sequencing.
- Modules and subjects.
- Learning outcomes for each module.
- Recommended contact hours.
- Theory/practical training ratio.
- Training methods.
- Required training facilities and equipment.
- Evaluation and assessment framework.

**Development of Training Materials Framework**

- Propose outlines for lesson plans.
- Recommend practical exercises and simulation-based learning scenarios.
- Provide guidance on assessment tools and examination procedures.

**Capacity Building of NSS Instructors**

- Develop a capacity-building plan for instructors responsible for delivering the new curriculum.
- Design and conduct a Training of Trainers (ToT) program.
- Introduce competency-based training methodologies, practical and simulation-based learning approaches, and learner assessment techniques.
- Provide mentoring and guidance on curriculum implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
- Recommend mechanisms for continuous professional development of instructors.

**Validation and Finalization**

- Facilitate a curriculum validation workshop with NSS representatives.
- Incorporate comments and recommendations.
- Submit the final curriculum package.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- All deliverables submitted according to the agreed timeline.
- All reports and curriculum documents accepted without requiring substantial revision.
- Curriculum demonstrates alignment with competency-based vocational education principles and relevant international border management standards.
- NSS stakeholders express satisfaction with the relevance and usability of the curriculum and training framework.
- At least 80% of workshop and ToT participants report increased confidence in implementing the new curriculum.
- Final curriculum approved for piloting and/or institutional adoption by the NSS Border Guard Troops.

***Required Qualifications and Experience***

**Education**

- Advanced university degree in border management, security studies, military sciences, law enforcement, education, public administration, or related field.

**Experience and Skills**

- Minimum 10 years of professional experience in border management, border guard training, or security sector education.
- Demonstrated experience in curriculum development for border guard, law enforcement, military, or security institutions.
- Experience working with FRONTEX Common Core Curricula and EU Integrated Border Management concepts.
- Previous experience with border guard training reform, competency-based curriculum development, or capacity-building initiatives in Armenia, the South Caucasus region, Eastern Partnership countries, or other relevant partner countries is highly desirable.
- Experience facilitating stakeholder consultations and training workshops.

**Skills**

- Design and deliver border management training programs
- Develop competency-based curricula and learning materials
- Facilitate training workshops and Training-of-Trainers (ToT) sessions
- Assess and strengthen institutional training capacities
- Coordinate and engage stakeholders throughout project implementation

**Languages**

For this consultancy, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Proficiency in Armenian or Russian would be beneficial.

**Travel** **required**

Yes.

**Required Competencies**

**Values**

- ***Inclusion and respect for diversity:*** respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- ***Integrity and transparency:*** maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- ***Professionalism:*** demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- ***Courage:*** demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- ***Empathy:*** shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators *level 1*

- ***Teamwork:*** develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- ***Delivering results:*** produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- ***Managing and sharing knowledge:*** continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- ***Accountability:*** takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- ***Communication:*** encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

***Other***

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the [IOM e-Recruitment](https://fa-evlj-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1) system (for internal candidates link [here](https://fa-evlj-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/fscmUI/redwood/internalmobility)). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)
