- Support the Team Coordinator in income forecasting and quarterly analysis of results.

*Others*

- Participate in the Community of Practice for Individual Major Donors of MSF in particular with other German-speaking sections.
- Work proactively on projects as needed in the Unit, upon request by her/his supervisor.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing,
- Communications, Political Science, International
- Relations or other relevant areas

*Experience*

- First professional experience in the non-profit sector or in the fields of marketing/sales/communication or client relationship management

*Languages*

- German mother tongue & very good English
- French and Italian an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Proven excellent writing skills (drafting and editing)
- Excellent in oral public presentations
- Strong knowledge of the Windows environment (Word, Excel, Power Point) and tech-savvy
- Strong Analytical skills
- Knowledge of the humanitarian and development sector in Switzerland.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Service oriented
- Dynamic, proactive and autonomous
- Rigorous and good organizational skills
- Empathic, enthusiastic, optimistic
- Discretion
- Team spirit.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Zurich, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: As soon as possible
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 80’856.- to CHF 97’224.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

title: Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator - BU Support
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
- The Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator will also perform any other duties as assigned by the manager.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong communication skills.
- Analytical Skills: Ability to apply logical thinking and problem-solving techniques to break down complex issues and reach sound conclusions.
- Data Analysis Skills: Proven ability to collect, analyze, and interpret large datasets to inform decision-making. Advanced proficiency in data manipulation and visualization tools, including expertise in Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, and Array formulas).
- Solid stakeholder management skills
- Strong working knowledge of process improvement tools and methodologies, DMAIC, 5Whys
- Supply chain risk management skills
- Commercial contracting skills
- Strategic sourcing skills
- Supplier relationship management skills
- Commercial negotiation skills
- Minimum 3 years of work experience in a demanding professional environment.
- Bachelor's degree in procurement, project management, business strategy, or related discipline. Candidates with higher diploma and extensive relevant experience may also qualify.
- Professional qualification e.g CIPS, CILT preferred
- Familiarity with procurement models, sourcing frameworks, and PR-PO systems such as Odoo or Power BI
- Language: Fluent in English and Kiswahili preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Grants officer (F/M) - Afghanistan
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing grants management, donor compliance, resource mobilization, and partnership and donor engagement for MdM in Afghanistan. In addition, you will be responsible for the mission's communication and will promote visibility on MdM works, particularly when it comes to ensuring implementation of donors’ communication requirements.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Proposal management:**

- Lead and coordinate concept notes and proposals
- Write the non-technical sections (context, needs analysis, cross-cutting)
- Ensure coherence between narrative, logframe and budget as well as alignment with MdM strategy and donor requirements

**Reporting:**

- Track all active grants and deadlines
- Coordinate donor and internal reports (including the monthly situation report)
- Ensure quality and consistency between programmatic and financial information

**Donor engagement:**

- Maintain donor mapping and a database of calls for proposals
- Train teams on donor rules, prepare meetings and briefing materials for the general coordinator
- Support audits and evaluations

**Partnerships:**

- Support the development of MoUs and partnership agreements
- Coordinate due diligence
- Manage collaboration with partners, including in a consortium

**Communication:**

- Develop communication products (factsheets, country profiles, success stories)
- Contribute to the visibility strategy, train staff on guidelines
- Collect field content, and manage social media in line with MdM and donor guidelines

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the program officer at HQ, the Institutional Funding Unit, the technical coordinators, the support coordinators, the MEAL team, and the communication teams at HQ and in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following or related field: Development, International Relations, Humanitarian Management
- Have at least two years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in coordinating and preparing strong narrative and financial reports for a variety of donors
- Have a strong understanding of donor compliance, especially for ECHO/INTPA, FCDO, BHA, GFFO
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in multi-donors’ budgets
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 069 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: National Recovery & Resource Mobilization Manager
source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
body:
**Job duties and responsibilities**

*Strategic Government Engagement and Partnerships*  
• Build and maintain strategic relationships with key government institutions involved in recovery and ‎reconstruction of joint opportunities. ‎  
• Develop and maintain a stakeholder map of government actors, recovery institutions, and public sector ‎partners relevant to the URCS recovery priorities. ‎  
• Identify opportunities for URCS engagement within national, regional, and local recovery programmes and ‎initiatives. ‎  
• Support URCS leadership in high-level engagement with government counterparts and recovery stakeholders.‎  
• Represent URCS in recovery-related coordination platforms, consultations, and working groups. ‎  
• Advise leadership on government engagement priorities, risks, and emerging opportunities.‎

*Recovery Resource Mobilization Opportunities ‎*  
• Identify funding, partnership, and co-financing opportunities for URCS recovery programmes. ‎  
• Develop relationships with donors, development partners, financial institutions, and private sector actors. ‎  
• Support the development of funding proposals, concept notes, and partnership opportunities. ‎  
• Advise teams on resource mobilization strategies and donor positioning.‎

*Alignment of URCS Programmes with National Recovery Priorities*  
• Align URCS recovery programmes with national, regional, and local recovery priorities. ‎  
• Identify opportunities to position URCS programmes within government-led recovery efforts. ‎  
• Support programme teams to incorporate government priorities into project design and implementation. ‎  
• Facilitate engagement with government stakeholders during programme development

I*nternal Coordination and Advisory Support*  
• Coordinate closely with programme teams, branch development and branch networks, and relevant ‎counterparts to advance recovery opportunities. ‎  
• Provide technical advice on government engagement, partnerships, and resource mobilization. ‎  
• Support a coordinated organizational approach to recovery stakeholder engagement. ‎  
• Strengthening institutional capacity in recovery partnership development and positioning.‎

*Policy Analysis, Intelligence, and Reporting*  
• Monitor recovery policies, plans, funding opportunities, and stakeholder developments. ‎  
• Analyse opportunities and risks relevant to URCS recovery objectives. ‎  
• Prepare briefings, stakeholder analyses, and recommendations for management. ‎  
• Provide regular reporting on partnerships, resource mobilization, and government engagement.‎

*Branch and Local Recovery Engagement*  
• Support branches in identifying/ or pitching for local recovery partnership and funding opportunities. ‎  
• As needed, facilitate connections between branches, local authorities, and other recovery stakeholders. ‎  
• Promote locally driven recovery initiatives aligned with national priorities. ‎  
• Share good practices and lessons learned across the URCS network.‎

Duties applicable to all staff  
‎1.‎ Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals. ‎  
‎2.‎ Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.‎  
‎3.‎ Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.‎

Education

**Required**

- Advanced university degree in Public Administration, Public Policy, Economics, ‎Development Studies, International Relations, Political Science or another relevant ‎field.

**Preferred** ‎

- Specialized training or professional certification in resource mobilization, public ‎investment, infrastructure development, donor relations, or partnership management ‎is considered an advantage. ‎
- Additional training in stakeholder engagement, strategic partnerships, programme ‎development, financing mechanisms, or grant management would be considered an ‎asset.‎

Experience

**Required**

- Minimum 7-10 years of professional experience in recovery, reconstruction, ‎development cooperation, public sector engagement, resource mobilization, ‎programme development, or a related field.‎
- Demonstrated experience working with government institutions, particularly those ‎involved in recovery, reconstruction, regional development, infrastructure, social ‎policy, or public investment processes. (experience with Ukrainian government is ‎advantage)‎
- Proven track record of developing strategic partnerships and mobilizing resources ‎from government, donors, development finance, private sector, or other financing ‎sources. ‎
- Experience working in humanitarian, development, recovery, or resilience-building ‎programmes, preferably within large national or international organizations, is an ‎advantage. ‎
- Strong understanding of stakeholder coordination and partnership management ‎within complex, multi-actor environments.‎

**Preferred** ‎

- Experience supporting the design or implementation of national, regional, or local ‎recovery and reconstruction initiatives is highly desirable.‎

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

**Required**

- Strong knowledge of humanitarian, recovery, resilience, and development ‎programming. ‎
- Good understanding of resource mobilization strategies, donor engagement, and ‎partnership development. ‎
- Knowledge of institutional donor funding mechanisms, grant processes, and financing ‎instruments. ‎
- Understanding of Ukraine's recovery and reconstruction architecture, government ‎institutions, and public sector planning processes. ‎
- Understanding of stakeholder engagement, public-private partnerships, and multi-‎sector coordination mechanisms. ‎
- Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic ‎digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem ‎solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.‎
- Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values. ‎
- Fluent spoken and written English
- Fluent spoken Ukrainian

**Preferred** ‎

- Familiarity with humanitarian principles, Red Cross Red Crescent Movement ‎structures, and partnership models is an advantage.‎
- Knowledge of policy analysis and the ability to interpret legislative, regulatory, and ‎institutional developments relevant to recovery and reconstruction.‎

Competencies, Values and Comments

**Values:** Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability

**Core competencies:** Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society ‎and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

**Functional competencies:** Strategic orientation; Building alliances; Leadership; Empowering others

**Managerial competencies:** Managing staff performance; Managing staff development.

title: Climate Resilience and Adaptation Advisor
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

**Summary:**

Position Summary

The Climate Resilience Advisor provides technical and advisory support to strengthen climate resilience of Habitat for Humanity’s housing and settlement work across Asia Pacific programs. The Advisor will work with the Asia-Pacific regional team to support Country Offices. This will include the implementation of strategic guidance, provision of technical assistance, design and delivery of capacity strengthening, supporting research, evidence-based implementation and knowledge management, advocacy and partnership development. This will include coordination with HFHI Global Program Operations, and specifically the Director-Climate Resilience (e.g., on development and implementation of the Global Climate Approach). The Advisor will work to ensure the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation into housing and settlement work and community development initiatives.

The Advisor will serve as the regional focal point for climate action, and in this capacity will support Country Offices to understand climate risks, and options to address/mitigate these risks to reduce vulnerability and build resilience of low- and middle-income households and communities across the Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Key Result Areas and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Alignment and Stakeholder Engagement (30%)**

Provide technical thought leadership to ensure climate resilient housing and settlement programming is aligned with the Global Climate Approach, with contextualized implementation across Country Offices in Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical leadership to support contextualized/localized implementation and monitoring of HFHI’s Global Climate Approach within the Asia Pacific region.
- Advise on current/recent sources of climate risk data and analyses, and options for integrating climate these risks into housing/settlement-focused project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Facilitate alignment and promote integration between climate resilience programming and broader disaster risk reduction/humanitarian programming.
- Serve as a technical resource and thought partner to Habitat Country Offices, supporting program design, implementation and learning.
- Engage with external stakeholders (HFHI’s global and regional partners, research institutions, NGOs, and networks) to strengthen technical positioning and partnerships opportunities around climate resilience and DRR.
- Represent HFHI and contribute to relevant regional and global forums, working groups, and coordination platforms, as required.
- Support strategic partnerships and collaboration opportunities that advance Habitat's climate resilience agenda.

**2. Capacity Building and Technical Support (25%)**

Strengthen the technical capacity of Country Offices and partners to design, implement, and scale high-quality climate resilience housing/settlement programming

**Key Responsibilities**

Assess in-country capacity, design and facilitate targeted capacity building initiatives (e.g., structured training, workshops, coaching) for National Organization staff on climate resilience.

Develop and maintain technical resources, tools, guidance documents, and learning materials.

Facilitate communities of practice, peer learning, and regional exchanges.

Promote organizational learning across countries, programs and operations.

**3. Technical Program Oversight (25%)**

Provide advisory support to Country Offices to help ensure the quality of climate-related program design, implementation and monitoring. considerations into program designs, projects—supporting Country Offices to scale impact, and cross-learning across the Asia Pacific Region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical input and advisory support to Country Offices to strengthen integration of climate risk data/analyses and evidenced-based approaches into climate resilient housing/settlements project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Advise Country Offices on context specific adaptation measures, including resilient construction techniques, site selection, safer land use, and community-based approaches.
- Where feasible, advise Country Offices on context appropriate mitigation measures, where feasible,
- Contribute technical input to concept notes, program proposals, and donor reports related to climate resilience (e.g., adaptation and mitigation).
- As requested, support donor engagement resource mobilization efforts.
- Collaborate with other Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and technical teams to ensure climate considerations are integrated into cross-sectoral programming.

**4. Research, Innovation, Learning and Knowledge Management (15%)**

Strengthen evidence generation, cross-learning and innovation, to improve climate resilient housing/settlement programming and support scaling of effective approaches.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support research design and implementation, the generation and synthesis of evidence, and institutional learning specific to climate resilient housing.
- Document and share climate resilient housing/settlement promising practices, case studies, and lessons learned.
- Contribute to integration of climate and DRR indicators into MEAL systems and contribute to regional and global learning agendas.
- Contribute to research, support innovation pilots, and partnerships related to climate resilient housing and settlements.
- Develop and disseminate technical resources, and guidance materials.
- Provide subject matter expertise and technical advisory support to other departments and initiatives within HFHI.

**5. Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery Support (5%)**

Provide advisory support to integrate climate risk reduction and resilience into disaster preparedness, response and recovery efforts

**Key Responsibilities**

Work with the Housing Disaster Risk and Resilience (HDRR) team on climate risk reduction measures in response and recovery

Provide technical input on risk-informed approaches to recovery planning and implementation

Support alignment of recovery interventions with long-term resilience objectives

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Risk Reduction, Urban Planning, Engineering, Development Studies, or a related field
- Minimum 5–7 years of relevant experience in climate resilience, DRR, or risk-informed programming, preferably in the Asia-Pacific region
- Demonstrated experience supporting multi-country programs and working with decentralized teams
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, and resilience approaches in housing, settlements, or community development
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, resilience, and mitigation approaches in housing, settlements, infrastructure, or community development.
- Experience in humanitarian, recovery, or nexus programming is an asset
- Experience in donor engagement, proposal development, or climate finance is an advantage

**Key Skills & Competencies**

- Strong technical expertise in climate adaptation and the built environment
- Sound understanding of climate mitigation, with the ability to understand where synergies and tradeoffs exist between mitigation and adaptation (especially where these impact affordability)
- Ability to translate technical concepts into practical, field-oriented guidance
- Proven advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English (regional languages an asset)
- Strong cross-cultural collaboration skills and ability to work in matrixed environments
- Willingness and ability to travel within the Asia-Pacific region

**Core Behavioral Competencies**

- Commitment to HFHI’s mission, values, equity, and safeguarding principles
- Collaboration and partnership mindset
- Learning oriented and solution focused
- Accountability and integrity

**Working Conditions**

- Regional role with frequent collaboration across multiple countries and time zones.
- Periodic travel to Country Offices and Country Offices, including fragile, climate-vulnerable, and disaster-affected contexts.
- Ability and willingness to travel within the Asia-Pacific region as required.

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Accounting Assistant
body:
**Purpose and Objectives:**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization for cooperation in and implementation of disaster risk reduction and building climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. It was established in 1986 as a regional disaster preparedness center (DMC). ADPC has grown and expended its role to be for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) in and effective manner.

The Finance and Accounting Unit is one of the ADPC’s Program Support Service Units with interlinked responsibilities with the Human Resource and Administration Unit and Procurement Unit and solely or jointly responsible for:

- Ensure compliance with statutory, legislative, and donor requirements.
- Safeguard ADPC’s cash, resources, and financial assets through effective internal control procedures.
- Monitor the effectiveness of the key control framework to minimize the risk of fraud and irregularities across ADPC.
- Ensure the availability of accurate and timely financial information for management decision-making.
- Develop and utilize appropriate financial tools to capture, store, and analyze financial data effectively and efficiently.
- Ensure the accuracy of budgetary information by promoting accountability and ownership among budget owners and facilitating budget monitoring.
- Allocate resources based on the priorities outlined and approved in the annual work plan.
- Administer institutional and donor audits in accordance with established guidelines.

**Purpose for the Assignment:**

ADPC is seeking a Finance and Accounting Assistant under a consultant contract to support its financial operations as the organization adopts International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) from 1 January 2027. The assignment will focus on reviewing supporting documents, assisting with payment processing, preparing accounting entries, and maintaining financial records. The Assistant will help ensure timely and accurate transaction processing, contributing to the Finance Unit’s capacity to meet new accounting and reporting requirement.

**Expected Outputs:**

The Accounting Assistant will provide support throughout the assignment in reviewing financial documents, assisting with payment processing, and preparing accounting entries and supporting records. Tasks will be assigned by the supervisor according to the Finance Unit’s operational needs and accounting and reporting requirements.

This position will be based in Headquarters in Bangkok, Thailand.

Note:

*It is not the intent of this Terms of Reference to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

Under the supervision of the designated Finance supervisor, the Accounting Assistant will perform the following tasks :

**Document examination**

- Review payment and advance requests to ensure they are properly authorized, fully supported with required documentation, and in compliance with ADPC policies and procedures.
- Review liquidation of cash advance to ensure that reported expenditures are adequately supported and comply with established policies and procedures.
- Follow up with relevant staff on missing documents, discrepancies, and outstanding liquidations, and notify them by email of the completion of liquidations and the corresponding settlement amounts
- Ensure that project codes, activity codes, and account codes are accurate and consistent with the nature and purpose of each transaction
- Calculate withholding tax on payment to vendor, supplier, consultant as applicable, as per Thai Revenue Code.

**Payment Processing Support**

- Ensure that all payment requests are processed within the required deadlines.

**Accounting**

- Prepare accounting entries for review, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency with ADPC’s accounting policies
- Maintain supporting records in an orderly manner and compile transaction information for financial reporting and audit purposes

**Others**

- Perform any other related duties and responsibilities as may be assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the purpose and scope of this assignment

**Corporate Responsibilities**

- Ensure that all duties and responsibilities are carried out with a commitment to gender equality, diversity, social inclusion.
- Create a working environment at ADPC and ensure the protection and safety of all beneficiaries in accordance with ADPC’s PSEA and child protection policies.
- Contribute to environmentally sustainable practices, minimize waste, and ensure do no harm to people or the environment is observed.
- Ensure fraud is prevented, detected and dealt with promptly in their area of work. Be responsible for safeguarding resources entrusted to ADPC and for upholding and protecting its reputation.

**Working Principles:** The consultant will work in close collaboration with the Finance and Accounting Unit. The role requires adherence to accounting policies and key operational guidelines to ensure smooth workflow and compliance with ADPC policies.

**Qualifications:** The candidate should hold:

**Required Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree, preferable in accounting, finance, business or related field.
- Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply. Working/Internship experience in finance and accounting, particularly within an international non-profit or non-governmental organization, would be an advantage.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, MS Office applications, and Google Sheet. Experience in accounting software (preferable SUN systems) and database would be advantage. Knowledge on basic accounting principles and practices, familiar with international Accounting Standards would be an advantage.
- Knowledge on relevant tax laws and regulations would be an advantage.
- Attention to detail with excellent organizational skills.
- Good command of English, both written and spoken.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Ability to work in a team and across teams, in a multi-cultural environment
- Strong motivation, desire to learn; undertake new challenges
- Self-confidence, commitment and willingness to work hard
- Ensure confidentiality in all sensitive information

**Duty Station:** ADPC Bangkok office, Thailand

**Duration:**  Twelve months consultancy contract January – December 2027

**Itinerary:** N/A

**Condition of payment:**

The payment will be based on a monthly basis, supplemented with a monthly timesheet submitted and approved by designated supervisor.

title: Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** will provide strategic and technical expertise in the design, development, governance, and deployment of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data systems, including databases, digital platforms, and AI-enabled solutions. Support evidence-based management and strengthen capacity across Pacific Island countries through innovative, standardised, and sustainable data systems.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Develop and maintain high-quality regional and national coastal fisheries and aquaculture databases and information systems and provide training in their use**

- Develops, maintains and updates the regional coastal fisheries (science, management and development) and aquaculture databases including training in the use of databases, data extraction and analysis
- Develops new web and mobile applications for the regional and national databases in line with country needs and the needs of the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff
- Develops and assists in maintaining national databases based on the regional databases and additional modules.
- Develops specific queries for data extraction and analysis as required by countries or the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff.
- Promotes and encourages the use of standard databases and information systems across the region for coastal fisheries and aquaculture data, and countries to providing the data they collect for back-up and storage at SPC.
- Identifies and develops linkages between the coastal fisheries and oceanic fisheries databases in collaboration with oceanic fisheries statistics and data collection section.
- Identifies ways to better use GIS and remote sensing products in relation to the analysis of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data.

**Practical assistance to members in the designing and targeting of appropriate awareness raising and educational information**

- Develops training materials on data entry, cleaning and extraction.
- Assists with developing and maintaining the website for the CFAP with the Information Unit to assist with the dissemination of information in general.
- Provides input to awareness raising and educational materials focused on coastal fisheries science and/or management or livelihoods and aquaculture

**Develop Artificial Intelligence based tools and models for data collection**

- Improves coastal fisheries and aquaculture data collection using photos and videos automatically processed by computer vision and artificial intelligence
- Develops and trains models to calibrate and reproject pictures for measurement from picture
- Develops and trains models to automate measurements of fishes and invertebrates for the various types of measurements
- Develops and trains models for species identification

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration in coastal fisheries and aquaculture**

- Develops links with other CROP agencies and NGOs in regard to database needs and design for coastal fisheries and aquaculture
- Advocates at global forums on behalf of the Pacific region sectoral interests
- Develops and promotes collaborations within the CFAP on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.
- Works closely with other sections of CFAP to ensure smooth implementation of projects.

**Administration and communication**

- Assists the CFAP Deputy Director and Section heads, to include information and database needs in the annual work plans and work plan reports for each Section, consistent with the strategic plan.
- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, and Divisional reports for CRGA.
- Produces reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity including technical reports and trip reports, and input to funding proposals, donor reports.
- Manage, develop and train direct report.
- Fills in for senior staff when they are on leave or duty travel, when required

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master’s in computer science, database development or a related field/discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ of demonstrated experience in database management, project management and software development associated with the successful implementation of medium- to large-scale web and desktop application systems.
- At least 8 years’ of demonstrated experience in the use of Microsoft products, both as a user and developer, in particular, (i) experience in software engineering, (ii) programming in client-server environments in C# with MS Visual Studio, (iii) ASP.NET Core and single page web applications with MS Visual Studio (C#, JavaScript and angularjs), (iv) database technologies (preferably SQL Server) and other database formats, (v) development of mobile application in C# (.NET MAUI).
- Demonstrated experience with (i) producing system and user manual documentation, (ii) user training and (iii) ongoing technical support for deployed applications.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills, detail orientation, and ability to multi-task.

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and negotiate with people from different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 5,012-6,169 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 723,251-890,185 (USD 6,717-8,267; EUR 6,061-7,460). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

title: Finance & HR Manager
body:
**MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people.**

**We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect.**

**Finance & HR Manager - Country Programmes**

**French speaker**

**Based in country programmes of MSF-OCA**

The Fin/HR Manager is responsible for the implementation of Human Resources policies in the project and the Administrative Management of all staff working in the project (including those recruited locally and internationally), along with the proper implementation of financial administration, management and control in the project.

This job description provides a framework for the main responsibilities and primary activities of the position, it is not all-encompassing. Therefore, the responsibilities and activities of the position may differ from those described in this job description due to organizational and operational needs.

**Objectives and responsibilities of the position**

- In close coordination with the Project Coordinator and the HR Coordinator, calculate the HR operational needs and the associated budget to efficiently ensure the project's required sizing and capabilities and facilitate budget follow-up.
- Plan, supervise and ensure the implementation of the staffing processes (including recruitment, training, briefing, induction, evaluation, development and communication) of the project staff, in close coordination with the HRCo.
- Take ownership of recruitment processes by ensuring effective hiring practices, integrating safeguarding measures at every stage, and strengthening staff capabilities, engagement, contribution to mission objectives, and commitment to MSF values.
- Supervise, coach and develop the Finance and HR team, ensuring appropriate delegation, performance follow-up and capacity building.
- Advise on set-up and updating the project's organizational chart and job descriptions and assisting the Project Coordinator, and/or team leaders and supervisors to draw up annual holiday planning and staff shifts in order to forecast HR needs and to ensure HR availability for the project activities.
- Ensure hiring, carry out amendments and contract termination formalities for employees at project level, according to labour local laws, managing individual employee files, informing them on their rights and preparing all mandatory tax declarations, in order to ensure legal compliance of the project activities.
- Supervise/perform payroll procedures, ensuring correct entry of all data related to monthly salary calculation of employees of the project.
- In close collaboration with the Project Coordinator and HRCo, look for options to avoid/solve possible labour conflicts in the project.
- Is responsible for all movements and/or accommodation of staff in the project.
- Ensure that MSF staff who have financial responsibilities are aware of and comply with local finance procedures, including those related to security.
- Ensure that project finance activities are carried out in line with OCA and mission finance policies & procedures, for example cash & safe management, advances management, authorizations (expenses and payments), payments (cash, bank & cheque), cash flow management, etc.
- Is responsible for assessing and suggesting mitigation measures of the financial risks of the project.
- Ensure that reliable internal control systems are in place, and financial ethics are respected within the project.
- Ensure proper and timely day-to-day bookkeeping takes place in the accounting software per MSF OCA Chart of accounts
- Ensure proper bookkeeping support documentation (hardcopy invoices/receipts, PO/PL/contract as applicable) is available for each bookkeeping entry.
- Ensure that daily and monthly bookkeeping closure takes place in line with the standard procedure, with due quality and on time.
- Support Project Coordinator and the Finance Coordinator with budgeting and monthly budget control activities, in order to ensure that funds are used in line with last approved budgets.

**Requirements**

- A degree in finance, management (business, HR) or administration is desirable.
- Essential working experience of at least five years in relevant and similar jobs.
- MSF or other NGO experience is desirable.
- Working proficiency in English and French (minimum B2 or equivalent) are required.
- Computer literacy (word, excel, internet) is essential.
- Knowledge of HR and Financial (MSF) software or willingness to learn.
- Availability for project durations of 6-9-12 months depending on operational needs.
- Willingness and ability to work in high insecurity zones and emergency responses.

**Assets**

- A good command of Arabic and/or Spanish language.

**Information and Application**

If you recognise yourself in this profile and meet the requirements, we encourage you to apply directly via the Apply button on this page and upload the following documents:

- Your most recent CV (in English) not exceeding 3 pages
- A cover letter explaining your motivation to work with MSF

***Female candidates who meet the requirements are strongly encouraged to apply.***

If you are interested and would like to have additional information, please contact Recruitment, recruitment@amsterdam.msf.org.

title: ERL Program Manager
body:
## General Information

- **Department:** ERL/FSL Program
- **Job Title:** ERL Program Manager
- **Duty Station**: Aleppo

### Overview of Bonyan Organization

Bonyan is an independent non-profit organization established in 2004 in Aleppo, Syria, and officially licensed in Turkey in 2014. Our response program focuses on three main areas: **Education, Protection, and Livelihoods**.

### Vision

We envision a developed and responsible population capable of contributing to the rebirth of Syrian society and the development of its civilization.

### Mission

To improve the quality of education and instill core values that contribute to the rise of Syrian society.

### Our Values

- Proficiency
- Initiative
- Welfare
- Abundance

## Job Purpose

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programs, the Early Recovery Program Manager will be responsible for the successful strategic planning, implementation, and overall oversight of all Early Recovery projects within Bonyan's operations. This includes projects focused on shelter, livelihoods, and critical infrastructure that contribute to early recovery.

The role involves managing the program team, ensuring proper integration and achievement of projects in line with organizational strategies, and collaborating closely with other departments to ensure all activities are properly executed. The Program Manager will also play a crucial role in leading business development activities, representing Bonyan in coordination meetings with donors and other relevant bodies, and ensuring financial sustainability and compliance of the program.

## Duties and Responsibilities

**I. Program Management & Leadership:**

- Lead the development of a comprehensive work plan for the implementation of the Early Recovery program.
- Drive strategy development and articulate the vision for the Early Recovery program within Bonyan's broader strategic framework.
- Oversee the successful implementation and monitoring of all Early Recovery program projects, ensuring adherence to project timelines, objectives, and quality standards.
- Lead monthly program follow-ups, including active participation in grant management meetings, thorough review of procurement plans, analysis of budget forecasts, and assessment of progress against contractual indicators.
- Lead the financial management of the Early Recovery programs, encompassing comprehensive budget development, meticulous expenditure, tracking, and rigorous adherence to donor financial regulations and Bonyan's internal policies. This includes identifying needs for budget revisions and proactively working to secure funding for project sustainability.
- Directly manage and supervise program staff, which includes preparing and monitoring staff performance plans, developing tailored training plans for staff capacity building, and providing constructive feedback.
- Provide technical management, support, and expert advice to staff and project managers who implement Early Recovery activities.
- Develop and conduct necessary training sessions for both Bonyan staff and partner organizations to enhance program delivery.
- Supervise, motivate, and mentor the staff under their responsibility, ensuring clarity of objectives and strong team performance.
- Conduct initial data analysis and prepare early drafts of reports for surveys and studies conducted as part of the program.
- In collaboration with the related department, participate in developing comprehensive program plans, including detailed Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) frameworks, recruitment plans, procurement schedules, and accurate budget forecasts.
- Represent Bonyan in Clusters, technical working groups, and donors’ meetings.

**II. Strategic Development & External Relations:**

- Oversee the planning and achievement of business development activities related to the Early Recovery program, identifying new opportunities and partnerships.
- Represent Bonyan professionally in coordination meetings, relevant program meetings, and engagements with donors and other coordination bodies.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including local authorities, community leaders, NGOs, and UN agencies.
- Contribute to the development of concept notes and proposals to secure new funding for Early Recovery initiatives.

**III. Capacity Building & Quality Assurance:**

- Ensure that all ERL projects are implemented in strict alignment with Bonyan's policies and comply with all donor regulations and international standards.
- Play a key role in adapting Bonyan's policies to the specific contextual realities of Syria, ensuring they are culturally sensitive and effective.
- Lead initiatives for gathering systematic feedback from beneficiaries and communities to inform program design and adaptation.
- Ensure the planning and implementation of Humanitarian Principles, meticulously ensuring adherence to "Do No Harm" principles and appropriate sensitization across all activities.
- Lead staff capacity development initiatives, including the design and delivery of training programs, assessment tools, and monitoring frameworks related to protection issues.
- Stay continuously updated on new donors’ requirements, trends, legal frameworks, and best practices relevant to the Syrian context, integrating this knowledge into program design and implementation.

## Academic Qualifications, Requirements, and Skills

**Academic Qualifications:**

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Disaster Management, International Development, Humanitarian Studies, or a closely related field.

A Master’s degree in a relevant field is highly preferred.

**Requirements:**

- Minimum of 5 years of progressive professional experience in managing early recovery and livelihood projects, including those related to shelter and critical infrastructure, within a humanitarian or development context.
- Demonstrated ability to represent the organization's image in a professional and effective manner.
- Profound commitment to humanitarian relief standards, Sphere standards, and other relevant international humanitarian principles.
- Strong understanding of early recovery principles, durable solutions, and humanitarian-development-peace nexus (HDPN) approaches.
- PMP (Project Management Professional) certification or equivalent project management qualification is highly preferred.
- Proven ability to engage effectively with donors and meticulously review narrative and financial reports.
- Prior experience working in Syria or similar complex humanitarian contexts is a significant advantage.

**Skills:**

- Communication: Excellent interpersonal skills, highly effective verbal and written communication, and comprehensive report writing skills.
- Management: High managerial skills, including strong remote management capabilities, and a proven ability to build, lead, and motivate high-performing teams.
- Financial Acumen: Strong knowledge of financial follow-up matters, budgeting, and financial reporting.
- Problem-Solving: Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to navigate complex challenges and make sound decisions in dynamic environments.
- Teamwork: Strong commitment to teamwork and collaborative approaches.
- Innovation: Innovative mindset and proven ability to work effectively under pressure and tight deadlines.
- Leadership: Strong delegation skills and the ability to empower and develop staff.
- Adaptability: High ability to learn, adapt, and develop in a rapidly changing operation
- Language: Fluency in both Arabic and English (written and spoken) is essential.

## General Principles

Bonyan Organization is committed to the highest standards of integrity and social responsibility, and maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of sexual exploitation, abuse, or child maltreatment. We take all concerns and complaints related to such matters seriously, whether they involve our staff members or individuals associated with the organization. Bonyan is dedicated to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults engaged through our activities by ensuring a safe environment free from any actions or negligence that may expose them to abuse, exploitation, or harm. As part of this commitment, we conduct thorough background checks and reference verifications for all candidates throughout the recruitment process. Bonyan is also committed to gender equality and promoting diversity within its workforce. We strongly encourage qualified women, persons with disabilities, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply for available opportunities. We believe that achieving the highest standards of competence, capability, and integrity must go hand in hand with fostering diversity and inclusion in the workplace.

title: Advocacy Advisor Multi Country (Nairobi Based, Open for Kenyans only)
body:
**Background:**

The humanitarian situation in Somalia and Kenya in 2026 remains among the most severe and protracted, driven by conflict, economic pressures, climate shocks, disease outbreaks, mass displacement, and shrinking humanitarian funding.

Conflict and climate shocks in Somalia fuel internal displacement, placing additional pressure on already overstretched services and humanitarian systems.

NRC works in Somalia to protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis and meet immediate humanitarian needs, prevent further displacement, and contribute to durable solutions. Access remains a significant operational challenge due to active conflict, insecurity and bureaucratic impediments, making it difficult for aid organisations to reach those in need. Our programmes primarily include rapid response to emergencies, multipurpose cash assistance, legal protection, education, shelter, and water, sanitation and hygiene. Beyond this, NRC co-leads or supports coordination structures in both countries, including Shelter, CCCM and Protection clusters and the HLP and Durable Solutions Working Groups.

**What you will do:**

The Advocacy Advisor plays a pivotal role in shaping NRC’s policy influence and public positioning in Somalia and Kenya, two of the most complex humanitarian contexts globally. Operating at a senior level, the role leads the design and implementation of advocacy and communications strategies, ensuring coherence with country programme priorities and global standards. It provides expert analysis, develops evidence based advocacy products, and represents NRC in key fora, while also building the capacity of staff and partners to amplify the voices of displaced communities. By bridging operational realities with policy engagement, the Advocacy Advisor ensures NRC’s responses are not only impactful on the ground but also contribute to systemic change at national, regional, and international levels.

General Responsibilities:

1. Identify and coordinate NRC’s advocacy response to prioritised issues both within the country and internationally
2. Develop and implement an impactful advocacy and communications strategy, aligned with the overall country strategy.
3. Develop CO media plan and lines, ensuring risk analyses are made regarding public positions or statements and sign-off procedures are adhered to
4. Line management of communications teams, including development of staff if applicable, budget planning and execution, and other administration
5. Ensure systematic training on advocacy and communication to develop capacity of all relevant staff (within and beyond the advocacy and media department) and ensure compliance with NRC policies, e.g. informed consent, data protection, social media standards

Specific responsibilities:

1. Strategically and ethically raise issues and voices of displaced people in Somalia and Kenya to the attention of decision-makers, duty-bearers, and the public, through both traditional and innovative means
2. Increase accountability of NRC Somalia and Kenya through providing regular and consistent information publicly, about the situations we are responding to and the state of our response (or contributions to coordinated responses)
3. Contribute to Country Office and Area Office problem, protection, and programme analyses and ‘systems thinking’ with a policy lens and a public interest lens, and subsequently promote that relevant policy, advocacy, and communications elements are integrated when designing responses and strategies
4. Coordinate and monitor implementation and impact of NRC Somalia, Kenya, etc. advocacy and media plans and strategies
5. Prepare high quality briefings, reports, press statements, letters, and other communications materials (including visual, digital, and social media) for internal coordination and external use

**Please read the** [**full Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCTQMUUk7ptS4YRhDoAd2svASLS69XHBdPcOta_N73QWUg?e=cMfDfW) **as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Post-graduate with minimum five years of relevant experience within the humanitarian field or international media/organisations
- Must have humanitarian advocacy experience and policy management from different contexts.
- Relevant experience in advocacy, communications, media, or humanitarian policy
- Experience working in complex and insecure contexts, preferably in the Horn of Africa
- Strong understanding of humanitarian coordination architecture and donor environments
- Proven experience engaging media and managing sensitive external communications
- Experience producing high-level advocacy products and policy analysis.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- High levels of flexibility and creativity
- Documented professional experience of working in or with international media
- Strong managerial and interpersonal skills
- Fluency in English with strong verbal and written communications skills

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Nairobi **(national contract)**
- Contract: 24 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: *70% of dedicated time to the Somalia country office, including regular visits to Somalia (once every 3 months); 10% dedicated time to the Kenya country office; and 20% travel to other countries in East Africa to be identified.*
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **national** salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Applicants should include to their Cover Letter, links to their three most compelling advocacy, media & communications production in their cover letter, ideally one text, one video, one TV/radio interview.**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Kenya. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency permits.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Program Development and Awards Advisor, WACAR
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors. These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD**.** The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview**

The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.

These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.

In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.
