**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Project Manager Digital Transformation
body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with a contract duration of two years. Employment location will be Bonn, Germany.

As a Project Manager at WHH, you will play a crucial role in coordinating our strategic digital transformation project that drives real impact, collaborating with international teams, and ensuring our mission to create a world without hunger is achieved. If you are passionate about global change and have a track record of delivering successful projects, we invite you to make a difference with WHH.

## Your responsibilities

- Create and maintain project plans, including timelines, milestones, critical paths, and resources.
- Track project tasks, maintain task logs, and follow up with stakeholders to ensure timely completion.
- Proven experience in managing projects involving CRM systems and marketing automation platforms
- Identify and track project risks and coordinate mitigation measures.
- Plan and monitor project budgets
- Prepare project status reports and presentations for project teams and C-level management.
- Maintain project documentation and knowledge sharing using SharePoint and Confluence.
- Coordinate operational handovers, including the preparation of operational handbooks.
- Support the development and improvement of project management tools, templates, and processes (PMO toolbox).

## Your profile

- At least 3 years of experience in IT project management, business administration.
- Proven project management skills, ideally supported by certifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, or Scrum.
- Experience with traditional (Waterfall), Agile (Scrum), and Hybrid project management methodologies.
- Hands-on experience with project management tools such as Jira, MS Project, or similar.
- Strong organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- You recognize the growing value of data in your field and are eager to build your awareness and skills to incorporate data-informed approaches into your work.
- Fluent in German and English

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Work-Life Balance: Enjoy flexible working arrangements to support a balanced lifestyle.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which are listed under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-employees-in-germany/).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

title: 23673 Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Ghana (resident), Togo, and Benin, and in close collaboration with the relevant units at the Regional Office (RO) and Headquarters (HQ), the Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer will be responsible and accountable for supporting the coordination and facilitation of project development, donor and institutional reporting in the fields of migration management, emergency response, as well as assisting with liaison activities with counterparts in the government, UN agencies, and other relevant stakeholders in line with IOM’s regional and country strategies.

**Responsibilities**

1. Contribute to the development of results-based programmes and projects, concept notes and project proposals, in close coordination with the CoM, Project Managers, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), relevant donors, government counterparts and project partners, by providing technical inputs and support that respond to emerging trends and priorities and that are in compliance with IOM and donor interests and requirements.
2. Review resource requirements, document programmatic needs, gaps and opportunities. Contribute to the alignment to IOM global, regional and country strategies during project development and donor reporting, including supporting and promoting use of Strategic Results Framework (SRF) global results and indicators.
3. Support the endorsement process for concept notes and project proposals. Support the Project Managers in drafting donor reports in close coordination with relevant units in the Country Office (CO) and RO in line with IOM policies, standards and internal procedures.
4. Research potential and realistic funding opportunities among government and non-government donors, review calls for proposals and collect donor information. Draft donor profiles and guidance notes on donor priorities and assist with developing approaches to expand the IOM donor base.
5. Support effective working relationships with donor counterparts and project/programme partners, such as government authorities, diplomatic missions, and other relevant agencies and working groups.
6. In coordination with relevant Units in the CO, draft visibility and other resource mobilization materials and organize donor briefings and visits.
7. Capacity building and training activities in the field of programme development, donor and institutional reporting and the roll-out of the SRF for CO’s staff through workshops and seminars.
8. In support of knowledge management, maintain accurate, updated and pertinent records of all correspondence, project development and donor and institutional reporting files, and related information in IOM’s relevant software application.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, International Development, Political or Social Sciences, Migration Studies, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in supporting results-based project development and reporting, technical writing and editing, preferably in the international development/humanitarian sector;
- Proven experience in donor relations and grant management for specific donors of IOM’s interest;
- Demonstrated experience with Results-Based Management approach and other strategic planning approaches; and,
- Proven experience in donor report writing in humanitarian and/or development settings.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated communication, writing and organizational skills; ability to prepare clear and concise reports;
- Demonstrated knowledge of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and methodologies;
- Proven analytical and planning skills; capacity to establish working relationships with  
    governmental authorities, national and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations;
- Demonstrated capacity to supervise and train support staff; ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds;
- Demonstrated ability to work with accuracy under constraints and pressure; high sense of confidentiality, initiative and good judgment;
- Demonstrated personal commitment, efficiency, flexibility, drive for results, creative thinking; and,
- Good level of computer literacy, including database applications.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Finance Manager
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Finance Manager** for our operations in Addis Ababa Country Office.

**Instruction for applicants:**  
***All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered***

**Overall purpose of the role**

This role has a country focus and ensures the financial health and stability of DRC ETH, foster strong donor relationships and support the organisational localisation efforts while ensuring compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country Finance activities.

The Finance Manager is vested with powers to execute management policies and responsibilities to hire, suspend, layoff, dismiss or assign employees within the Finance department as necessary for the operations.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**Management & Leadership:**

Within his/her management mandate, and in alignment with DRC’s leadership standards and policies, the position holder:

- Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
- Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
- Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team and implementing termination decisions in accordance with DRC’s two-step principle.
- Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
- Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
- Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.Is accountable for people management of direct reports, including hiring & firing, objective setting and priorities as per the strategic direction, probation, performance appraisal, development of staff, managing performance, including poor performance, etc.
- Is accountable for making sound decisions based on DRC policies, MOPs, standards, and the advice of technical experts in DRC.
- Accountable for making significant decisions on what the Finance team does: its purpose, functions and role, and for making commitments and decisions that require the expenditure of significant unit resources.
- Manages all finance related tasks within the country (Addis and field offices) - this includes but not limited to financial planning & analysis, cash flow management, financial risk management, budgeting & reporting, compliance and finance capacity building or teams and DRC implementing partners.
- Support the development and implementation of financial management capacity building of staff in the Country Finance team and provide support to the Area based Finance teams.
- Work to build the capacity of finance staff members throughout the program through frequent in-service training sessions and mentoring support.
- Ensure data protection and confidentiality in handling all financial information and organization documents

**Financial Management and Planning**

- Oversee the finance department for the entire operation, providing training and oversight to country office finance staff as well as advising and ensuring adequate support to area office finance staff.
- In close cooperation with Managers and AMs, reinforce existing procedures and systems for financial management and control in compliance with guidelines of DRC’s Operations Handbook, internal guidelines and donor requirements.
- Support timely delivery of quality financial reports to donors and internal reports to colleagues and HQ.
- Ensure compliance with relevant country statutory and other financial obligations such as tax, levies and statutory returns.
- Monthly/weekly financial briefings to Head of Support Services
- Ensure Finance team preparation and active participation in monthly Budget Follow Up reviews and in monthly/quarterly Project Monitoring Meeting (financial aspects) to discuss key variances, reasons for these, and any remedial action that is required.
- Ensure thorough and effective budgetary control in the country programs.
- Liaise with relevant Managers and budget holders on key financial issues for all programs in the country, including co-funding, financial reporting, key variances, and recommend and support any remedial action required, reporting major issues to the Head of Support Services for action.
- Collecting cash forecasts from all Programme Managers and requesting funds in a timely manner.
- Maintain a continuous overview of funding levels and pay particular attention to shared support costs, including staff salaries and other shared cost lines.
- Ensure all required documentation for financial audits in cooperation with Coordination staff and HQ.
- In preparation for local audits, the Finance Manager will support the Head of Support Services and the Senior Management Team of DRC in liaising with government officials, and external auditors, in relation to issues of audit and compliance.
- Contribute to the development of proposals with regards to budgeting in cooperation with Managers.
- Ensure a Master Budget is in place and UpToDate, in Dynamics and lead a monthly gap analysis meeting with Senior Management Team.
- Coordinate the allocation table & resource scheduling with the different budget holders
- Forecast future financial performance and analyse financial data to guide decision-making.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to the DRC standards for operations. This includes, among other things, supervision of all financial reporting and financial procedures, including the monthly schedule for financial reporting, donor reporting and audits, cash flow and liquidity management, legal framework and reporting relations to National authorities.

**Systems Improvement and Compliance**

- Ensure DRC Dynamics is used to its full capacity as per the guidelines set by DRC’s Headquarters.
- Ensure proper application of ERP finance processes across the country, providing remote and in-person field support and guidance.
- Responsible for ensuring all new Finance staff across DRC Ethiopia receive an in-depth induction to Microsoft Dynamics as applicable to their role.
- Apply reports and data analytics from ERP system to improve performance in the country.
- Ensure that Country ERP support is in place (i.e. super users).
- Improve and implement comprehensive internal office controls in line with DRC’s Operations Handbook.
- Develop process for approving and monitoring spending to different DRC’s projects through Area Managers.
- Coordinate financial management and systems training for non-finance staff.
- Travel to field location(s) as necessary (30% of time) and provide oversight of field office financial systems and processes if needed.
- Support the finance team on key compliance issues, such as DRC’s Operations Handbook, ChSA (Charities and Societies Agency) audit.
- Review key processes and work closely with the Head of Support Services (HoSS) to suggest improvements for scale and efficiency, while managing risk.

**Reporting and Analysis**

- Lead monthly review of project expenses comparing actual to budget and analyzing variances.
- Participate in ongoing analysis, forecasting and review of project expenses, accruals, and projections.
- Prepare and submit ad hoc reports on portfolio financial status for senior management, including annual Prognosis reports, in coordination with Head of Programme for pipeline projects affecting Master Budget gap analysis.
- Review and approve the financial close-out of program activities as required by grant rules, and verify documentation and information is complete
- Run financial KPI meetings as necessary.
- Develop a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy. This will be done through regular review of the country Risk Register and Issues Log and submission of quarterly inputs from the Finance department.

**Accounting**

- Review all financial data entries that go into the Dynamics ERP system.
- Ensure all payment requests and wire transfer requests for payments to vendors are completed in compliance with contract requirements and paid on time, adjusting work processes in the country office Finance department as required.
- Ensure on time management, review, and processing of payroll, invoices, and in-field fee payments in accordance with DRC’s accounting procedures and donor policies.
- Ensure bank statements, bank reconciliations, and submitted expense reports are reasonable, allocable, and auditable are posted on Dynamics.
- Review monthly reconciliation of Bank accounts and prepare monthly close out as per the guidelines provided by HQ.
- Prepare for and participate in all financial reviews/audits required.
- Ensure that all month & year end accounts reconciliation and closure are done on a timely basis\*\*.\*\*

**Partnership Management**

- Participate in setting partner selection criteria and in the final selection
- Participate in potential partner due-diligence assessment
- Review sub-grant agreement for donor’s audit requirement, instalments, reporting, etc.
- Participate in partners project kick-off and close-out meeting
- Process advance/reimbursement payment request of partners
- Participate in partner capacity assessment and work with partner to execute the capacity development plan
- Participate in partner monitoring visit and prepare a report
- Actively engage in partner project management/review meeting
- Review and approve financial report of partner

Within **Technical Supervision mandate of Field Support Services Managers / TL and Field Finance Officers and Assistants**, the position holder is responsible for:

- Providing technical direction, guidance, and where mandated, instructions to ensure compliance with DRC policies, standards, and strategies.
- Supporting managers and technical staff through regular communication, capacity building, and promotion of best practices.
- Support managers with assessing the technical skills and performance of most senior supply chain staff in field offices.
- Escalating and, where authorized, addressing issues of non-compliance or poor performance in line with the technical supervision mandate.
- Participating in the recruitment of Finance staff in the field offices.

All DRC roles require the post-holder to master DRC’s core competencies:

- Striving for excellence: Focusing on reaching results while ensuring efficient processes.
- Collaborating: Involving relevant parties and encouraging feedback.
- Taking the lead: Taking ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- Communicating: Listening and speaking effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating integrity: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- At least 5 years’ experience in in a senior financial management position.
- At least 3 years’ experience with people management
- Proven experience in managing large budgets of international humanitarian organizations
- Proven leadership skills and a competence in people management
- Competence in providing technical guidance and training
- Proven experience in working with national partners, local/government authorities
- Working experience with relevant donors (e.g. NORAD, SIDA, EU, ECHO, ECHO, DANIDA, GFFO, SDC, FCDO, etc.) and sound understanding of their respective financial rules and regulations including financial reporting requirements
- Advanced proficiency in Excel as well as experience working in a financial IT system, particularly Microsoft Dynamics
- Have a track record of achieving high targets in a highly demanding and challenging context with multiple conflicting priorities.
- Demonstrate expert proficiency in advance Excel with large/complicated financial data analysis and presentation.
- Have a collaborative approach to work and have been able to achieve results through influencing others. .
- Be able to multitask and deliver results while working independently.
- Be self-driven and solutions oriented, with a record of solutions created through personal initiative.

**EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)**

- Master’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting or related field.
- Professional certification in Accounting.

**LANGUAGE:** (indicate Fluency level)

- Full professional proficiency in English (Verbal and written).

***In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:***

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: 12 Months with possibility of extension

Contract Type: National Contract

Band: F1

Designation of Duty Station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Please note that this position is not eligible for relocation.

Required Employees: 1

Start date: 1st January 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for National employees

title: Project Manager, Programme Portfolio Transitioning
body:
## **The assignment**

Children’s Villages Worldwide (CVW) will conclude its funding of SOS Children’s Villages Syria at the end of 2028. Seven programme units — family-like care, semi-independent living, family strengthening, youth care and a programme for children and young people with disabilities — serving a planned caseload of 901 participants must reach a safe, defined onward arrangement before that date.

We are looking for an experienced transitioning Project Manager to run that process on the ground in Damascus. This is not a start-up role and it is not a conventional country-director post. It is a closure and transition assignment, in a politically sensitive environment, where the central obligation is that no child, young person or family is worse off at the end of it. Four units are designated for handover to a receiving partner under an agreement that is currently blocked on government approvals. Three units, including the disability programme, have no pathway yet. Defining one is the first thing this role has to solve.

## **What you will do**

- Hold the transitioning plan across all seven units and drive it to the timetable — designs, transfers, closures, and  
    the gate reviews in between.
- Lead the search, due diligence and safeguarding audit for receiving partners where no pathway yet exists and  
    prepare the contracting recommendations.
- Make sure every transfer is phased rather than a cut-over: joint case conferences, shadowing, transfer of  
    responsibility, and follow-up visits at one and three months.
- Build one verified child-by-child baseline register from five inconsistent sources and keep it accurate.
- Work alongside Syrian ministries, receiving partners and retained legal counsel to secure the approvals the  
    transitioning depends on.
- Run the degressive funding schedule with the finance specialist, so that services shrink behind the caseload and  
    never ahead of it.
- Deliver a monthly dashboard and quarterly reporting that give CVW and the GSC an honest picture, including of  
    what is going wrong.

## What we are looking for

The Project Manager will have an appropriate balance of leadership, managerial, technical, and interpersonal skills and experience.

**Essential**

- Around ten years in humanitarian or development programme management, with senior delivery responsibility in a complex or conflict-affected setting.
- Real experience of closing or transferring a programme, portfolio or service to another organisation — not only of building one.
- Experience in executing large budgets and supervise budget expenditure across several projects in emergency  
    context.
- Alternative care or child protection expertise, including case management and best-interests processes.
- Professional Arabic and English, strong enough to negotiate and to draft in both.
- A track record of working with government ministries on approvals, registration and closure.
- Ensure the project management and compilation of project data including progress tracking and reporting to CVW and other relevant stakeholders.
- Act as the main focal point between the CVW and the SOSCV Syria or designated local partners: ensure key  
    decisions and commitments are accurately documented and turned into clear, tracked actions, agreed and  
    coordinated with all relevant parties
- Lead on the portfolio transitioning risk management: assessment and mitigation plans development.
- Willingness to be based in Damascus for the duration or travel on regular basis.

**Desirable**

- Experience in Syria or the wider Levant; disability-inclusive service provision; familiarity with international  
    federated organisations;

**The kind of person this suits**  
Someone who can hold a plan steady while several of its assumptions are still unresolved. Someone who documents as they go, escalates early rather than absorbing problems. The role carries responsibility for outcomes it cannot always control, and reports honestly on both.

**Safeguarding**  
This is a child-contact role. Appointment is subject to safer-recruitment checks: verified references covering all work  
with children, criminal-record or equivalent checks in every country of residence over the past ten years, disclosure of  
any previous safeguarding investigation or finding, and signature of our Child and Youth Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct before any engagement. Candidates must declare any existing relationship with SOS Children’s Villages Syria or SOS Children’s Villages Jordan,

title: 23559 Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Afghanistan and the direct supervision of the Head of the Programme Support Unit and in coordination with relevant units at Headquarters (HQ) and the Regional Office (RO), the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will be responsible for leading the management of the monitoring, evaluation, learning, reporting and communicating functions of the Country Office (CO), supporting the CoM in identifying IOM-relevant project opportunities, developing the country strategy and project proposals and liaising with government counterparts, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), and other development partners, as necessary.

**Responsibilities**

**Institutional and Operational Set-Up**

1. Supervise and guide the implementation of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) activities of the CO according to projects/ programmes/strategy result matrices and M&E plans, in close coordination with the Project/Programme Managers and other relevant IOM staff and partners.
2. Ensure adherence to existing Evaluation and Monitoring policies and guidelines and Results-Based Management (RBM) roadmaps, frameworks and guidance, including proper use of Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) for monitoring, reporting and evaluation.
3. Contribute, in collaboration with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer, to the development of plans, tools and systems to monitor implementation of projects/programmes and/or strategies within the CO focusing on activities, results, expenditure, budget, risks and assumptions, in line with donor/UNCT requirements, IOM strategies, and institutional M&E and reporting requirements.
4. Ensure that risks are assessed and new ones identified during the regular monitoring of project activities, and where appropriate ensure that associated Project Risk Register Matrix and Risk Treatment plans are monitored and regularly reviewed.
5. Provide substantive inputs to strengthen the capacity of IOM staff and partners to carry out M&E activities in the CO through training, mentoring, and coaching.
6. Regularly update the evaluation and monitoring plans for projects/programmes/strategies at the CO, including identification of key performance questions, indicators, and parameters for monitoring and evaluating performance in line with the Strategic Results Framework (SRF), and share the evaluation plan with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer on a regular basis.
7. Actively engage in M&E activities for and with UN Agencies, UNCT, donors, government and external partners at country level, including on possible joint monitoring and evaluations, for instance in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Evaluation.
8. Document good practices and lessons learned through analysis of monitoring findings and evaluation reports, identify causes of potential bottlenecks and corrective measures, and facilitate discussion of related M&E and RBM findings and challenges with relevant IOM project staff, management, and partners.
9. Facilitate regular feedback from beneficiaries and stakeholders on activities and services provided through the organization’s support, in close coordination with field units and relevant focal points of CO.

**Reporting and Communication**

1. Support Project/Programme Managers in compiling periodic donor reports in line with the M&E plans and agreed reporting schedules, as well as the CoM/ Head of Office (HoO) in compiling data for UNCT reporting requirements.
2. Provide comprehensive inputs for materials requested by the UNCT/ Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) or individual agencies, Government institutions, Donors, IOM relevant Units at HQs, RO and/or other partners.
3. Monitor the work of Implementing Partners (IPs) by receiving and reviewing progress reports in a timely manner as per agreement with IOM, UN and donors' terms and conditions.
4. Provide technical support to IP to improve the quality of data collection, consolidation, analysis, and reporting through capacity building and regular monitoring visits to the field.
5. Support the CO’s communication strategy through documenting IOM activities such as capturing case studies, life-changing stories for donor/UN reports, updating CO’s social media accounts, and producing quarterly newsletters and local media briefings.
6. Contribute to the preparation of meetings and events, to include donor/UN briefings, donor visits, and conferences.
7. Manage submissions for the IOM global institutional reporting processes, including the Institutional Questionnaire.
8. Conduct M&E activities that can contribute to the management and analysis of migration trends and related data relevant for IOM in the country.

**Project Development Support**

1. Contribute to the identification of new project development opportunities in close coordination with CoM, Project/Programme Managers, and RO’s Thematic Specialists, and in line with IOM global frameworks and CO’s strategy.
2. Provide inputs for the development of project/programme logic, including Results Matrices and Theory of Change, and for the monitoring and evaluation sections of project proposals/strategies.
3. Ensure that adequate monitoring and evaluation costs are budgeted and advocated for as per IOM M&E policies, guidelines, and Project Handbook.
4. Participate in UN, donor, sectoral, working groups, and other meetings aimed at development of new projects, for instance within Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) regional and national networks.
5. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in project/strategy conceptualisation, development, monitoring, reporting and evaluation;
- Experience in capacity-building activities, including design and delivery of trainings;
- Experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities as well as with national and international institutions;
- Demonstrated experience and familiarity in financial and business administration;
- Proven understanding and experience of internal and international migration issues in the country and in the region;
- Experience in organizing consultations, workshops and seminars with high-level stakeholders;
- In-depth knowledge and experience of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and techniques including qualitative and quantitative methods, participatory approaches, and evaluative methodologies; and,
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of UN and bilateral donor programming and institutional requirements.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated writing and research skills;
- Excellent communication and analytical skills;
- High degree of judgment and initiative, ability to work with a high degree of independence within assigned areas;
- Demonstrated interpersonal and teamwork skills; and,
- Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with people of diverse cultural and national backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Career Development Specialist, NVPPA
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Program Background:**

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which the International Rescue Committee (IRC) serves newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal. NVPPA operates alongside other federally funded programs, such as initial resettlement services and Matching Grant, and is designed to complement rather than replace or duplicate these programs.

**Job Overview**

The Career Development Specialist is the participant's primary point of contact in the program, working remotely with refugees across the country by phone, video, and online tools. From intake and eligibility verification through an approved Professional Advancement Plan (PAP), this position guides each participant toward their career goal, whether that means finding a training partner, completing credential evaluation and recertification, or moving forward with an approved vehicle purchase. The role coordinates closely with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, administrative and job development staff, and external resettlement partners to ensure participants move smoothly between services, while maintaining accurate case records and documentation in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) in line with ORR reporting requirements and IRC financial controls.

**Major responsibilities:**

**Outreach and Intake**

- Conduct virtual outreach, intake, and enrollment for eligible participants, including verifying eligibility documentation.
- Coordinate with IRC offices, resettlement agencies, and local partners to identify and connect with eligible participants.

**Career Navigation**

- Complete a skills assessment with each participant and develop an individualized Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) that defines their career goal, pathway, and planned use of direct financial assistance.
- Review the PAP with each participant, provide feedback on the career goal, and confirm that proposed use of funds meets ORR eligible-use requirements.
- Provide ongoing navigation by phone and video to help participants access training, credential evaluation and recertification, and other approved supports.
- Research career advancement, certification, and vocational education opportunities across state and local labor markets.
- Connect participants to resources and services within IRC and in their local communities.
- Maintain working knowledge of credential evaluation services and state licensing requirements in high-demand fields, and carry a caseload of participants pursuing those pathways.

**Coordination**

- Work with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, Administrative Staff, and Job Development staff so participants move smoothly between navigation, training, and placement services, and to ensure financial assistance requests align with approved PAPs.
- Coordinate with other service providers, including PIR providers and Matching Grant employment specialists, to support co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Compliance**

- Maintain accurate, timely case files in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO), including documentation and the service and outcome data required for ORR reporting.
- Ensure documentation for each financial assistance request is complete before submission, consistent with IRC financial controls.

**Job Requirements (Simplified)**

- 1-2 years of demonstrated experience in a human services field, preferably in a nonprofit or social services setting.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build rapport with clients by phone and video.
- Ability to deliver services remotely to clients across states and time zones, protect client confidentiality and sensitive documents, and work independently as part of a fully virtual team.
- Experience managing a high-volume caseload, with strong organization, prioritization, time management, and follow-through.
- Ability to build and maintain productive internal and external relationships.
- Ability to research and navigate workforce, education, and social service systems in unfamiliar local markets.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office, video conferencing, and remote collaboration tools, and with tracking and reporting information in a database.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients.
- Fluency in spoken and written English.

**Preferred**

- Undergraduate degree in Social Work or a related field
- Experience in workforce development, career coaching, or case management.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant.
- Experience with Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways.
- Fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $19-$28/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Assistant Safety Advisor – Syria (national staff only)
body:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO Syria**

The Syria program supports more than 290 NGOs delivering urgently needed aid and assistance to an estimated 13.1 million people across the country. First launched as an emergency response operation in 2014, INSO Syria has grown to become a program covering all Syrian governorates, with a Country Office in Damascus. The Syria conflict is unique and complex: you will find that every day is different and there is always more to learn.

**Job Summary**

Under the direct supervision of the Safety Advisor, you will collect and verify information and enter data into CHDC. You will assist the SA and the Deputy SA with the development and management of a local information network and provide liaison with NGOs using INSO services in the region.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Develop a diversified and consistent network of contacts at the communal and regional levels.
- Develop, verify, and summarise safety and security information in a concise and actionable format. Enter the information into CHDC.
- Proactively ensure daily liaison with field monitors and submit requests for information to deadlines.
- Assist the SA and the Deputy SA in the preparation of relevant reports, area assessments, and other INSO products.
- Assist the SA and the Deputy in visualising and analysing data by using charts and mapping tools.
- Help to enhance INSO information collection capacity in the region.
- Act at short notice with due regard to developing events.
- Ensure strict compliance with INSO HR, financial, and logistics procedures.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**

- Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in security analysis, humanitarian coordination, or information management.
- Strong analytical and report-writing skills.
- Ability to produce clear, concise written products in English.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel required).
- Strong Arabic and English language skills (spoken and written).
- Prior field assessment experience is an asset.
- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Security Studies, or a related field.

*Nice to Have:*

- Experience with databases or incident tracking systems.

**Core Competencies**

- Professionalism – Demonstrates neutrality, integrity, and ethical conduct in all interactions and responsibilities.
- Organisation – Manages time, priorities, and workloads effectively to ensure efficient task delivery.
- Resilience – Maintains performance and composure while working under pressure and tight deadlines.
- Accuracy – Ensures close attention to detail and precision in work, documentation, and processes.
- Communication – Builds positive relationships and communicates clearly and effectively with diverse stakeholders.

The successful candidate must demonstrate:

- Commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Political neutrality and impartiality.
- Integrity and professionalism.
- Respectful engagement with colleagues and partners.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable fixed-term contract, 1.75 working days annual leave per month, private health insurance coverage or allowance.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

title: Project Manager, Cairo Culinary Training Programme - DAPP (55219)
body:
**THE ORGANISATION**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation/charity/non-profit that advances children's rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children's rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won't stop until we are all equal.

Plan International started working in Egypt in 1981 and has a presence in ten of the 27 governorates in which the country including Greater Cairo, Alexandria, Giza, Beheira, Kalyoubia, Damietta, Qena, Assuit and Sohag. Plan international Egypt implements programmes designed to enable communities to improve the lives of the most marginalised children and their families. Plan Egypt's Country Strategy focuses on five strategic objectives.

Through a five-interconnected, gender transformative and context-fit country objectives, PIE intends along with the various stakeholders at all levels to continue delivering positive and transformative changes so that "Children, especially girls, and young people grow up in an enabling environment, realizing their rights and contributing in both development and humanitarian settings as active agents of change".

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

You will be responsible for the overall management, planning, implementation and successful delivery of the Youth Inclusion and Employment Project (YIEP) - Cairo Culinary Training Programme. Working in collaboration with local partners and the Melting Pot Foundation (MPF), you will lead all phases of the project management cycle to ensure the achievement of project outcomes, donor compliance and Plan International minimum standards. You will bridge the gap between Cairo's hospitality sector demand and the limited access young people have to quality training by ensuring the delivery of competency-based culinary training, structured internships and employment pathways. Further, you will be accountable for achieving the project's target of reaching 200 young people, with at least 50% female participation and a 90% employment rate.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Contribute to the initiation of the project idea in line with the country strategy and identification of project potential local partner(s).
- Ensure realistic project design, lead due diligence with cross-department input, and coordinate gender-transformative scope with partners and advisors.
- Analyze context, risks, and resource needs, manage pre-start-up activities, confirm partners, and integrate safeguarding for children and youth with budgeted mitigation actions.
- Set project governance with partners, develops a detailed implementation plan covering risks, resources, and budgets, and collaborates with leadership to launch the project internally and externally.
- Lead project implementation within agreed frameworks and timelines, coordinate technical support and resources. With partners, this role will oversee delivery, monitoring, and evaluation, address deviations and risks while optimizing daily operations across logistics, finance, and HR.
- Ensure accurate reporting, timely procurement and payments, budget control, and realignment when needed. Core responsibilities include achieving gender-transformative results and integrating safeguarding and PSHEA risk mitigation into all activities.
- Ensure proper project closure by reviewing achievements with partners, finalize activities, completing procurements and payments, and manage staff transitions in line with guidelines and laws.
- Lead final evaluations, coordinates audits, prepare comprehensive reports for internal and donor stakeholders, close project records, and establishe institutional memory through systematic archiving and knowledge management.
- Model Plan International’s values, lead a motivated team, ensure clarity of objectives, manage tasks and staff development, enforce compliance with policies, oversee monitoring and resource use, and strengthen partner capacity to achieve project goals effectively.
- Ensure partner-aligned data systems for monitoring and future design, embed PSHEA policies with staff accountability, and support due diligence for compliance.
- Plan International has a robust global policy for Safeguarding and Gender Equality and Inclusion standards, ensuring staff and associates within your scope strictly comply with these principles and guidelines.
- You will be trusted to take on additional assignments within the scope of work as assigned by your supervisor on need basis.

**What we are looking for:**

- Someone with knowledge and experience in project management.
- Someone knowledgeable on project cycle management best practice.
- Should have experience in working with partner organisations (co-creating and mutual oversight).
- Someone knowledgeable and experienced in project budgeting, activities and expenditure monitoring.
- Should have knowledge and experience in M&E activities tracking, evaluation and reporting.
- Should have understanding of human resources management and procedures.
- Someone with understanding of procurement processes and supply chain management.
- Should have experience of managing people/teams.
- Someone with good working knowledge of donor compliance.
- Should have strong planning and organisational skills.
- Ability to prioritise his/her workload and project team workload.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
- Excellent influencing, communication, strong negotiation skills and facilitation skills.
- Ability to act as part of a multi-disciplinary team.
- Should have strong collaboration skills, able to build cooperation and negotiate compromises.
- Ability to build and maintain strong working internal and external relationships.
- Should be able to deliver projects with partners on agreed timelines, ensuring quality through joint evaluation systems.
- Highly positive, proactive, and results-focused.
- Degree in Business administration, management or related academic background.
- Microsoft office skills (Word, Power Point, Excel, Outlook) and able to use project management software.

**Please respond to the requirements of this role in your cover letter.**  
**Only applications in English language will be accepted.**

**Location: On site working and the role is based at Cairo**

**Reports to: Country Director**

**Job Grade: Hay Level 16**

**Vacancy advert closing Date: 13th November 2026**

**This vacancy is subject to availability of funding and is open to Egypt nationals only**

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**Disclaimer: Plan International is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on any basis. We also do not charge Job seekers any fees at any point of the recruitment process.**

title: Business & Human Rights Legal Adviser
body:
***Note: This position is contingent upon funding approval.***

**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a BHR Legal Adviser to join our team. The BHR Legal Adviser is GRC’s in-country legal lead for the programme in Cambodia. The role will work closely with Cambodian trade unions, civil society organisations, and legal aid centres to turn worker-reported evidence into effective routes to remedy.

The role combines legal research and analysis on Cambodian and international routes to remedy; hands-on support to partners on monitoring and documentation for legal aid centres, and engagement with suppliers, international brands and government stakeholders. Furthermore the role will design and deliver training, contribute to advocacy objectives and help the team track and report on program results.

**Full / Part-time:** Fixed-term contract (2 years)

**Location:** Phnom Penh (with regular domestic travel)

**The Role:**

- Support and contribute to the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration, consistent with strategic priorities.
- Support trade union and CSO partners to collect, verify and use worker-reported data on labour rights violations.
- Support partners in analysing monitoring data to identify patterns, priority cases and systemic issues.
- Translate documented cases into legal briefs, complaints, supplier and brand engagement and advocacy outputs.
- Conduct legal research and jurisprudence reviews on Cambodian routes to remedy, including the Labour Law, the Trade Union Law, the Arbitration Council, Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training dispute resolution and inspection processes.
- Link international and regional business and human rights standards and international due diligence laws and forced labour import bans to Cambodian compliance mechanisms.
- Review and draft legal briefs, submissions and accountability tools on business-related labour rights violations, access to remedy, documentation and investigation.
- Provide legal guidance to legal aid centres and partner lawyers on case strategy.
- Coordinate day-to-day with trade union and CSO partners and support their capacity on legal and documentation work.
- Engage suppliers, international brands and government stakeholders, including through brand grievance mechanisms and multi-stakeholder initiatives.
- Plan and deliver launch events, roundtables, briefings and other advocacy activities.
- Design and deliver workshops, training courses and mentorship for workers, union representatives, legal aid staff and other stakeholders in Khmer and English.
- Ensure materials are practical, gender-responsive and adapted to the local context.
- Make regular visits to legal aid centres to meet field staff and workers and support casework and monitoring.
- Apply do-no-harm principles across all activities, including informed consent, protecting the identities of workers and union members and secure handling of personal data.
- Monitor retaliation and security risks to workers, partners and staff, and escalate concerns promptly under GRC’s safeguarding and security policies.
- Support GRC’s team to collect and track data against the program’s indicators and contribute to narrative reports, workplans and other donor-requested materials.
- Bring local context, stakeholder insight and knowledge of administrative procedures to team planning.
- Work closely with GRC colleagues across a multicultural, partly remote team to deliver on time.

**Your Background**

- 6+ years of experience in labour rights, business and human rights, or related legal practice.
- Qualified with a law degree, LLM or other postgraduate qualification in human rights, labour or international law or equivalent is desirable.
- Strong working knowledge of Cambodian labour law and dispute resolution.
- Knowledge of international labour rights and business and human rights frameworks and how they apply to the garment and apparel sector.
- Practical experience working with trade unions, civil society organisations, businesses and government institutions on labour rights or corporate accountability.
- Demonstrated understanding of the risks facing workers and union representatives in Cambodia and experience working safely and confidentially in a sensitive environment.
- Experience designing and delivering training and workshops.
- Experience applying gender-responsive approaches, including on gender-based violence and harassment at work.
- Proactive and practical, anticipates problems, proposes solutions and can break a strategy down into workable steps.
- Flexible and willing to support deliverables beyond the core remit when needed.
- Well organised and able to manage competing urgent demands.
- Fluency in English and Khmer, both written and verbal skills.
- Admission to the Bar Association of the Kingdom of Cambodia is desirable.
- Experience with worker-led monitoring, documentation or investigations including handling sensitive data is desirable.
- Experience working on donor-funded projects, including activity planning, indicator tracking, narrative reporting and coordination across multiple partners is desirable.
- Experience engaging with international garment brands, suppliers and other business actors on labour rights violations, remediation and human rights due diligence is desirable.
- Familiarity with brand grievance mechanisms, multi-stakeholder initiatives and due diligence laws is desirable.
- Access to Cambodian legal databases and repositories is desirable.

title: Finance Analyst - Field Reporting, Compliance and Cost Allocation
body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As Finance Analyst - Field Reporting, Compliance and Cost Allocation, you will independently deliver complex Field Office compliance and Cost Allocation analysis. You will apply professional judgment to investigate material exceptions, determine analytical approaches, recommend corrective actions, and coordinate resolution across Field Offices, Regional Finance, Shared Services, and GFSC teams. You will also lead defined improvements and emerging Compliance and Cost Allocation project workstreams.

**CORE COST ALLOCATION WORK**

You will independently perform and coordinate Cost Allocation operations and analysis, including validating allocation results, accounting codes, and transactions; reviewing support-cost actuals against budgets; investigating exceptions and root causes; coordinating required adjustments; and supporting office onboarding or transitions to centralized Cost Allocation processes. You will apply policy and accounting requirements, escalate material or unresolved risks, and recommend sustainable controls and process improvements.

**FIELD OFFICE FINANCIAL REPORTING AND COMPLIANCE**

You will conduct risk-based, in-depth reviews of Field, Regional, and Offsite Office financial reports, including bank reconciliations, staff advances, balance sheets, and other priority compliance areas. You will analyse trends and recurring issues, assess exceptions, recommend corrective actions, and monitor resolution with relevant stakeholders.

**REPORTING, DATA MANAGEMENT AND PROCESS IMPROVEMENT**

You will design, enhance, and maintain financial reports, templates, dashboards, and data controls using Power BI (PBI), PMQA, advanced Excel, SharePoint, approved AI-enabled tools, and other authorized reporting and analytics technologies. You will reconcile and validate data, define business requirements, test outputs, document controls, and identify automation and standardization opportunities. You will apply AI tools responsibly for data preparation, exception identification, documentation, draft insights, and process improvement, ensuring professional review, validation, and compliance with organizational data-security requirements.

**STAKEHOLDER GUIDANCE, CAPABILITY BUILDING AND ISSUE RESOLUTION**

You will serve as a technical resource for Field Offices, Regional Finance, Shared Services, and GFSC teams on compliance and Cost Allocation matters. You will explain analytical findings and policy implications, facilitate issue resolution, prepare guidance and training materials, and deliver targeted orientations and knowledge-sharing sessions.

**EMERGING PROJECTS: COMPLIANCE AND COST ALLOCATION**

You will lead defined workstreams or make significant analytical contributions to emerging Compliance and Cost Allocation projects. You will clarify scope and requirements, assess risks and dependencies, develop analyses or prototypes, coordinate testing and implementation, report progress, and document decisions, lessons learned, and handover requirements.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
- Minimum 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in finance, accounting, financial reporting, compliance, Cost Allocation, audit support or a related analytical role.
- Experience resolving cross-functional issues and recommending process or control improvements.
- Experience working in a multicultural, geographically dispersed or shared-services environment.
- Experience with SunSystems, OLAP, data warehouse or data-modelling environments, Power Apps and Power Automate.
- Experience supporting centralised Cost Allocation operations, Field Office finance, policy implementation, project workstreams, user acceptance testing or change adoption.
- Experience developing or improving financial templates, reports, dashboards, procedures or training materials.
- Professional accounting certification is preferred but not required. Equivalent relevant professional training or demonstrated expertise may be considered, subject to P&C requirements.
- Strong knowledge of financial accounting, reporting, reconciliations, internal controls and Cost Allocation principles.
- Demonstrated ability to perform complex analysis, identify material risks, connect issues across data sources, and develop practical recommendations.
- Strong Excel skills and working capability with Power BI or similar reporting tools.

title: Head of Monitoring, Research, Primate Habituation, One Health and Forest Department.
Resilience & Humanitarian Systems Manager - Manila (Filipino Nationals Only)
body:
Duration : **12 months**  
Start date : **ASAP**

## **You'll contribute to ending world hunger by ...**

- Strengthening Action Against Hunger's technical leadership and positioning in Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Shock-Responsive Social Protection (SRSP), Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), and Resilient Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL)
- Ensure the quality, coherence, accountability, and effectiveness of resilience and humanitarian programmes through technical guidance, capacity strengthening, learning, innovation, and compliance with organizational and sectoral standards
- Lead the development, implementation, and coordination of integrated resilience and humanitarian action while collaborating with internal departments, government institutions, donors, and partners to achieve Action Against Hunger Philippines' strategic objectives

## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Strategic Leadership and Programme Development**

- Contribute actively to the definition and implementation of the country strategy and resilience roadmap
- Develop and update technical strategies, frameworks, and approaches related to DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL in line with policies and country priorities in coordination with other technical departments
- Monitor humanitarian, climate, socio-economic, and policy context and trends to inform programme design and strategic positioning
- Support Country Director and Deputy Country Director in donor mapping, partnership identification and development, resource mobilization, and identification of funding opportunities
- Promote innovative, integrated, and evidence-based approaches that strengthen resilience and humanitarian preparedness and response

**Objective 2: Programme Quality, Technical Support, Reorting and Implementation**

- Lead and oversee assessments, analyses, and programme design processes related to resilience and humanitarian programming in coordination with other departments and field offices
- Provide technical guidance to field teams to ensure the relevance, quality, and effectiveness of DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL interventions
- Ensure programmes comply with standards, donor requirements, humanitarian principles, and sector best practices
- Support the development of high-quality proposals, budgets, technical narratives, and implementation plans
- Ensure timely submission of mission reports in accordance with internal and external reporting systems
- Strengthen integrated approaches by mainstreaming gender, protection, accountability, environment, nutrition, and inclusion across programmes in coordination with other departments
- Anticipate operational and technical challenges and support teams in identifying timely solutions
- Participate and support regular project review meetings and follow through sector specific action plans and agreements
- Support CD and DCD budget oversight of on-going resilience programs

**Objective 3: Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning, and Knowledge Management**

- Ensure the collection, consolidation, analysis, and use of programme data to support evidence-based decision-making and programme improvement
- Support the development of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) systems and resilience indicators
- Lead learning reviews, technical workshops, evaluations, and knowledge-sharing initiatives
- Monitor changes in disaster, climate, food security, livelihood, and social protection contexts to inform programme adaptation
- Document and disseminate best practices, lessons learned, and technical guidance across the mission

**Objective 4: Representation, Coordination, and External Engagement**

- Establish and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, academic institutions, private sector actors, and community stakeholders
- Represent in relevant coordination platforms, clusters, technical working groups, and resilience forums
- Contribute to donor reports, technical updates, and internal reporting requirements
- Facilitate effective coordination between programme teams, support departments, and field offices
- Promote technical leadership and visibility in resilience and humanitarian programming
- Function as lead of assigned consortia project within the sector

**Objective 5: Team Leadership, HR management and Capacity Strengthening**

- Provide leadership, supervision, and technical support to resilience and humanitarian programme staff
- Lead workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, coaching, and professional development of assigned team members
- Strengthen technical capacities in DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL through training, mentoring, and knowledge exchange
- Ensure clear roles, effective communication, and collaboration across teams and departments
- Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, learning, punctuality and continuous improvement
- Ensure the fostering of conducive working relationships within the team, and a collaborative environment for the project

**Objective 6: Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Security Compliance**

- Provide technical leadership during emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, rapid response, and recovery operations
- Support contingency planning, scenario analysis, emergency assessments, and response planning in coordination with Humanitarian Action Manager
- Ensure programme implementation considers operational and security risks and complies with security policies and procedures and timely communication with designated staff
- Coordinate with Heads of Base, Security Focal Points, and Logistics teams to maintain safe programme implementation
- Ensure timely reporting of security incidents and compliance with mission security protocols by all supervised staff and immediately report incidents to the Logistics Coordinator and Country Director
- Support business continuity and operational readiness Action Against Hunger’s team and offices in coordination with Humanitarian Action Manager

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- Advance or Bachelor's degree in either Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change Adaptation, Agriculture, Economics, Development Studies, Earth Science, Environmental Science, Social Protection, Humanitarian Action, or a related field.
- Strong expertise related to Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Shock-Responsive Social Protection (SRSP), Anticipatory Action (AA), Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), Rapid Response Mechanisms (RRM), Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA), or Emergency Response Management is an advantage.
- Demonstrated experience in resilience programming, emergency preparedness and response, and humanitarian-development nexus approaches.
- Knowledge of social protection systems, cash and voucher assistance, market systems analysis, and livelihood resilience programming.
- Expertise in vulnerability, risk, capacity, and needs assessments, including participatory and community-based approaches.
- Experience in developing anticipatory action frameworks, contingency planning, early warning-early action systems, and forecast-based interventions.
- Strong understanding of climate risk analysis, adaptation strategies, and resilience-building approaches for vulnerable communities.
- Expertise in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL), knowledge management, and evidence generation.
- Strong proposal development, donor engagement, project design, and resource mobilization skills.
- Knowledge of gender-responsive, inclusive, and protection-sensitive programming approaches.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement, coordination, representation, and partnership-building skills.
- At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience in resilience, humanitarian, disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, social protection, emergency response, or food security and livelihoods programming.
- At least 3 years in a management or technical leadership role within an INGO, UN agency, government institution, or development organization.
- Proven experience managing programs related to DRR, CCA, SRSP, AA, MPCA, RRM, and FSL in disaster-prone, climate-vulnerable, conflict-affected, or fragile contexts.
- Demonstrated experience leading emergency preparedness, rapid response, humanitarian recovery interventions and humanitarian coordination system in the Philippines.
- Previous experience working with government agencies, local authorities, humanitarian clusters, social protection systems, and development partners.
- Experience designing and managing multi-sectoral programs integrating livelihoods, nutrition, social protection, and resilience outcomes.
- Proven experience in project design, donor reporting, budget management, and grant management.
- Experience working with vulnerable and marginalized populations, including remote and hard-to-reach communities.
- Previous experience in the Philippines or Southeast Asia is an advantage.
- Experience managing diverse technical teams and providing coaching, mentoring, and capacity strengthening.
- Understanding conflict and security context in the Philippines
- Fluent in English and Filipino
- Full literacy with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Access, etc), GIS (advantageous), Full familiarity with Windows OS, Kobo and other data management software an advantage
- National and to be deployed during emergency in the field
- Regular field visits to follow-up ongoing projects and support project teams
- Opportunity to work in different contexts, e.g. urban and rural, remote and volatile contexts
- Valuable prior experience in issues related to the promotion of gender equality or personal commitment to gender equality

## **Our remuneration package:**

- Compensation: based on Action Against Hunger grid
