title: Officer, Events and Entertainment Relations Engagement
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**IRC UK**  
IRC UK is part of the IRC global network, which has its global headquarters in New York. Our team in the UK works to raise profile, deliver policy and practice change, and increase funding to help restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Since 2021, IRC UK has also provided integration services directly to refugees in England.  
In Europe, the IRC also has offices in Berlin, Bonn, Brussels, Geneva and Stockholm.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Experiential Marketing Team—working across the Marketing & Mobilization (M&M) Team and the UK Communications Team—this role is primarily responsible for elevating the IRC’s profile, brand, and influence, while supporting fundraising efforts. This will be achieved through event support, strategic engagement of celebrity ambassadors and digital tactics. In alignment with our Strategy100 commitments and the UK strategic plan, the position will deliver event production and talent-focused strategies that enhance the impact of IRC campaigns, initiatives, and appeals.

**Scope and Authority**

- Oversee the UK and European market events portfolio with flexibility to support other priority markets on a case-by-case basis as directed by leadership
- Lead and oversee various aspects of event project management (in-person and virtual), including team coordination, logistics, production, and execution from planning through post-event wrap-up. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

\- Drafting concept notes

\- Creating creative briefs

\- Conducting venue/vendor searches or setting up virtual platforms

\- Collaborating with various teams to align on event messaging and donor engagement strategies

\- Preparing and distributing event materials, communications, and other professional documents

\- Evaluating event effectiveness and analyzing audience data

- Assist on management of a global entertainment relations portfolio  
    \- Help identify and create opportunities to leverage existing talent in support of events and digital campaigns that advance the IRC’s fundraising, brand and advocacy goals (listed in order of priority)  
    \- Support Director with IRC’s celebrity supporters by managing ongoing communications to keep them informed, engaged, and aligned with IRC’s mission.
- Support in proactively identifying current events and cultural trends to leverage events and celebrity partners to meaningfully engage in support of IRC initiatives and events.
- Be available for occasional travel and work outside of standard hours, including evenings or weekends, to attend meetings or events.

**Key Working Relationships**

Ability to work effectively and creatively with a diverse array of external and internal collaborators in a way that represents the best of the IRC. These include IRC Fundraising, Policy & Advocacy, Digital and Media teams, as well as Celebrity representatives and contacts.

Strong social skills and project management skills, with emphasis on creating tangible outcomes. Ability to thrive in an fast-paced environment, to be flexible, to work across various internal teams and manage high-profile stakeholders.

Eager to learn about the entertainment industry and build meaningful relationships to help continue growing talent relations.

**Person Specification**

**Experience**

- Strong experience in event planning with the ability to organize events through all phases of development.
- Knowledge and experience of using social media channels as part of celebrity engagement and PR campaigns.
- Demonstrable experience of working strategically, identifying opportunities to support organisation-wide marketing strategies.

**Skills**

- Proven ability to project manage campaigns and events; working with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.
- Outstanding written and oral communication skills, and the ability to interact with a diverse range of people. In this post this would include senior leadership, celebrities, agents and journalists.
- Excellent relationship management skills.
- Exceptional judgement, analytical and prioritizing skills and experience of applying these in a fast-moving environment.
- Proven ability to take responsibility for tasks and act on own initiative particularly to solve problems and find solutions.
- Outstanding MS office and Event database management skills (Salesforce and Pardot, aka Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, experience preferred).

Candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

**Compensation:** (GBP46,780 - GBP57922.78 GBP/Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

IRC UK strives to be an equal opportunities employer. IRC UK is committed to equality of opportunity and to non-discrimination for all job applicants and employees, and we seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce regardless of gender, race, religious beliefs, nationality, ethnic/national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.  
  
IRC UK welcomes applications from all candidates, including underrepresented groups and refugees who have the right to work in the UK.

  
IRC UK will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application and/or interview process, and for essential job functions if appointed to a role. Please contact us if you may need such adjustments.   
  
If you have any questions or need assistance with the online recruitment process, please contact the IRC UK HR team at applications@rescue-uk.org

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Project Officer- Laos
International Migration Data Governance Specialist
body:
## **Job Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

The consultancy contributes to the the ‘Awda Amina Phase II: Strengthening Miration Governance in Iraq’ project funded by the European Union and to the ‘Strengthening Data Systems to Improve the Managament of Internally Displaced Persons Referral Systems in Iraq’ project funded by the United Nations Internal Displacement Solutions Fund.   
Under the overall guidance of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil) and the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), The consultant will provide specialized technical support and policy-development support to IOM staff working on migration and displacement data governance initiatives under the project portfolio. The consultant will draft technical and policy documents under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and support technical consultations, workshops, framework development, implementation tracking, and reporting activities, identify technical and policy challenges, and provide recommendations for consideration by the Programme Officer (DTM and Research). All managerial, representational, and decision-making functions shall remain the responsibility of IOM staff.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
The consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil).

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**Data ownership and access**

  
i. Support the development a structured framework that outlines roles, responsibilities and processes for managing migration and displacement data across government ministries and agencies, in both Federal Iraq and KRI.  
ii. Provide technical support and draft clear guidelines for data ownership, access, sharing and utilisation, complying with national policies and promoting adherence with international best practices in terms of data protection.  
iii. Under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and in consultation with relevant IOM staff, the consultant will provide technical input and draft documentation for consideration by IOM in relation to:  
 i) Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between relevant ministries and the Central Statistical Office; and  
 ii) data-sharing protocols between Federal and KRG authorities aimed at enhancing collaboration and access to migration-related data.  
iv. Draft a Data Integration Framework and provide technical recommendations regarding its implementation under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), to establish links with the National Referral Mechanism and enable seamless data flow by connecting the digital infrastructure for migration management.

**Data standards**

  
v. Draft a national framework for migration and displacement-related statistical definitions and concepts aligned with international/UN recommendations and standards, integrating inputs from consultations led by IOM staff with relevant national and international partners.  
vi. Develop technical data guidelines and standardized indicators to ensure consistency and comparability across different governmental agencies in the operationalization of agreed definitions.

**Data analysis and use**

  
vii. Utilize secondary data analysis to inform and enhance policy development and facilitate Iraq's participation in international migration data forums.  
viii. Develop recommendations for improved data analysis and reporting on migration and displacement by relevant Ministries, supporting evidence-based policy formulation.  
ix. Prepare briefing materials and provide technical support to IOM staff for intra- and inter-ministerial workshops led by IOM staff.Draft recommendations, publication schedules, and other technical documents to facilitate the publishing of periodic statistics on government-owned websites to ensure public availability of migration data.

**Other**  
x. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

• Agreed outputs set out in the ToRs are delivered in a timely manner and to a satisfactory quality standard.  
• Technical outputs produced by the consultant result in measurable improvements in data governance practices.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

• Master’s degree in law, economics, political science, public policy, demography/statistics, or a related field with at least five years of relevant professional experience, or Bachelor’s degree with seven years of professional experience.  
• Proven experience in migration data governance through previous work with government bodies, international organizations or think tanks.  
• Familiarity with international statistical standards such as the International Recommendations on IDP Statistics and the Recommendations on Statistics of International Migration and Temporary.  
• Familiarity with IOM’s Data Protection Principles and with othe international data protection frameworks and best practices.  
• Familiarity with the Iraqi context and government institutions.  
• Strong writing and communication skills; experience in facilitating multi-stakeholder workshops and in drafting policy framework, guidelines and technical standards.  
• Fluency in Arabic and English.

**Languages**

For this consultancy, excellent command of English is required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

Yes

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: Senior Data Analyst
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Candidate Verification Step:** As part of our application process, candidates are asked to complete a brief verification exercise. This will involves In place of a cover letter, please complete a short data task. Download donors.csv and gifts.csv from [https://github.com/neilcuz/recruitment](https://github.com/neilcuz/recruitment) and use any tool you like (SQL, Python, R or similar) to answer the three multiple-choice questions there. It should take less time than writing a traditional cover letter. Upload a Word document (.docx) in the cover letter field containing only your answers, one per line, in this format:

- Q1: A
- Q2: B
- Q3: C

**Why we’re asking:** This step helps us confirm that every applicant is a real person and keeps the selection process fair for all candidates. It is not part of your skills assessment, and it will take only a few minutes.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The External Relations (ER) department was created in February 2020 and is comprised of 3 main but complementary functional areas: Private fundraising, Communications and Advocacy. The ER department is at the beginning stages of creating a radical and ambitious global strategy that will enhance IRC’s ability to ‘punch above its weight’ in private income, advocacy, and brand awareness. The main objective of the department is to enable this organization of more than 12,000 staff to have the resources needed to continue serving 18 million people worldwide in places affected by war and disaster, shape the humanitarian sector by influencing key policies and reforms, and build and grow IRC’s reputation.

We are looking for an experienced and highly analytical Senior Data Analyst to join our team, with a primary focus on supporting our Philanthropy and High Value fundraising teams. As a Senior Analyst within our Global Analytics team, you will play a pivotal role in supporting and driving data-driven insights for our fundraising efforts across the globe.

You will leverage your expertise in data analysis, statistical modeling, and reporting to guide the strategic decisions of our fundraising initiatives, ensuring that we continue to meet and exceed our goals. This position offers the opportunity to work closely with cross-functional teams, including fundraising, marketing, and finance, to deliver actionable insights that enhance donor engagement and maximize fundraising outcomes.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Data Analysis & Reporting:
    - Analyze and interpret large datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and insights that inform global fundraising strategies.
    - Create and maintain dashboards, visualizations, and reports to track fundraising performance and donor engagement metrics.
    - Develop and deliver regular performance reports to key stakeholders, highlighting actionable insights and areas of opportunity for growth.
    - Develop comprehensive data models and reports for external benchmarking to assess performance against peers and identify opportunities for new investments.
- Strategic Insights & Recommendations:
    - Collaborate with senior leadership to translate analytical findings into strategic recommendations for improving fundraising effectiveness.
    - Provide insights that influence global fundraising campaigns, donor retention strategies, and personalized donor experiences.
- Stakeholder Collaboration:
    - Act as the main analytics partner to the Philanthropy and High Value teams, building trusted relationships, understanding their priorities and building strong business knowledge of how these teams operate.
    - Work closely with cross-functional teams (e.g., fundraising, marketing, and finance) to ensure data-driven decisions are integrated into the global strategy.
    - Present findings to senior management, explaining complex data insights in a clear and actionable manner.
- Process Improvement & Innovation:
    - Identify opportunities to enhance the data collection and reporting processes, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with global goals.
    - Keep abreast of industry trends and emerging analytics tools, and bring innovative ideas for improving the team’s capabilities.
    - Acting as a technical leader, collaborate with fellow Analytics colleagues to ensure best practices in coding, statistics, and general analysis.
- Work with integrity and accountability to the “IRC Way” – IRC Global Standards for Professional Conduct.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

**Experience**

- 3+ years working in the field of data analytics.
- Proven experience with advanced data analytics tools (e.g., SQL, Python, R, Tableau, Power BI) and data visualization platforms.
- Demonstrable experience planning and executing complex analytics projects across multiple stakeholders.

**Skills & Competencies**

- More than two years of professional experience with SQL and relational databases.
- Knowledge of dimensional modeling and experience with workflow orchestration tools.
- Familiarity with PowerBI, Tableau, Looker, or other business intelligence tools.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data and provide actionable insights.

**Soft Skills**

- Curiosity and willingness to explore complex and ambiguous problems and deliver actionable insights through both quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
- Desire to work in a multi-cultural environment and collaborate with people from different backgrounds and experiences, with a partner-first approach to interacting with stakeholders.
- Strong data visualization and communication skills: ability to “tell a story” with numbers in a variety of formats: PowerPoints, dashboards, memos, and presentations.
- Strong attention to detail & commitment to a high standard of work product.

**Nice-to-Haves / Areas You Will Grow:**

- Knowledge of philanthropy, major gifts, or nonprofit fundraising analytics.
- Experience with Databricks and dbt.
- Experience with web analytics and behavioral data, and relevant tooling like Heap or Amplitude.
- Knowledge of Salesforce or similar CRM technology.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard office working environment.
- Some international travel.
- This role may require working remotely full or part time and part time remote employees may be required to share workspace.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America and United Kingdom.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $85,000 - $100,000/yr; UK Pay Rate £65,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Standard Responsibilities**

Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies

**Standard Job Requirements**

The IRC and IRC workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Related standard content:**

IRC strives to build a diverse and inclusive team at all levels who as individuals, and as a group, embody our culture statement creating a working environment characterized by critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity for us to achieve our aspirations as a team and deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Recruitment Process**

The process for this role will be as follows

- Screening call online
- First round panel interview online – including assessment / test
- Second round panel interview – online – including presentation task
- Final role and expectations alignment call with Senior Director, online

title: Mission France - Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable de la promotion et de la médiation en santé pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec les responsables de la protection, des activités médicales et de la santé mentale de l’unité migration, vous piloterez la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé et d’engagement communautaire.

Vous encadrerez les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, superviserez les interventions de terrain et contribuerez à adapter les activités du projet aux besoins et aux retours des personnes accompagnées.

Votre fonction associera pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe, mobilisation communautaire et présence opérationnelle sur le terrain.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de promotion et de médiation en santé**

- Concevoir, déployer et actualiser la stratégie de promotion de la santé, de médiation et d’engagement communautaire, en lien avec le·la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration.
- Définir les priorités, les activités, les outils et les modalités de suivi en fonction des besoins identifiés et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir une approche participative, en associant les personnes accompagnées et les communautés à l’identification de leurs besoins et à l’élaboration des réponses.
- Superviser la création de supports de prévention et d’éducation à la santé, adaptés aux différents publics, en veillant à leur pertinence, à leur validation et à leur accessibilité linguistique et culturelle.
- Contribuer aux réflexions stratégiques et opérationnelles du projet, en collaboration avec les responsables des autres pôles.

**Piloter les activités communautaires et les interventions de terrain**

- Organiser et superviser les activités d’« aller-vers », les actions de sensibilisation, les ateliers collectifs et les activités de médiation individuelle.
- Veiller à la qualité des interventions menées sur les lieux de vie, lors des activités collectives et dans le lieu de répit.
- Développer des approches favorisant l’écoute, la confiance et la participation des personnes aux décisions qui concernent leur santé.
- Superviser la surveillance à base communautaire, notamment l’identification des besoins et des situations préoccupantes, la recherche active de cas et l’orientation vers les services de santé adaptés.
- Accompagner les médiateur·rices dans l’organisation des entretiens individuels et des rencontres communautaires.
- Coordonner, avec les autres responsables de pôles, les évaluations rapides des besoins et les interventions nécessitant une approche pluridisciplinaire.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences de l’équipe**

- Encadrer les médiateur·rices en santé et les médiateur·rices interculturel·les, et organiser leurs plannings en fonction des activités du projet.
- Participer aux recrutements, à l’intégration et à l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe, en collaboration avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant formation, accompagnement individuel, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Superviser la qualité des activités, notamment les méthodes participatives, les techniques pédagogiques, l’écoute active et l’utilisation des outils de médiation.
- Favoriser la coopération, la circulation des informations et la complémentarité entre les équipes, tout en assurant la continuité des activités en cas d’absence.

**Analyser les besoins et renforcer les liens avec les communautés et les partenaires**

- Mettre en place des dispositifs de recueil et d’analyse des retours des personnes et des communautés, notamment des perceptions, préoccupations et rumeurs liées à la santé.
- Contribuer aux évaluations rapides, aux enquêtes et à l’analyse qualitative des besoins individuels et des dynamiques communautaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie participative des communautés, des associations et des acteurs du territoire, en intégrant les observations des équipes de maraude.
- Entretenir les relations avec les partenaires et partager les informations utiles à l’adaptation des interventions.
- Superviser la collecte des données, analyser les tendances, produire les rapports d’activité et documenter les enseignements tirés des interventions.
- Utiliser ces analyses pour proposer des ajustements opérationnels et améliorer la pertinence des actions de promotion et de médiation en santé.

**Garantir la sécurité, la qualité et les moyens nécessaires aux activités**

- Assurer la fonction de point focal sécurité pour les équipes lors des interventions  
    d’« aller-vers ».
- Veiller à l’application des mesures de safeguarding dans l’ensemble des activités et à leur bonne compréhension par les membres de l’équipe.
- Garantir le respect des principes, protocoles et standards de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Planifier et suivre les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires au fonctionnement du pôle, en collaboration avec les départements concernés.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des pratiques et à la capitalisation des expériences du projet.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Licence en sciences sociales, sciences du comportement, santé publique, médiation en santé ou santé communautaire, ou diplôme d’infirmier·ère en santé communautaire.
- Une expérience significative dans l’accompagnement de publics vulnérables et le management d’équipe peut également correspondre au profil recherché.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes ou de projets de médiation en santé ou de santé communautaire, en France, à l’étranger ou au sein de MSF.
- Expérience indispensable dans l’utilisation de méthodes qualitatives.
- Expérience requise dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi de stratégies.
- Expérience en management d’équipe.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Solides capacités d’analyse, de réflexion stratégique et d’adaptation des interventions aux réalités du terrain.
- Aptitude à encadrer, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe.
- Sens de l’écoute, qualités relationnelles et capacité à instaurer un dialogue avec des publics divers.
- Capacité à travailler en équipe pluridisciplinaire et à coopérer avec différents partenaires.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Engagement envers les principes de promotion de la santé et de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Flexibilité et capacité à évoluer dans des environnements difficiles et changeants, y compris lors d’activités de nuit.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais souhaitée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.
- La connaissance de logiciels de traitement de données qualitatives (NVivo), de création graphique (Photoshop), de collecte de données ou de cartographie (KoboCollect, OsmAnd, QGIS) constitue un atout.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an.
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

title: Medical Device UniQuality & Unidata Product Information Specialist
body:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** Permanent contract at 100%

**Starting date:** 01.12.2026

**Deadline to apply:** The position will close once a suitable candidate has been selected

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**I. MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and 19 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**II. POSITION BACKGROUND**

Coordination and Source of Product Information (SPINCO) was created to maintain consistency in the choice of medical and non-medical articles between MSF sections in order to improve MSF interventions, while considering field realities.

SPINCO is the driver for effective collaboration across the movement to deliver a central source of trusted product information that enables continuous process improvements. SPINCO contributes to MSF’s social mission by enabling improvements in field operations through the provision of product information to all layers of the organization. This enables product quality and visibility for better quality of care, enables assortment management, improvement in supply chain performance and increases overall interoperability whilst reducing duplication of effort. SPINCO’s core role is coordinating the expression of the demand of articles (medical and non-medical) and ensuring it is properly translated for supply whose role is to fulfil that demand.

In 2018, UniQuality was implemented as the unique central quality assurance database of MSF, containing the quality assured drugs, medical devices and specialised food validated for use in MSF projects. It is used by the MSF International Pharmacist Network, International Specialised Foods Network, and International Medical Devices/In-vitro Diagnostics Network, and Supply Centres to allow access to the most up-to-date validated product-manufacturer information.

In 2022, the UniMed project was launched to connect UniQuality to the supply centres’ ERP systems and automate the dissemination of the information regarding medicines and specialized food, to ensure the accuracy and consistency of quality review information. This position will support the completion of UniQuality for Medical Devices and IVDs in preparation of the linkage of both systems for this category of products as well.

In 2024 the Medical Device Repository, a SharePoint library for regulatory, quality and technical documents, went live to facilitate importation procedures with a direct access for field teams, and to keep product validation documentation after assessment by IO and ESC QA referents.

In 2025, the NexSpin project was launched to replace the existing solutions including UniQuality and the MD repository by a new Product Information Management System aiming at improving operational efficiency, user experience and user interface. This requires cleaning of the existing solutions, providing input to the NexSpin team as key users and being involved in the implementation phase scheduled in 2027.

Medical Device UniQuality & Unidata Product Information Specialist open-end position (100%).

**III. PLACE IN THE ORGANISATION**

- The person reports to the SPINCO Product Information Specialists Coordinator with a functional reporting line to the Deputy Quality Assurance coordinator for Medical Devices.
- The person will closely coordinate with the Data-Owners in the International QA MD Coordination team and the European Supply Centres.

**IV. OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION**

This position is focused on Medical Devices (MD). The objective of the position is to ensure that information related to Entities and Quality Review in UniQuality and the MD Repository is complete, accurate and available for the relevant MSF stakeholders. By guaranteeing the compliance with Quality Assurance processes, the Uniquality Data Steward’s role is to safeguard the quality of information in UniQuality and the MD repository, as well as the consistency between both tools.

They will act as primary point of contact for all stakeholders in case of questions about rules or non-conformity of information contained in UniQuality. They will develop a plan to gradually introduce a data quality and reporting plan to ensure that trust is maintained.

The Unidata Product Information Specialist role contributes to MSF social mission by ensuring the availability of trusted, standardized, and high-quality product information. This role supports field operations, supply chain performance, and interoperability through centralized data stewardship, product portfolio management, and collaboration with diverse stakeholders.

**V. MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**A. UniQuality Data Steward**

**1. Management of Entities in UniQuality:**

- Currently close to 1300 MD international entities in UQ
- Create, validate and update MD entities according to the relevant SOP, more specifically:
- Create new entities upon request of ESCs QA referents and Spinco data stewards (creation of a new article code), by verifying the availability of documents in the MD Repository for manufacturers not existing in UQ
- Support the update/cleaning of the ESC database of entities.
- Approve the entities for MD International purchase by checking for completeness of data in relevant public database, e.g. Eudamed, FDA registration, Conformity Assessment Bodies database for ISO certificates
- Update the entities (name / address) according to new supplier information received from ESC and by regularly checking public database

**2. Management of ISO certificates**

- Close to 1000 ISO certificates in the MD repository
- Search for online information: manufacturer’s website, Conformity Assessment Bodies and Accreditation Bodies database
- Ensure that information related to ISO certificates in UQ and in the MD Repository are updated and consistent, especially for entities associated to quality reviews.
- Request updated documentation to the ESC referents or regulatory assistants.
- Update the list of the certification bodies in UQ and the related information: NB number, accreditation, link to online directories for certificates verification

**3. MD Repository**

- Currently around 9000 documents in total, will grow as quality reviews are completed
- Ensure that the rules set for the uploading and tagging of regulatory and quality documentation in the MD repository are followed by all stakeholders, i.e., IO MD QA Coordination, supply centers QA referents and regulatory assistants, RA Pharma, and field users.
- Check regularly recently uploaded documents: naming of file is correct, tagging is completed, certificates information in UQ (ISO and EU/CE certificate) is updated, duplicates are removed
- Assist the end-users with practical use of the MD Repository and report issues to the helpdesk if needed.

**4. Eudamed**

- Follow up the use of the different modules in Eudamed: changes of activities, new documentation and information available. Inform the QA referents of changes.
- Train the different groups (ESC QA referents, intersection pharmacists) in the practical use of Eudamed.
- Liaise with the Spinco development team for the possibilities to link with Eudamed in Uniquality

**5. General UniQuality / MD Repository**

- Propose improvements and updates of SOP for UniQuality and the MD Repository as necessary, in collaboration with the product owners and in agreement with the main stakeholders
- Propose an action plan to review and improve the quality of information aligned with the needs and work capacity of the stakeholders.
- Implement an annual report/control on data quality of UniQuality and the MD repository by defining the quality criteria and setting the KPI in collaboration with the MD QA coordination
- Train new UniQuality / MD Repository users by developing e-learning tools, and organizing training sessions in collaboration with the UQ product owner

**B. Unidata Product Information specialist**

**1. Product Information Management**

- Monitor, evaluate, and process requests for new, modified, or removed products in alignment with MSF guidelines, protocols and standards.
- Consolidate and validate information on product description, quality, pricing, field testing, and maintenance requirements for approval by the Medical Directors' platform.
- Ensure product availability and suitability for field use by collaborating with QA teams, buyers, and regional hubs.
- Owns the data product lifecycle and technical specifications
- Ensures the product meets user needs and use cases
- Prioritises improvements and manages changes over time

**2. Harmonization and Interoperability**

- Collaborate with intersectional platforms, supply centres and field operations to standardize products across MSF operations.
- Facilitate resource sharing and intersectional field operations by ensuring product harmonization.
- Promote responsible use of product data to balance efficiency, cost, and humanitarian mission.

**3. Data Stewardship**

- Ensure and maintain the high quality of product information in terms of accuracy, validity, consistency, completeness, uniqueness and accessibility of product information in the UniData tool, MSF central article database.
- Ensure UniData serves as the single source of truth for downstream systems (e.g., ERP, UniQuality, order tools).
- Govern the central database and ensure compliance with regulatory standards (e.g., EU norms, ISO standards, IATA transport regulations).
- Promote consistency and usability by maintaining aligned definitions (Knowledge database, KPIs) and making data fit for decision-making.
- Support continuous improvement by identifying data issues, proposing enhancements, and acting as a bridge between technical team and IT

**4. Data ownership: accessibility and visibility**

- Responsible and accountable for the accessibility and visibility of product information
- Publish product information on accessible platforms (web, intranet, offline tools) for global MSF staff.
- Act as the focal point for central database governance and user support.

**5. Process Design and Improvement**

- Responsible and accountable for data governance: how product information is defined, created and used
- Design, implement, and enhance processes related to data requirements, product codification, and multilingual labelling.
- Pushing data governance by setting the direction and objectives
- Actively promoting improved data governance practices (RACI).
- Ensure product information data supports reliable operational & strategic decision-making
- Publish annual summaries of medical product changes and updates to MSF catalogues.
- Publish monthly reports on medial product changes for the ESC referents and medical referents of the OC/OD’s
- Develop policies, guidelines, and training materials for approximately 1,700 database users.

**6. Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Work closely with MSF field staff, headquarters, Quality Assurance teams, tactical buyers and intersectional platforms to ensure product standardization and quality of product information.
- Participate in international projects with NGOs and UN sectors, such as emergency health kits and medical device nomenclature initiatives.

**VI. SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it to protect others.

**VII. REQUIREMENTS**

- Master’s degree in scientific, engineering, pharmacy or paramedical sciences
- Detail-oriented, meticulous and organized for data entry/modification in database is essential
- Computer & analytical skills, including MS Excel are essential
- Knowlegde of Medical Devices regulatory environment (MDR/IVDR) and ISO standards is a plus
- Proficiency in English (both speaking and writing) and knowledge of French
- MSF field or Supply experience in a medical position is an asset
- Fast learner, able to adapt quickly to a changing environment
- Customer oriented, resilient, with good people and communication skills
- Self-motivated, with an interest in problem solving
- Excellent time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and multi-task depending on the needs.
- Technical writing capacities.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

title: Mission France - Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Aux côtés du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous participerez au pilotage des opérations, à l’organisation des activités et à l’accompagnement des équipes dans un contexte exigeant et en constante évolution. Vous contribuerez à l’analyse des besoins et des risques, à la coordination des interventions et à la qualité de la prise en charge. En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous assurerez la continuité de la coordination.

Vous assisterez également le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet dans la planification, la coordination et le suivi des activités de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, afin de garantir une réponse cohérente, sûre et adaptée aux besoins des personnes exilées.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Favoriser une communication claire et respectueuse entre les personnes accompagnées et les équipes MSF, en atténuant les barrières linguistiques, les incompréhensions culturelles et les discriminations, afin de contribuer à un accès équitable à des soins et à un accompagnement adaptés.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

**Contribuer à la coordination des opérations sur le terrain**

- Participer à la transition des projets de Calais et Dunkerque vers un projet Littoral Nord intégré.
- Contribuer à l’organisation et au suivi des activités sur les lieux de consultation, les lieux de survie et les plages ou zones de départ.
- En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, assurer la coordination des activités et la continuité opérationnelle.
- Organiser, avec les responsables de pôle, la participation des équipes aux maraudes de prévention et de prise en charge des personnes lors des tentatives de traversée.
- Veiller à l’application des protocoles opérationnels et de sécurité, notamment les briefings et débriefings et les procédures liées aux distributions.
- En lien avec le ou la référent·e pluridisciplinaire du projet Migration, contribuer à la coordination entre les équipes et à la qualité de la prise en charge, dans le respect du secret médical partagé et des standards MSF.

**Analyser le contexte et contribuer à la représentation de MSF**

- Participer au suivi du contexte politique, humanitaire et sécuritaire à la frontière et faire remonter les évolutions susceptibles d’affecter les opérations.
- Contribuer aux missions exploratoires sur le littoral, notamment en dehors des zones d’intervention actuelles de Calais et Dunkerque, afin d’identifier les besoins et les priorités.
- Assurer le lien avec les acteurs du littoral et participer aux réunions de coordination.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à la représentation de MSF auprès des autorités, des services publics, des forces de l’ordre, des associations, de la société civile et des médias.
- Participer aux actions de communication et de plaidoyer liées aux interventions de MSF sur le littoral.

**Accompagner les équipes et veiller à la sécurité**

- Contribuer à l’organisation des ressources humaines, à l’intégration du nouveau personnel, au suivi quotidien des équipes et à l’identification des besoins de formation.
- Participer à l’analyse des risques et à la mise à jour des consignes de sécurité ; être le point focal sécurité lors des interventions selon les responsabilités définies pour le projet.
- Soutenir les équipes dans la mise en œuvre des activités et assurer la transmission des informations opérationnelles.
- Promouvoir les principes de safeguarding et veiller à leur compréhension et à leur application au sein de l’équipe et du projet.

**Assurer le suivi, la qualité et le reporting des activités**

- Superviser ou contribuer à la compilation et à l’analyse des données collectées, ainsi qu’au reporting des activités.
- Veiller au respect des standards MSF et à la qualité de la prise en charge pendant les interventions, notamment en matière de distributions et de safeguarding.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à l’accompagnement des équipes de support, notamment logistique et RH/finance.
- Participer à l’identification de pistes de plaidoyer en lien avec la présence de MSF lors des tentatives de traversée.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau bac+3 minimum.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience en gestion de projet, dans l’aide humanitaire, au sein de MSF, d’une autre ONG ou d’une association.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.
- Une expérience dans des contextes migratoires est souhaitée.

**Qualités :**

- Capacité d’analyse et vision stratégique.
- Leadership et aptitude à accompagner les équipes.
- Sens de l’organisation, de la planification et des priorités.
- Esprit d’équipe et capacité à coopérer avec des interlocuteurs variés.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à un environnement changeant et exigeant, y compris lors d’interventions de nuit.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques de base, notamment Word, Excel et Internet.
- Permis B obligatoire.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne connaissance de l’anglais souhaitée.
- La maîtrise d’autres langues est un plus.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 598,40 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

title: Head of Programmes - CAR
body:
DanChurchAid (DCA) is looking for an experienced Head of Programmes to lead its Central African Republic (CAR) programme portfolio. Reporting to the Country Director and serving on the Senior Management Team, you will turn country strategy into well-managed projects, strengthen programme quality and partnerships, and support teams delivering assistance in a demanding operating environment.

**Duty station:** Bangui, with regular travel to field locations | International, non-accompanied position

**Contract:** 12 months, with the possibility of extension | Opening date: 22 October 2026 | **Closing date: 20 November 2026**

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply early.

**Our programme in CAR**

DCA has worked in CAR since 2015, implementing humanitarian, development and peacebuilding activities directly and with national civil society partners. Our work responds to the consequences of conflict and displacement while supporting recovery, community resilience and efforts to reduce violence and exclusion.

The portfolio brings together protection, psychosocial support and assistance to victims of conflict; conflict prevention, peacebuilding and social cohesion; and cash assistance and food security. Humanitarian mine action and explosive ordnance risk awareness also form part of DCA’s experience in CAR. We seek practical links between these areas, informed by communities’ priorities and by conflict-sensitive analysis.

Current projects portfolio includes project funded by the Gov. Of CAR (back donor World Bank) alongside interventions supported by ECHO, INTPA, FPI, the CAR Humanitarian Fund, the UN Peacebuilding Fund, the ICC Trust Fund for Victims and Danish strategic partnership funding. These projects combine different delivery models, partnership arrangements and reporting requirements. The Head of Programmes will maintain a coherent portfolio while ensuring that each project meets its commitments to communities and donors.

**Your team and working relationships**

You will work with project managers, area coordinators, MEAL colleagues, technical staff and national partners, supported by DCA headquarters advisers. Based in Bangui, you will maintain close contact with field teams and make regular visits to implementation locations.

DCA CAR is strengthening area-based management and clarifying responsibilities between programme and support functions. The Head of Programmes provides programme, MEAL and quality oversight and technical supervision within the authority delegated by the Country Director. Area coordinators retain line management of staff assigned to them, while multi-area project oversight and management remains under the Head of Programmes. You will make these arrangements work in practice through clear priorities, coaching, joint planning and timely escalation of unresolved issues.

Close collaboration with finance, procurement, logistics and HR is essential. Together, you will ensure that activity plans, procurement schedules, staffing, budgets and donor commitments are realistic and aligned.

**What you will lead**

• **Programme strategy and relevance:** translate the country strategy into operational priorities; use needs assessments, IPC and MSNA findings, response coverage and community feedback to guide geographic and sector choices; identify and secure opportunities that fit DCA’s capacity and added value.

• **Delivery and quality:** steer complex projects through integrated project management frameworks; oversee and support implementation against agreed results, budgets and timelines; support project managers and area coordinators to identify delays early, agree corrective actions and follow them through; ensure technical standards, protection mainstreaming and conflict sensitivity across the portfolio.

• **People and management:** manage staff assigned to you under the country organigram; set clear objectives, delegate effectively and address performance issues; provide technical supervision and coaching to area coordinators and programme colleagues through the agreed management framework.

• **MEAL and accountability:** strengthen practical monitoring systems, data quality and analysis; create and maintain project and portfolio dashboards covering progress, results, expenditure, procurement, deadlines and risks, and use them to guide management reviews and corrective actions; ensure accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms, including safe referral of sensitive complaints; use findings to improve delivery and demonstrate results.

• **Partnerships and localisation:** build equitable relationships with national organisations; agree responsibilities, resources and capacity-strengthening priorities jointly; work with support colleagues on proportionate due diligence, partner monitoring and follow-up.

• **Project development and funding:** lead concept notes, proposals, results frameworks and donor reports with country and HQ colleagues; work with finance and support teams on credible budgets, staffing and procurement plans; maintain a realistic funding pipeline.

• **Grant and risk management:** maintain oversight of reporting deadlines, contractual commitments and programme risks; work with finance colleagues on budget reviews, forecasts and partner expenditure; ensure that changes requiring donor approval are identified and addressed in time.

• **Cash working group Co-lead:** Act as the Cash Working Group co lead; providing support to the WFP / OCHA led structure and ensuring adequate support to the group.

• **Senior management and representation:** contribute to country-level decisions, organisational priorities and risk reviews; represent DCA with donors, clusters, authorities, civil society and peer agencies; promote cooperation across departments and support agreed SMT decisions.

**The challenges you will help us address**

You will join a programme that needs both strategic direction and consistent management follow-through. Priorities include keeping a diverse portfolio on track, strengthening the connection between field delivery and Bangui oversight, and improving the use of monitoring and financial information in decisions. The World Bank-funded NDOYE project adds a substantial implementation and contractual workload alongside humanitarian and peacebuilding grants.

Success will require early procurement and staffing planning, clear ownership of actions, strong programme–support collaboration and constructive engagement with partners. You will balance immediate delivery pressures with team development and sustainable systems, adapting plans to access and security constraints while protecting programme quality and accountability to communities.

**What you bring**

• At least three years of experience managing a multi-project programme portfolio, including responsibility for staff, programme quality, donor engagement and delivery in a complex humanitarian or fragile setting.

• Strong knowledge of CAR or comparable Central African contexts, and the ability to translate political, conflict and humanitarian analysis into practical programme decisions. Previous experience in CAR is a strong asset.

• Previous substantive experience in at least two of the following three areas is required: cash programming; food security; and Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, including Accountability to Affected Populations. Experience in protection, conflict prevention or peacebuilding is an additional asset.

• Demonstrated people-management skills: setting priorities, coaching managers, delegating, resolving disagreements and holding teams accountable while maintaining respectful working relationships.

• Proven experience developing successful proposals and producing clear donor reports. Familiarity with ECHO, pooled humanitarian funds, UN funding or institutional development financing is an advantage; World Bank-funded project experience is particularly relevant.

• Demonstrated experience steering complex projects involving multiple locations, partners, funding requirements or interdependent workstreams. You can translate contractual commitments into integrated workplans, track milestones and dependencies, and lead corrective action across programme and support teams.

• Hands-on experience designing and using project or portfolio dashboards that bring together activities, results, expenditure, procurement, reporting deadlines and risks. You can establish reliable data flows, assign responsibility for updates, and use dashboards in management reviews to drive decisions and follow-up.

• Experience strengthening community accountability and equitable partnerships with national organisations, including capacity development and management of implementation risks. Strong judgement under pressure, experience working in insecure environments, and a commitment to safeguarding, inclusion and responsible risk management. Recent HEAT or equivalent training is desirable.

• Fluency in written and spoken French and a good working knowledge of English are required. You must be able to lead teams and engage with partners in French, and work effectively with English-language donor documents, reporting and headquarters communications.

**What we offer**

• A 12-month contract with the possibility of extension and a competitive salary package.

• 30 days of paid annual leave and three R&R cycles per year, subject to DCA’s Staff Welfare Policy for Bangui as a duty station.

• Insurance as per industry standards.

• A substantive leadership role with opportunities to shape programme quality, develop colleagues and strengthen national partnerships, with support from country and headquarters teams.

**How to apply**

Please submit your CV and cover letter through DCA’s online recruitment system by **20 November 2026**. Explain how your experience relates to the portfolio, management responsibilities and challenges described above. Only applications submitted through the recruitment system will be considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Applications open on 23 October 2026 and will be reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the three-week publication period. Shortlisting and interviews may begin before the closing date, so early applications are encouraged.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply. DCA conducts an anti-terror check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

title: PSS and Community Development Unit Manager
body:
**Job Title:** PSS and Community Development Unit Manager

**Location:** Erbil, Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), with regular travel to other areas of KRI.

**Type of position:** Employment contract

**Length of Contract:** 12 Months

**Compensation and Benefits:** Competitive salary and benefits commensurate with skills and experience. Expatriate/National Compensation Package: includes local transportation allowances, Medical insurance and Life insurance

**About SEED**: SEED is a women-led, local NGO in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, dedicated to creating a thriving society by advancing social protection and human development. We support individuals, empower communities, and strengthen systems to drive lasting change and equal opportunity. With a focus on collaboration, we promote gender equality, protect children, combat human trafficking, and improve mental health and well-being. SEED’s holistic, locally-driven approach integrates transformational services, community development, training and education, and advocacy to create sustainable impact. SEED is committed to creating a just, equitable society where everyone's rights are protected, with healthy families and strong communities, and a future where everyone can thrive.

**Role of the PSS and Community Development Unit Manager:**

SEED is seeking a dynamic and experienced Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Community Development (CD) Manager to lead the PSS/CD Unit and guide on SEED’s strategic objective of engaging and empowering communities. The PSS/CD Manager will lead and plan for the implementation of community-based programming aimed at engaging and empowering communities towards the development of a strong, healthy, resilient, and cohesive society through community-based initiatives designed to foster social and emotional well-being, prevent violence and discrimination, and promote social and economic empowerment. The PSS/CD Manager will oversee and support the technical/thematic leads and implementation of PSS/CD programming across thematic pillars, various programs, and locations across Kurdistan. The Manager will lead a team to design, manage, adapt, and support implementation of programming that improves MH and psychosocial wellbeing, achieves gender equality and ends GBV, and protects children and empowers their development. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will work in close collaboration with the MEAL Unit to ensure communities are involved from the start until the end of each program and that feedback is collected and the learnings are at the foundation of any future programming and requests for funding. This position requires a leader with both a deep understanding of psychosocial support and the ability to design community-driven interventions that promote positive social behaviors. The role also includes managing PSS resources, managing staff and building their capacity, and planning and guiding the strategic direction and execution of SEED’s community programming. The ideal candidate will bring strong leadership, planning and management skills, along with technical expertise in PSS, community development, promoting equality and combating gender-based violence (GBV), protection, mental health (MH), social behavioral change, and social cohesion programs, and a passion for empowering communities through transformative, locally driven change. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will oversee the 3 Technical Thematic Leads and ensure activities are appropriately tailored to the needs of each community. This position is based in Erbil with frequent travel required to Sulaimani and surrounding areas.

**Specific Tasks:**

**Management, Leadership, and Technical Support (60%):**

- Lead and manage SEED’s PSS/CD Unit and its 3 Technical Thematic Leads, and provide strategic direction to SEED on its cross-cutting strategic objective to engage and empower communities.
- Develop technical strategies, guidelines, and standards for the unit and provide strategic direction and day-to-day management of SEED’s PSS and community development programming.
- Oversee development, adaptation and dissemination of technical resources, including group curricula, training manuals, facilitator guides, and standardized tools for PSS and community development interventions created by the Technical Thematic Leads.
- Support the Technical Thematic Leads with the design, adaptation and delivery of awareness-raising sessions, PSS group activities, and community development interventions.
- Collaborate with Program Managers and Coordinators to align community needs with interventions and ensure technical quality and consistency across projects.
- Ensure the formation of community led initiatives, social cohesion activities, and social behavioral change (SBC) programming.
- Ensure PSS teams have PSS outreach plans for all locations and provide inputs into new partnerships engagement.
- Identify, mitigate and manage risks related to program delivery, partnerships, safeguarding and community dynamics
- Develop policies related to PSS program implementation and community engagement and accountability.
- Ensure the development of partnerships to enhance SEED’s PSS portfolio.
- Ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and international standards and practices.
- Set project direction by prioritizing and organizing actions & resources to achieve objectives.
- Provide input into program development pertaining to SEED’s PSS/CD work.
- Support the recruitment, interviewing, and onboarding of Thematic Leads, PSS facilitators and coordinators working on various programs and across locations.

**Reporting, MEAL, and Communications (30%)**

- Work closely with the MEAL unit to ensure communities are actively engaged throughout the whole programming cycle.
- Support with the development and adaptation of MEAL tools that collect information from communities, stakeholders, and other relevant parties to ensure community based ownership.
- Monitor implementation quality and adapt programming based on learning and community feedback.
- Ensure quality assessments are taking place to understand community needs prior to starting programs / interventions, and use data to inform program adjustments and quality improvements.
- Contribute to the development of PSS tools to ensure that M&E systems provide adequate feedback.
- Measure impact of interventions through proper feedback mechanisms and data collection.
- Provide input on safe and ethical data collection and storage.
- Contribute to developing articles, flyers, briefs, and other communication materials as needed.
- Provide input into awareness raising campaigns and advocacy strategies on related topics / thematic areas.

**Coordination and Organizational Representation (10%)**

- Identify, build and manage collaborative partnerships with other partners, coordination bodies, local authorities and other stakeholders.
- Represent SEED in meetings with communities, stakeholders, NGOs, KRG, and with donors.
- Develop strategic partnerships and maintain effective working relationships with key stakeholders including donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs.
- Work closely with program partners, consultants, contractors, and sub-grantees.
- Conduct external meetings, presentations, or trainings on PSS related topics as requested.

**Key values:**

- Serve as a positive role model and SEED ambassador at all times.
- Treat all people with respect regardless of age, gender, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, disability status, marital status and ethnicity.
- Working collaboratively with all colleagues, and maintaining a positive, cooperative attitude.

**Essential criteria:**

- Master’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Gender Studies, International Development, Public Health or related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in managing teams and building staff capacity through training, coaching, and supervision.
- Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in PSS, community engagement, GBV prevention, social behavioral change, MH, and peacebuilding in humanitarian or development settings.
