title: MHPSS and Protection Coordinator - LEBANON - based in Beyrouth
body:
**PUI all around the world**

**Deadline for application: 30/11/2026**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** Millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents
- Thanks to the work and commitment of :
- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

**Focus on our activities in Lebanon**

Our mission in Lebanon has been open since 2012. PUI develops its integrated approach with health, protection, food security & livelihoods, and shelter interventions. Furthermore, PUI works on strengthening existing public systems and infrastructure, while also providing direct, emergency support to affected population depending on the local context. Today, the mission is implementing 12 projects.

**What about the MHPSS and Protection Coordinator ?**

**As Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and Protection Coordinator, you are responsible for the development and implementation of the mission's operational MHPSS and Protection strategies respectively as well as for the quality of current and future MHPSS and Protection programmes throughout the design, implementation monitoring and evaluation phases. You build the capacity of the mission’s MHPSS department and Protection department (technical teams and projets’ teams) and provide technical support to the project teams. You represent PUI to the authorities, humanitarian actors and donors for the MHPSS and Protection sector.**

For this purpose, you will be responsible for :

- Context analysis / Strategy / Development : You participate in the development of the operational strategy in MHPSS and Protection and contribute to the design of new relevant MHPSS and Protection interventions on the mission based on the identified MHPSS and Protection needs in the country, and in line with PUI MHPSS and Protection intervention frameworks. In coordination with the MHPSS and Protection teams in the bases, you monitor MHPSS and Protection activities in the country and analyse their strengths and weaknesses, offer programmatic adjustments in line with the needs, regulations and contextual developments.
- Programmes quality: You provide technical support in your field of expertise to the technical and programme teams (Specialists, PMs, Deputies PMs, Supervisors and implementing staff) and ensure the quality and effectiveness of the mission's MHPSS and Protection programmes through field visits, data analysis and regular check ins with the base teams within their specific areas of expertise.
- Representation / Coordination: You ensure PUI's external representation for the MHPSS and Protection sector to partners, donors, national authorities and local actors. You represent PUI in relevant Clusters/Sub-Clusters (Protection, GBV) or MHPSS sector working group meetings. You contribute to the good information sharing within the MHPSS and Protection sector and inform PUI of the discussions and update from these discussions.
- Human Resources / Training: You provide technical support to the project teams and in particular to the MHPSS and Protection teams. You provide support to the project managers for the recruitment of technical staff in MHPSS and Protection. Working alongside the Deputy HoM for Programs and the HQ MHPSS and Protection and Gender Advisors, you identify key strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and gaps within MHPSS and Protection departments. You work on a capacity building plan/training plan for the teams and supervise the content of these trainings where relevant. You also provide clinical supervision to the psychologists in the bases.
- Logistics and Administration: You ensure the teams under your responsibility follow logistic and administrative procedures and keep the logistic and administrative departments informed of any relevant developments.
- Security: You contribute to the compliance with security rules on the mission and share all information related to security to your line manager and/or to the mission's security manager.

**The challenges that await you :**

Support to enhance visibility and fundraising for Protection activities and Protection mainstreaming Lead the full integration of MHPSS services in the national system, including but not limited to supporting the integration of MHPSS in the national health information system, piloting the support for psychiatric hospitalization and supporting the primary healthcare network to directly provide quality MHPSS services Lead the integration between MHPSS, Protection and Health departments Respond to the rapidly changing and compounding needs of displaced and conflict-affected populations

**What you will need to succeed**

- **Training** You hold a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in psychology, psychiatry, mental health, or similar relevant field.
- **Experience** With at least 3 years of experience implementing MHPSS programs, at minimum 2 years of clinical practice in mental health or psychosocial care and 3 years of Protection Programmes management (including including design, implementation, and monitoring of interventions) or a similar position. You have a strong understanding of global Protection and/or GBV principles and standards and relevant bodies of international law. You have previous experience with NGO and in humanitarian or development settings, ideally with populations affected by crisis, displacement, or conflict. You have worked in environments with protection/GBV threats.
- **Skills** You have solid understanding of the IASC Guidelines on MHPSS in Emergency Settings and MHPSS intervention pyramid and of the IASC Guidelines GBV in Emergency, on Protection and on Gender in Humanitarian Action. You have competence in designing and monitoring psychosocial and psychological interventions, including referral systems and stepped-care approaches and in designing and monitoring community based and general protection and/or GBV case management interventions, including person/survivor centered approach and referral systems.
- **Qualities** You demonstrate good written communication skills, good knowledge of program management and quality monitoring, excellent writing and speaking skills, and good knowledge of donors. You demonstrate strong and proven capacity in diplomatically working among an integrated multi-cultural project team.
- **Languages** English and French have no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak another language, it would be a definite asset.

**A word from the manager**

*« In the challenging and interesting context of Lebanon, PUI is among the largest NGOs providing health/MH services and a highly responsive actor nationwide, including in the south and Baalbeck-Hermel. The MHPSS/Protection Coordinator leads a dynamic team of specialists in Beirut and oversees programming across our 3 field-offices. With the rapidly changing context and high needs, this is a demanding but interesting role contributing to safety and wellbeing at a large scale. »*

**PUI will offer you**

- **Status :** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income :** 2 650,00 - 2 970,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Housing** in collective accomodation or housing allowance
- **Daily Living Expenses** ("Per Diem")
- **Break Policy :** 5 working days at 3 and 9 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy :** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

**Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts. PUI expects all employees to perform their tasks and professional responsibilities in accordance with the PUI Ethical Framework.  
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.  
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.  
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.  
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.  
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale will under no circumstances request any financial contribution for administrative fees related to recruitment. Any information suggesting otherwise is fraudulent and should be disregarded.

**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments ? You feel ready to take up the **challenge** and to join **PUI great family ?**

title: Pre-Hospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d)
body:
The **German Red Cross (GRC)** assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

**Our Mission:**

We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape.

The GRC is currently seeking a **Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d)**.

The Delegate will advise the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) and the GRC on prehospital emergency care (PHEC) and related health matters. In addition, the Delegate will oversee the implementation of a new project funded under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)’s Social Structure Funding (SSF) programme, in close cooperation with ERCS.

The three-year project, entitled **“Strengthening the Ethiopian Red Cross Society as a key actor in the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) system and improving the national enabling environment,”** is planned to run from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029. It aims to strengthen ERCS’s institutional and technical capacities in Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and contribute to the further development and standardisation of EMS in Ethiopia. Key areas include capacity building, the development and implementation of national guidelines and policies, and strengthening coordination and quality assurance within the national EMS system.

The Delegate will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia and work under the supervision of the Head of Office and will be part of an experienced team of three international delegates and local staff.

**The position is subject to final confirmation of BMZ funding.**

**Starting date:** 01.01.2027

**Duration:** 24 months, with possible extension

**Location:** Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent visits to the project sites

**Main duties & responsibilities**

- **Provide technical advice and contribute to strengthening ERCS capacities in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and related health areas**, including through the development and implementation of national standards, guidelines, training approaches and quality assurance mechanisms, capacity building and training-of-trainers approaches, and support to the institutionalisation and sustainability of PHEC and EMS services.
- **Oversee the implementation of the BMZ SSF-funded EMS project** in close cooperation with the ERCS, including project planning, reporting and budget management, ensuring effective, timely and quality implementation in line with the approved project proposal, budget and donor requirements.
- **Ensure close coordination with relevant national and international stakeholders**, including the Ethiopian Ministry of Health, NGOs, Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners providing technical support to health-related activities, and other actors working in health, particularly in PHEC. Represent GRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups and related clusters.
- **Support project monitoring, learning and quality assurance**, including regular monitoring of activities and results, collection and analysis of project data and indicators, identification of implementation challenges, and follow-up on agreed actions.
- **Support the identification and development of opportunities for additional funding for PHEC activities** from other institutional and private funding sources.
- **Provide support in emergencies in the area of PHEC and beyond**, as requested by ERCS and GRC.

**Required Competencies & Skills**

- **University degree** in Paramedicine/Prehospital Emergency Care, Public/Global Health, Health Management, Disaster Management or a related field. A clinical background as a paramedic, emergency nurse or physician with prehospital experience is an asset.
- **At least five years of professional experience** in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), emergency care, humanitarian health or a related field.
- **Strong technical knowledge and practical experience in PHEC**, ideally including experience in the development or implementation of PHEC systems, standards, guidelines, training programmes, quality assurance mechanisms and/or referral systems.
- **Demonstrated project management experience**, including project planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, budget management and financial monitoring of donor-funded projects. Experience with BMZ-funded projects is an asset.
- Experience in **capacity strengthening and adult learning**, including the design and facilitation of trainings, workshops and/or training-of-trainers approaches.
- Previous experience working with the **International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement** and knowledge of its structures, approaches and Fundamental Principles are strong assets.
- Experience in **multi-stakeholder coordination**, preferably with government authorities, National Societies, international organisations and other health or PHEC actors.
- Strong **communication, coordination and representation skills**, with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with partners at different organisational levels.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively in **complex and changing environments**, with a high degree of cultural sensitivity and adaptability.
- Excellent **written and spoken English**. Knowledge of German is an asset.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a **multicultural and multidisciplinary team**.
- Ability and agreement to adhere to the **Fundamental Principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement**.
- Ability to complete a thorough medical screening process for **working abroad under specific climate and health conditions and** willingness to travel within Ethiopia as required for project implementation and monitoring.
- Valid **International Driving Permit (IDP)**.

**What we offer you**

You will be part of a highly motivated professional and multicultural team. We offer you a compensation package according to the collective employment agreement of the GRC, an expatriation allowance during your mission as well as a personal allowance to cover your accommodation. In addition to a full insurance package, GRC is covering a home flight within a 12-month period of assignment. You will benefit from a comprehensive training package and receive briefings and coaching prior to, during and after your mission. Medical check-ups and Psychosocial Support Service are included in your assignment.

title: Administrative Assistant, Philanthropy
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**External Relations**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions: Private fundraising, Mobilization & Marketing, Policy & Advocacy and Operations & Analytics. To enable IRC to deliver our Strategy100 commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance our ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Administrative Assistant is a critical member of the team. We are seeking a professional to provide administrative and logistical support to the VP of Philanthropy, and account management support to fundraising leadership and staff. The role varies in what it covers and will suit somebody good at prioritizing effectively, multi-tasking and working autonomously. The right candidate can make judgements on what is important, will have the ability to solve problems, be efficient, diplomatic and have the inter-personal skills to deal with senior staff and colleagues.

***Support to the VP of Philanthropy - (25%)***

- Support the daily workflow of the VP of Philanthropy including handling appointments and complex calendar management
- Coordinate travel as needed, potentially including travel briefs, flights, accommodation, and ground transportation
- Collate and submit expense reports, purchase orders, contract payments and other finance transactions for approval. Support rollout of systems and processes related to expensing
- Provide finance operations support including vendor onboarding, invoice/PO/payment follow-up, workflow approval monitoring in Integra, and basic budget coding guidance as needed

***Fundraiser Support (50%)***

- Partner with assigned frontline fundraiser to keep donor and prospect portfolios organized and up to date, tracking next steps, deadlines, and follow-ups that support cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship plans
- Enter and maintain accurate donor, prospect, and portfolio data in Salesforce, including portfolio assignments, contact and activity records, contact reports, and giving proposals; run routine reports and flag data quality issues
- Draft and prepare correspondence and donor-facing materials for fundraiser review, such as letters, acknowledgments, and contact reports
- Prepare materials, agendas, and briefings for external donor and prospect meetings and for internal strategy meetings
- Track stewardship and reporting requirements and timeframes for assigned donors; coordinate with program and field staff to gather information and keep drafting and approval of proposals, reports, and budgets on schedule
- Support gift and payment processing, ensuring payment documentation is complete and compliant with IRC and donor policies and procedures
- Submit prospect research requests and coordinate with Prospect Research, Analytics, and Operations colleagues to support the donor cycle

***Department Administrative support and Coordination (25%)***

- Schedule department/team meetings included reserving conference rooms and setting up IT for meetings
- Manage onboarding materials for new staff (includes onboarding experience, coordination with IT and office services, integra training admin paperwork, maintaining docs, email distribution lists, internal newsletter, and IRC policy and process)
- Maintain and update key team-wide materials (e.g., org charts, onboarding materials, and internal intranet/team pages) to ensure accuracy with staffing and structural changes.
- Coordinate staff offboarding logistics including equipment return and timely updates to access, distribution lists, Teams, and reference materials.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Senior Officer, Strategic Planning and Operations
- **Day-to-day support to:** VP of Philanthropy
- **Indirect reporting: Other internal and/or external contacts:** Works closely with frontline fundraisers and other colleagues and departments across the organization, including Prospect Research, Analytics, and Operations.

**Candidate Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree preferred but not required.

**Work Experience:**

- At least one year in a fast-paced office setting (internship experience counts too!)

**Preferred:**

- Experience working in a non-profit development department
- Experience with a CRM database such as Salesforce, including data entry and reporting
- Experience drafting donor or client correspondence, or supporting a fundraising or sales team
- Prior experience working as an administrative assistant
- Interest in a fundraising career
- Experience working with high net-worth individuals and/or senior partners a plus

**Demonstrated Skills and Proficiencies:**

Minimum

- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization serving multiple partners
- Experience with Outlook email and calendar and familiarity with complex scheduling
- Solid Microsoft Office, database management, and Adobe Acrobat Pro experience
- Accurate, detail-oriented data entry and records management, with the ability to keep records clean and current
- Strong writing skills, with the ability to draft clear, polished correspondence and materials for review
- Ability to track multiple deadlines and commitments across a portfolio and follow through without reminders
- Have a can-do attitude with a flexible disposition to handle fast-paced, shifting priorities
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, interacting with a variety of internal and external contacts with confidence and poise
- Strong listening skills and the ability to accurately follow guidance
- Outstanding attention to detail and dedication to timelines
- Ability and interest to work both independently and in a multifaceted, cross-functional team structure
- Ability to handle change in a proactive and positive manner
- Dedication to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor and employee information

**Working Environment:** This role is hybrid and requires the ability to work on-site in the NYC office or Remote working. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** ($21-26/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

 **Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Project Activity Lead for Philippines
body:
**Position:** Project Lead

**Contract Length:** 24 months with possibility of extension

**Country Programme:** Philippines

**Base:** Manila, Philippines

**Line Manager:** Country Director

People in Need (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both in the Czech Republic and abroad.

## **About the Philippines Programme of People in Need:**

On November 8, 2013, Typhoon Haiyan (known in the Philippines as Yolanda) ravaged Eastern Samar, one of the poorest provinces of the country. The instant and large-scale emergency response provided by international organizations helped provide solutions to short-term problems and attended to the immediate needs of those affected. Now, we are also focusing on long-term development programs. We help revive and improve local markets and ensure new, alternative sources of livelihood for people. For instance, through LEAP, we promote sustainable livelihood opportunities by supporting seaweed farmers and coffee producers to improve production, access quality inputs, strengthen business skills, and connect with higher-value markets. By enhancing market access and value chain linkages, the project helps increase household incomes and build long-term economic resilience.

Following the Battle of Marawi, the longest urban war in the modern history of the Philippines, in cooperation with local partners, we helped young people affected by the conflict, distributed school uniforms, and provided legal advice and psychosocial support. We also provided sub-grants to local civil society organizations, and organized initiatives to empower the youth towards advocating for increased tolerance and respect for other religions and cultures.

We operate in some of the most impoverished and climate-vulnerable areas of the Philippines, strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities through disaster preparedness, early warning systems, and anticipatory action. By supporting communities to act on risk information before hazards strike and by delivering timely humanitarian assistance during emergencies, we help reduce disaster impacts and protect lives and livelihoods. We carry out this work in close partnership with local organizations, ensuring effective preparedness, early action, and rapid response for at-risk populations.

## **About the PASSAGE Project in the Philippines:**

Seaweed farming is the Philippines’ largest aquaculture commodity and a strategic sector with global demand projected to double by 2030. Despite its importance, the industry faces persistent challenges including unsustainable practices, fragmented value chains, poor access to finance and inputs, and limited ability to meet international traceability and sustainability requirements. These constraints threaten the livelihoods of thousands of smallholder farmers and weaken the country’s position in global markets.

This initiative, called PASSAGE, introduces a regenerative and traceable seaweed hub model designed to professionalize smallholder production, stabilize supply chains, and strengthen compliance with emerging social and environmental standards. By combining improved farming practices, affordable finance, digital traceability, and inclusive Marine Protected Areas, the project aims to increase productivity, reduce poverty, and enhance coastal ecosystem resilience while ensuring consistent, high-quality seaweed supply.

Over 48 months, PASSAGE will be gradually implemented in 6 provinces across the country, targeting more than 4,000 producers alongside processors, financial institutions, and public agencies. Through direct hub replication in ready sites and farmer readiness support in complex areas, the project will build resilient, investible seaweed value chains that reduce reliance on small scale fishing, strengthen local governance, and contribute to sustainable blue economy growth in Asia–EU markets.

## **About the role:**

The Project Lead will have a key role in leading a project team, coordination with partner organizations, implementation and ensuring the overall quality of the “Philippines Advancing Seaweed Solutions for Asia’s Green Economy” or PASSAGE project in the Philippines.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Project Leadership and Management**

- Lead the full project management cycle of the PASSAGE Project, supporting the development of the seaweed value chain across multiple provinces in Mindanao and BARMM (Sulu, Tawi Tawi, and the Zamboanga peninsula), Palawan, and the Visayas (Bohol and Antique).
- Provide overall strategic leadership and oversight throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring the achievement of project objectives and results.
- Ensure project implementation is guided by detailed work plans, realistic timelines, and adaptive management approaches.
- Coordinate and oversee project activities implemented by consortium partners and co-applicants.
- Manage relationships with co-applicant organizations and support effective collaboration throughout project implementation.
- Conduct regular field monitoring visits to assess implementation progress, provide technical guidance, and support project teams and beneficiaries.

**Team Leadership and Capacity Development**

- Lead, supervise, and support the project team to ensure high performance and effective delivery of results.
- Manage staff performance, including objective setting, coaching, performance reviews, and professional development.
- Promote staff learning, capacity building, and continuous improvement across the project team.

**Technical Leadership**

- Provide technical leadership and expertise in rural development, sustainable livelihoods, and agri-aqua value chain development.
- Ensure project interventions are aligned with sector best practices, innovation, and evidence-based approaches.
- Support the continued development of PIN's agriculture and aquaculture and value-chain development programming portfolio in the Philippines.

**Programme Quality, MEAL, Accountability and PIN Standards**

- Ensure project design and implementation comply with People in Need's programme quality standards, donor requirements, and international humanitarian and development standards.
- Promote evidence-based programming and adaptive management to improve project effectiveness and impact.
- In close collaboration with the MEAL Manager, lead monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) processes, including planning, data collection, analysis, learning, and reporting.
- Ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality collection and management of project data.
- Ensure project activities are supported by appropriate MEAL systems, indicators, methodologies, and learning mechanisms.
- Strengthen accountability to affected populations through effective feedback and complaint mechanisms and the use of lessons learned to improve programming.

**Safeguarding, Inclusion and Risk Management**

- Ensure the systematic integration of Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles across all project activities.
- Ensure the effective implementation of Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) measures and safeguarding policies.
- Identify, monitor, and mitigate programmatic, operational, compliance, and partnership risks throughout project implementation.
- Ensure all project activities are implemented in a manner that promotes protection, inclusion, and do-no-harm principles.

**Financial Management and Compliance**

- Oversee project budget management, expenditure tracking, cash flow management, and budget forecasting.
- Ensure efficient and compliant use of project resources in accordance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Guarantee full programmatic and financial compliance with donor regulations and People in Need policies and procedures.
- Ensure all procurement, contracting, financial transactions, and project expenditures comply with organizational and donor requirements.

**Partnerships, Representation and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Serve as the primary focal point for project partners, consortium members, donor representatives, local stakeholders, relevant NGOs, and government authorities.
- Represent the project and People in Need in coordination forums, technical working groups, and other stakeholder engagements.
- Strengthen partnerships and collaboration with government agencies, private sector actors, research institutions, and development partners relevant to the seaweed value chain.

**Donor Relations, Reporting and External Communication**

- Lead the preparation and submission of high-quality donor, government, and internal reports in a timely manner.
- Represent the project to donors and external stakeholders, promoting project visibility and organizational positioning.
- In coordination with the Country Director, oversee external communications related to the project.
- Contribute to donor engagement, networking, visibility, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

**Business Development and Fundraising**

- In coordination with the Country Director and Head of Programmes, identify and pursue fundraising opportunities in the rural development, agriculture, and aquaculture sectors, and value-chain development.
- Contribute to resource mobilization efforts, including the identification of co-funding opportunities for PASSAGE.
- Support proposal development and strategic growth of PIN's agriculture and aquaculture portfolio in the Philippines.
- Perform other duties as assigned by line management.

## **Main requirements:**

Philippine nationals are highly encouraged to apply.

**Technical Skills and Experience**

- At least 7 years of experience working with development organizations and the private/commercial sector;
- Experience in team management, project development, and project management;
- Strong grasp of all stages of programme cycle management, quality standards, and accountability mechanisms;
- University degree in a relevant field (Masters’ degree or equivalent experience);
- Experience in MSD (Market Systems Development) and VC (Value Chain) approaches would be an advantage;
- Preferably previous work-related experience in the Philippines and/or the Southeast Asia region;
- Preferable knowledge and experience in working with the European Union (EU) and managing EU-funded grants and projects;
- Experience leading or coordinating multi-partner consortia would be an advantage;
- Familiarity with the local context would be an advantage;
- Proficient spoken and written English;
- Knowledge of Tagalog or Visayan would be an asset;
- Willingness to travel, including to remote project sites.

**Soft Skills and Personal Competencies**

- Strong organizational, critical analysis, and problem-solving skills;
- Good networking, partnership-building, relationship management, and representation skills;
- Proficient communication and facilitation skills;
- Experience and passion for building the capacity of national teams;
- Strong ability and willingness to transfer knowledge;
- Dynamic and results-oriented, with the ability to organize and plan effectively, and a responsible and systematic approach;
- Reliable and self-reliant personality, with a responsible and systematic approach to work;
- Ability to work in difficult conditions and under pressure;
- Cultural sensitivity;
- Reliable and self-reliant.

## **PIN Offers:**

- Working environment in a well-established middle-sized and continuously growing humanitarian organization in a challenging context; in the largest INGO in Central and Eastern Europe;
- Salary and benefits according to PIN salary scale and HR policies; more detailed conditions will be shared with preselected candidates;
- Free access to e-learning sites, global PIN’s Induction Training, PIN Learning HUB, and individually tailored capacity-building opportunities; incl. HEAT training
- A supportive HQ that provides expertise and guidance on everything from finance and procurement to proposal development and strategic positioning;
- Personal and professional growth as a leader in the highly competitive development sector.

title: Monitoring, Evaluation, + Learning (MEL) Coordinator
body:
**Reports to:** MEL + Data Quality Manager  
**Department:** Compassionate Carbon Tanzania - Monitoring, Evaluation + Learning  
**Position classification:** Full-time  
**Location:** Lumuma, Kilosa District / Mbuga, Mpwapwa District  
**Employment type:** Full-time **(note: visa sponsorship not available for this position)**

**COMPANY INFORMATION**  
Compassionate Carbon Tanzania Ltd is a mission-driven organization launched by Compassionate Carbon LLC and Eden: People+Planet (Eden). Specializing in developing and implementing landscape-scale forest carbon projects through Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+), we collaborate with local communities to restore landscapes, create jobs, protect ecosystems, and mitigate climate change.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Monitoring, Evaluation + Learning (MEL) Coordinator connects field implementation with the information needed to understand progress, learn, and improve. Working across Compassionate Carbon Tanzania’s Forest Protection, Livelihoods, Forst Restoration and Community/Stakeholder Engagement workstreams, the Coordinator strengthens practical monitoring systems, builds the capacity of field teams and community-based data collectors, and ensures that monitoring information is collected consistently and maintained to appropriate quality standards. The role works closely with the MEL + Data Quality Manager and Program Managers to identify trends and gaps, inform program decisions, strengthen implementation, and contribute to reliable reporting and carbon-standard verification.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITES**

- **Data Collection Tools + Systems:** Develop, adapt, and maintain practical monitoring tools, forms, guidelines, and SOPs across Forest Protection, Livelihoods, Forest Restoration, and Community/Stakeholder Engagement functions. Maintain organized, secure, traceable, and audit-ready monitoring records and support effective use of EarthRanger and other data collection systems.
- **Program Data Coordination:** Coordinate monthly and quarterly data collection with Program Managers, field teams, and community-based data collectors. Ensure monitoring data across programs, including surveys and field monitoring activities, are collected completely, consistently, on time, and in alignment with standards.
- **Data Quality Assurance:** Conduct routine QA/QC, including completeness and validation checks, spot checks, and field verification to ensure that data meets Equitable Earth standards. Identify and resolve data gaps or inconsistencies with Program Managers and data collectors and ensure established data standards and procedures are consistently followed.
- **Data Analysis + Reporting:** Clean, compile, summarize, and conduct routine analysis of monitoring data to identify progress, trends, gaps, and data-quality concerns. Prepare clear monitoring summaries and contribute verified data and documentation to project reporting, learning reviews, and carbon-standard verification.
- **Training + Capacity Building:** Develop practical training materials appropriate to field and community contexts. Train and coach field staff, enumerators, community-based data collectors, and other relevant stakeholders on monitoring procedures, tools, data-quality expectations, and ethical data collection. Revise training materials as needed to address training gaps or quality issues.
- **Collaboration + Stakeholder Coordination:** Work closely with the MRV + Data Quality Manager, Program Managers, field teams, communities, and relevant government stakeholders to integrate monitoring into field activities, coordinate data collection, address monitoring gaps, and communicate relevant findings.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- A Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, or a related field
- At least 3 years of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation, field data collection, or data management.
- Prior experience working in natural resources, conservation, forestry, agriculture, or other rural development projects is preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with field-based monitoring and data collection, including coordinating or supervising enumerators, data clerks, community-based data collectors, or field teams.
- Experience training and supporting community members and field teams in data collection methods, tools, and data-quality requirements.
- Hands-on experience developing and using digital data collection tools, such as KoBoToolbox, ODK, Survey123, or similar platforms.
- Experience with data management and quality assurance, including data cleaning, validation, routine analysis, and preparation of monitoring summaries or reports.
- Additional professional training or certification in Monitoring + Evaluation is an advantage.
- Familiarity with EarthRanger, SMART, GIS tools such as QGIS, forest carbon projects, or carbon standards such as Equitable Earth or Verra is an advantage but not required..

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Monitoring + Evaluation:** Good understanding of monitoring and evaluation concepts, including indicators, baselines, data quality, results tracking, data collection methodologies, and learning from monitoring information.
- **Data Management + Analysis:** Strong analytical and data-management skills, including the ability to clean, organize, summarize, interpret, and present monitoring data and identify trends, gaps, and data-quality issues.
- **Data Collection Systems:** Ability to develop practical, user-friendly data collection tools and explain their use clearly to people with different levels of technical experience or formal education.
- **Quality Assurance:** Strong attention to detail and ability to apply defined QA/QC procedures consistently, identify errors and inconsistencies, and work constructively with teams to resolve data-quality issues.
- **Training + Facilitation:** Strong training and facilitation skills, with patience, humility, and respect when working with rural communities and community-based data collectors.
- **Communication + Writing:** Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare monitoring summaries, guidelines, SOPs, training materials, and supporting documentation for internal and external reporting.
- **Organization + Coordination:** Strong organizational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage monitoring activities across several programs, field teams, and locations while meeting competing deadlines.
- **Collaboration:** Ability to work independently in field settings while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams, community stakeholders, and government counterparts.
- **Technology:** Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Excel for organizing, checking, summarizing, and analyzing monitoring data, and comfort using smartphones, tablets, GPS devices, and digital data collection systems.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** Combination of office and field settings, including regular visits to forested and rural project sites under varied weather and terrain conditions. Frequent interaction with local communities and multi-stakeholder teams may involve basic field accommodations and extended time in remote areas.
- **Work Schedule:** Full-time, with standard office hours, requiring occasional flexibility (e.g. early mornings, evenings, or weekends).
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for fieldwork in rustic environments, including walking long distances on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods, Must be comfortable in challenging field conditions. Work also involves typical office tasks (computer use, meetings) when not in the field.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic travel within Tanzania to remote project sites for monitoring and community consultation, sometimes involving difficult travel conditions and overnight stays.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

**Disclaimer:** This document outlines primary duties but may not cover all responsibilities or conditions. Compassionate Carbon may assign extra tasks or modify roles for business needs or employee accommodation, per applicable law.

Compassionate Carbon is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team representing a variety of backgrounds, viewpoints, and skills. Candidate selection is based on technical qualifications and position requirements; employment will not commence until applicable background and reference checks are completed.

**Safeguarding:** Compassionate Carbon holds strict safeguarding principles and does not tolerate behaviors that harm others, including sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, and other injustices. Employees are expected to abide by company policies.

**Compensation:** Compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. Compassionate Carbon provides a competitive benefits package including annual leave, health insurance, and contributions to statutory funds.

title: Field Extension Officer
body:
**Reports to**: Programme Coordinator, Sustainable Livelihoods  
*Technical guidance from: Sustainable Livelihoods Manager*  
**Department**: Compassionate Carbon Tanzania, Sustainable Livelihoods  
**Position Classification**: Full-time  
**Location:** Assigned program village or project area within the Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project  
**Employment type:** Full-time **(note: visa sponsorship not available for this position)**

**COMPANY INFORMATION**

Compassionate Carbon Tanzania Ltd is a mission-driven organization launched by Compassionate Carbon LLC and Eden: People+Planet (Eden). Specializing in developing and implementing landscape-scale forest carbon projects through Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+), we collaborate with local communities to restore landscapes, create jobs, protect ecosystems, and mitigate climate change.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Field Extension Officer brings Compassionate Carbon Tanzania’s sustainable livelihood activities directly to farmers and communities, translating approved technical approaches into practical, farm-level support. Reporting to the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator, the Officer provides farmer training, demonstrations, regular farm visits, and follow-up to support adoption of Climate-Smart Agriculture practices, with an initial focus on Conservation Agriculture. As a frontline representative of the program, the Officer works closely with farmers, Lead Farmers, community stakeholders, and government extension personnel while monitoring field progress, maintaining accurate records, and communicating implementation challenges and feedback.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Farmer Extension + Technical Support:** Deliver practical training and farm-level support on approved Climate-Smart Agriculture and Conservation Agriculture practices, including minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover, crop diversification and rotation, soil fertility management, and soil and water conservation. Conduct regular farm visits, support farmers and Lead Farmers throughout the production cycle, and assist with approved Agroforestry, Quality Declared Seed, seed security, and other livelihood activities as introduced.
- **Farmer Training + Demonstration:** Mobilize participating farmers and support Farmer Groups and program learning structures. Facilitate Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, practical training sessions, farmer exchanges, field days, and other community learning activities. Work with Lead Farmers to strengthen farmer-to-farmer learning and translate approved technical recommendations into clear, practical guidance.
- **Field Monitoring + Documentation:** Monitor farmer participation, training attendance, adoption of promoted practices, crop performance, implementation challenges, and other agreed indicators. Collect and verify accurate field information using approved paper-based or digital tools; maintain complete records; and submit timely field updates and reports to the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator.
- **Community + Stakeholder Engagement:** Maintain regular field-level communication with farmers, Lead Farmers, Farmer Groups, village governments, community leaders, and government agricultural extension personnel. Coordinate local field activities, promote meaningful participation, document community feedback, and promptly report technical, operational, environmental, safeguarding, or community-level concerns through established channels.
- **Field Planning + Program Support:** Prepare and implement weekly and monthly field activity plans in coordination with the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator. Participate in required technical training and support program assessments, monitoring exercises, learning events, evaluations, and partner or donor field visits.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Diploma or bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Agricultural Extension, Rural Development, or a closely related field.
- Practical experience in agricultural extension, farmer training, community mobilization, crop production, or smallholder livelihood programs.
- Good understanding of smallholder farming systems and common production constraints.
- Working knowledge of Climate-Smart Agriculture and Conservation Agriculture principles.
- Experience facilitating practical and participatory farmer training through Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, Farmer Groups, farm-level coaching, or similar approaches.
- Experience collecting accurate field information, maintaining organized records, and preparing clear activity reports.
- Previous experience implementing Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, Quality Declared Seed, seed production, community seed systems, or seed-quality activities is an advantage.
- Experience using KoboCollect, ODK, or similar digital data-collection platforms is an advantage.
- Ability to ride a motorcycle and possession of an appropriate valid driving license is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Agricultural Extension:** Able to explain and demonstrate approved agricultural practices clearly and practically to farmers and provide reliable follow-up in the field.
- **Farmer Training + Facilitation:** Strong participatory training, facilitation, and community-mobilization skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers and community-based groups.
- **Field Monitoring + Documentation:** Strong attention to detail and the ability to collect accurate information, maintain organized records, document observations and feedback, and submit timely reports.
- **Communication + Collaboration:** Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with farmers, Lead Farmers, community leaders, government extension personnel, and project colleagues.
- **Technology:** Comfortable using smartphones or tablets for routine program work and digital data collection.
- **Language:** Able to communicate effectively in Kiswahili; knowledge of languages commonly used within the project area is an advantage.
- **Field Readiness:** Able to work independently within approved plans, travel regularly, and spend substantial time in rural communities and farmers’ fields.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** The position is primarily field-based, with regular work in rural communities, farms, Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, and other project sites. Work may involve basic facilities and exposure to heat, rain, dust, and varied terrain.
- **Work schedule:** Full-time, with standard working hours and occasional flexibility for early mornings, evenings, or weekends based on farmer availability, training schedules, agricultural cycles, and field activities.
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for frequent fieldwork, including walking on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods during training and demonstrations, and carrying routine training or field materials. Administrative duties include record keeping, digital data entry, and preparation of reports.
- **Travel:** Frequent local travel within assigned program villages and project areas is required and may involve difficult road conditions. Occasional overnight travel may be required for program activities or training.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

title: Programme Coordinator, Sustainable Livelihoods
body:
**Reports to**: Sustainable Livelihoods Manager  
**Department**: Compassionate Carbon Tanzania - Sustainable Livelihoods  
**Position classification**: Full-time  
**Location**: Lumuma, Kilosa District / Mbuga, Mpwapwa District (Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project Area)  
**Employment type:** Full-time **(note: visa sponsorship not available for this position)**

**COMPANY INFORMATION**

Compassionate Carbon Tanzania Ltd is a mission-driven organization launched by Compassionate Carbon LLC and Eden: People+Planet (Eden). Specializing in developing and implementing landscape-scale forest carbon projects through Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+), we collaborate with local communities to restore landscapes, create jobs, protect ecosystems, and mitigate climate change.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Sustainable Livelihood Programme Coordinator is the key operational link between program plans and effective delivery in the field, ensuring that livelihood activities translate into well-coordinated, high-quality support for participating farmers and communities. Reporting to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, the Coordinator oversees day-to-day field implementation, supervises Field Extension Officers, and coordinates farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, and follow-up across project communities. The role monitors progress and implementation quality, identifies and helps resolve field-level challenges, and brings forward practical insights and recommendations to strengthen delivery. Working closely with field teams, communities, government extension personnel, and other local stakeholders, the Coordinator helps ensure approved livelihood approaches are implemented consistently, responsively, and in line with program targets, technical guidance, and available resources.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Program Implementation + Coordination**: Translate approved workplans into weekly and monthly field schedules and coordinate farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, farm follow-up, and other livelihood activities. Track delivery against targets, timelines, technical guidance, and approved budgets; coordinate field logistics and support agreed program adaptations.
- **Field Team Supervision**: Provide day-to-day supervision and coordination of Field Extension Officers, review field plans, conduct regular supervision visits, and provide practical support in resolving implementation challenges. Ensure field staff maintain accurate records and submit complete reports on time, escalating significant capacity, performance, technical, or operational concerns to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager.
- **Implementation Monitoring + Reporting:** Track implementation progress, verify field records, consolidate weekly and monthly reports, and provide timely updates to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager. Identify delays, emerging risks, operational constraints, and areas requiring corrective action. Support assessments, evaluations, learning activities, and partner or donor field visits.  
    **Stakeholder + Community Coordination:** Coordinate field-level engagement with village governments, government agricultural extension personnel, Lead Farmers, service providers, participating communities, and other relevant stakeholders in support of program implementation. Maintain effective communication among program management, field teams, and communities and ensure concerns, feedback, and implementation issues are documented and escalated appropriately.
- **Program Quality + Continuous Improvement:** Ensure field activities follow approved program approaches and technical guidance, including Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, and participatory farmer training. Use field observations, monitoring information, and stakeholder feedback to identify implementation issues and recommend practical improvements to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, supporting agreed corrective actions and program adaptations.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Rural Development, Agricultural Extension, Project Management, or another relevant field.
- Relevant experience coordinating agricultural, livelihood, rural development, or smallholder farmer programs, including translating workplans into field implementation.
- Demonstrated experience supervising or coordinating field-based teams and supporting staff to plan, deliver, document, and report on activities.
- Practical knowledge of Climate-Smart Agriculture, particularly Conservation Agriculture and Agroforestry, and an understanding of smallholder farming systems, agricultural extension approaches, farmer organization, and participatory farmer training.
- Experience coordinating activities with rural communities, local government, agricultural extension personnel, service providers, or similar stakeholders.
- Experience tracking implementation progress, coordinating multiple field activities, and preparing clear, timely reports.
- Familiarity with Quality Declared Seed, community seed systems, seed security interventions, or digital field-data systems such as KoboCollect or ODK is an advantage.
- Experience coordinating programs across multiple villages or geographically dispersed communities is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Program Coordination:** Strong ability to organize field implementation, coordinate multiple activities, manage competing priorities, and maintain progress against workplans, targets, and timelines.
- **Team Supervision:** Able to provide clear direction, practical coaching, and effective day-to-day supervision to field-based staff.
- **Technical Knowledge:** Good understanding of smallholder agriculture, Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, agricultural extension, and participatory farmer training, with the ability to support consistent field implementation of approved approaches.
- **Monitoring + Reporting:** Able to track implementation, verify field records, identify delivery gaps or risks, and prepare clear and accurate program updates and reports.
- **Stakeholder Engagement:** Strong facilitation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers, communities, government representatives, service providers, and project colleagues.
- **Problem Solving + Adaptability:** Practical and solution-oriented, with the ability to respond constructively to field constraints and support appropriate program adaptations.
- **Communication:** Strong spoken and written Kiswahili and working proficiency in English.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** Combination of office and field settings, including regular visits to forested and rural project sites under varied weather and terrain conditions. Frequent interaction with local communities and multi-stakeholder teams may involve basic field accommodations and extended time in remote areas.
- **Work schedule:** Full-time, with standard office hours, requiring occasional flexibility (e.g. early mornings, evenings, or weekends) to accommodate field requirements.
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for fieldwork in rustic environments, including walking long distances on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods, Must be comfortable in challenging field conditions. Work also involves typical office tasks (computer use, meetings) when not in the field.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic travel within Tanzania to remote project sites for monitoring and community consultation, sometimes involving difficult travel conditions and overnight stays.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

title: Short Term Adviser: Performance Stories (Bougainville)
body:
**About TSSP Phase 3**

The Australia Transport Sector Support Program Phase 3 (TSSP3) is a flagship partnership between the Governments of Papua New Guinea and Australia that strengthens the transport sector to improve connectivity, safety and accessibility, supporting economic growth, service delivery and sustainable community development. Working with government agencies, industry and communities, its multidisciplinary teams support reforms and investments in transport planning, infrastructure, governance, safety and inclusion to build stronger institutions and a more resilient, better-connected transport network. TSSP3 offers a collaborative and inclusive workplace where skilled professionals contribute innovative thinking, grow professionally and help deliver lasting outcomes for communities across Papua New Guinea.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

  
**The Role**

The Short-Term Adviser: Performance Stories (Bougainville) will lead the development of a compelling evidence-based performance story that demonstrates how TSSP3, in partnership with the Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) and the Government of Papua New Guinea (GoPNG), has contributed to building a sustainable road maintenance ecosystem in Bougainville. The assignment will focus on documenting the broader systems change achieved through long-term investment in local institutions, contractors, governance arrangements and communities, rather than solely reporting on infrastructure outputs.

Working closely with the MERLA, Roads, Communications and Operations teams, you will design and implement an evaluation approach that captures evidence of institutional strengthening, local contractor development, government and private sector collaboration and community benefits resulting from improved transport access. You will undertake desktop reviews, key informant interviews, community consultations and field visits, analyse findings and develop practical, credible and decision useful products that contribute to TSSP3 performance reporting and organisational learning.

This role offers an opportunity to work with a nationally significant transport program, engaging with government agencies, development partners, community stakeholders and the private sector to highlight the lasting impact of transport sector investments in Bougainville.

Click on the link or copy and paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[https://l1nq.com/x4ocz7s](https://l1nq.com/x4ocz7s)

**About You**

You are an experienced evaluation professional who turns complex evidence into clear, credible findings. You bring sound judgement, cross-cultural collaboration and consensus-building skills, a commitment to locally led, inclusive and resilient development, and the ability to mentor others and adapt to resource-constrained environments.

- Relevant tertiary qualification and experience delivering complex development evaluations, performance studies or contribution-focused case studies.
- Strong MERLA/MEAL knowledge and experience evaluating institutional, policy, governance and systems change, capability and sustainability.
- Ability to translate Terms of Reference into practical evaluation plans, sampling strategies, stakeholder maps and research tools.
- Advanced qualitative research and consultation skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office and qualitative/data analysis tools.
- Government and senior stakeholder experience in PNG or comparable Pacific contexts, with strong cross-cultural communication and excellent English.
- Knowledge of locally led development and ability to embed GEDSI, disability inclusion, safeguarding/PSEAH, climate change and disaster resilience throughout evaluations.
- Familiarity with Australian Government/DFAT development program performance and reporting standards is highly desirable.

**Why Join TSSP3**

Be part of a program helping build a safer, better-connected transport system for Papua New Guinea.

At TSSP3, we work alongside local partners and communities to strengthen transport systems, build lasting capability and connect people with opportunities. Join a committed team of Papua New Guinean and international professionals, where your contribution matters and collaboration, innovation and care for people underpin our work.

title: Intensive Case Management Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Intensive Case Management (ICM) Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. The ICM caseworker will be expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for ICM programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized, SMART Self-sufficiency plans for each client enrolled in the ICM program.
- Evaluate client progress every six months during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Assist clients in navigating healthcare and social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. The ICM caseworker may also be expected to maintain a strong relationship with local and state level refugee coordinators and health coordinators to ensure client needs are met.
- Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as women’s health, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems at the local level.
- Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed.
- Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.
- Maintain up-to-date documentation in client’s case file to ensure services are properly documented throughout the client’s service period; document all services provided in IRC’s database, Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Attend relevant trainings and meetings at the local and national level.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work, public health, or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum of 1-2 years of case management experience with similar populations and/or client needs required.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English required, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group preferred, including Dari/Pashto.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23 - $25.90/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

title: Emergency Response Team Supply Chain Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster.
